title: 100 Million Bugs Later: A Field Report From the Agentic Era (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
description: CodeRabbit reviews code generated by major coding agents: 30M+ pull requests and 200K+ independent code reviews each day across open source and enterprises. As agentic development accelerated, PR volume grew 4x while review rounds per PR fell 20%. AI-co-authored PRs carry about 1.7x more issues and up to 2.74x more security issues than human-written code. David Loker, CodeRabbit VP of Applied AI, shares 12 months of review telemetry behind 100M caught bugs—and the enterprise pattern it reveals: heterogeneous coding-agent stacks are the end state. He introduces Agentic Change Management: an independent, agent-agnostic quality gate that assesses every change, surfaces what needs human attention, and explains what it approves. Leave with a vendor-neutral framework for scaling an agentic SDLC without sacrificing quality, security, or control. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.

title: 10x or bust: How Amazon's Frontier teams ship with Kiro
description: Amazon teams using Kiro and AI-native workflows are shipping features in hours that used to take weeks. But the gains didn't come from better prompts. They came from better practices, from rethinking how developers and teams work instead of just adding shiny tools on top of existing SDLC processes. This session dissects three real experiments: a pathfinder initiative, a structured sprint, and in-situ pilots across 50+ teams. You'll learn the five practices that compound into 4.5x–10x gains, the mistakes that kill momentum, and how to run your own pilot starting Monday.

title: 1 Customer, 1 Context, From all the Channels: (sponsored by Redis)
description: Join Toshish Jawale, Head of AI Engineering at Invoca, to learn how his team is putting context at the center of the business’ customer journeys. Hear how Invoca and Redis are delivering real-time, mutli-source context for Invoca’s agents, how they’re helping customers interact with their brand in exciting ways, and how they’re delivering complete pictures of user brand experiences. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.

title: 3 a.m. and Already Fixed: How PagerDuty’s SRE Agent Is Rewriting Incident Response (sponsored by PagerDuty)
description: Every SRE knows the pattern: an alert fires, and the next 20 minutes disappear into triage before you've even confirmed what's broken. Context is scattered across dashboards, runbooks, and tribal knowledge, and much of incident response is just reconstructing what already happened. This session explores how autonomous operations changes that story. PagerDuty’s SRE Agent investigates before a human is even involved and proposes fixes you simply approve. See it firsthand through PD Labs, a hands-on site for trying autonomous workflows, and SRE Workbench, launching in early access, where humans, agents, and automation meet in order to investigate, diagnose, and remediate issues. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.

title: 3-step blueprint for scaling AI with a modern enterprise core (sponsored by IBM)
description: AI is a catalyst for growth and innovation, yet only 17% of AI initiatives reach full-scale production. Join IBM and AI trailblazers to explore the three-step blueprint for scaling AI on AWS: modernizing the enterprise core across applications, data and infrastructure; fostering a culture that moves innovation forward; and putting digital labor to work in real workflows. Discover how IBM Consulting helps organizations move beyond isolated use cases, accelerate ideas into production and make AI work inside the enterprise, not around it. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: 4 foundations for building the agentic enterprises on AWS (sponsored by IBM)
description: Agentic AI is moving fast—but isolated agents and one-off experiments won’t transform the enterprise. To create value at scale, companies need a foundation that helps them build and modernize applications faster, orchestration across systems and workflows, governed execution, and control over the infrastructure, performance and cost behind them. Join IBM and industry leaders to discover what’s new from IBM on AWS. Hear real-world lessons and measurable business outcomes while exploring the four foundations organizations need to move from disconnected agents to secure, governed, enterprise-wide execution. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: 4 primitives to evaluate your on-call agent's autonomy (sponsored by Resolve AI)
description: AI that handles on-call autonomously requires agents to take on alert triage, investigations, acting on production, and learning from what happened. Autonomy progresses unevenly as investigations are bottlenecked on quality while actions are limited by trust. In this session we will walk through how we build each primitive of our autonomous agents at Resolve AI, and how we help engineering teams handle on-call and incident resolutions. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

title: 5 steps to faster data center exits with AWS Transform
description: 70% of applications still sit on-premises, and the longer they stay, the more tech debt compounds. AWS Transform uses agentic AI to compress the entire data center exit journey from assessment through execution. Start with AI-powered discovery that right-sizes thousands of servers, compares cost scenarios, and builds a business case that gets executive buy-in in days. Move into automated wave planning and landing zone deployment. Then see how network architectures convert into production-ready VPCs and workloads rehost to Amazon EC2 at scale. We follow one customer's real timeline from plan to exit and unpack what made it work.

title: Accelerate AI workloads with GPUs on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
description: Running GPU workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, right-sizing instances, and scaling without over-provisioning. Amazon ECS Managed Instances handles infrastructure lifecycle while giving you access to the latest GPUs and accelerators. In this session, explore how to launch GPU capacity with managed provisioning, scale based on real GPU metrics rather than CPU proxies, and automatically recover from hardware failures. Hear how a customer built and scaled their production AI infrastructure on Amazon ECS Managed Instances to serve GPU-backed workloads while optimizing cost and operational agility.

title: Accelerate Apache Spark data processing with GPUs at lower cost
description: Data-intensive workloads like feature engineering, large-scale ETL, and real-time analytics push CPU-based clusters to their limits. In this session, learn how Amazon EMR with NVIDIA RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark runs Spark workloads up to 3.7x faster on Amazon EC2 G7 instances—with no code changes. We share benchmarking results, walk through architecture and tuning patterns, and show how finishing jobs faster lowers the cost per run, even at a higher hourly rate.

title: Accelerate declarative resource management with Amazon EKS Capabilities
description: Platform teams struggle to deliver self-service infrastructure that is both fast and governed. Developers want Kubernetes-native provisioning, but adopting new tools while managing existing IaC investments creates friction. In this builders session, explore the latest Amazon EKS Capabilities features including kro Collections, Graph Revisions, and reactive watches for advanced declarative resource management. Then use Kiro to build an agentic workflow that accelerates migration from legacy IaC to Kubernetes-native resource definitions. Leave with working implementations you can bring back to your platform.

title: Accelerate legacy Java modernization with custom AI-powered transformations
description: Legacy applications on outdated frameworks and deprecated runtimes represent a growing modernization challenge. In this workshop, use AWS Transform custom to build and execute transformations that accelerate Java modernization at scale. You'll define transformation rules using natural language and code examples, execute multi-step upgrades (Java 8 to 21, Spring Boot 2 to 3, Jakarta EE), refine quality through the agentic AI feedback loop, validate with built-in testing, and run campaigns across multiple repositories. You'll leave with reusable transformation definitions you can apply to your own Java codebases. Laptop required.

title: Accelerate Physical AI development with NVIDIA on AWS
description: Physical AI is reshaping manufacturing, robotics, and autonomous systems, but realizing that potential requires robust infrastructure and purpose-built tools. AWS and NVIDIA have partnered to simplify the entire Physical AI development lifecycle: from synthetic data generation and model training through sim-to-real validation and hardware-in-loop testing. In this session, discover how the Physical AI Toolchain from AWS provides access to AWS managed infrastructure and NVIDIA’s foundation models and training applications to accelerate every stage of development, reduce time-to-market, and optimize resource utilization across your pipeline.

title: Accelerate service onboarding with composable AI plugins
description: Service onboarding workflows consume hours across security, risk, and governance teams through manual approvals, evidence gathering, and threat modeling. These tasks are auditable, repetitive, and ripe for agentic decomposition. In this chalk talk, we walk through a composable AI plugin pattern that decomposes service onboarding into lightweight modules any agentic client can consume. We discuss how each plugin integrates with any agentic client to execute governance checks end-to-end. We share architecture patterns, working code examples, and show you how to reduce security review time. You’ll leave with a decomposition pattern and an open-source repo to get started.

title: Accelerate your agentic AI mission from prototype to ATO in weeks
description: Agencies, the industrial base, and technology partners want agentic AI in production, but few have navigated the path across classification levels. In this chalk talk, learn real-world patterns for taking Bedrock agents and foundation models from prototype to authorized production across commercial and AWS Government Regions (FedRAMP, DoD CSP SRG IL2/4/5, classified) on one portable security baseline, without a rebuild; what is authorized at each level; the tradeoffs at each level; and ATO strategies that turn guardrails, observability, and evaluations into control evidence your assessor can use. Guardrails and audit-trail demos. Ideal for architects and security leads.

title: Accelerate your GenAI mission from prototype to ATO in weeks
description: Every agency wants GenAI in production, but few have navigated the path across classification levels. In this Chalk Talk, learn real-world patterns for deploying Bedrock agents and foundation models across Government Regions - service parity, ATO strategies, and tradeoffs. Ideal for architects.

title: Accelerating AI inference with Amazon EBS
description: As organizations optimize AI workflows to keep GPUs highly utilized, Amazon EBS plays a distinct role in the AI pipeline where key business data is close to compute. In this session, learn how EBS minimizes pre-staging time for model weights with low latency, accelerates data preparation and checkpoints on high-performance EBS volumes, and reduces response times by serving vector embeddings at sub-millisecond latencies during inferencing, all while delivering elasticity and configurability in storage and performance. Leave with architecture patterns, volume configurations, and a framework for extending your storage architecture with EBS for AI/ML workloads.

title: Accelerating AI-powered business transformation and SAP Modernization
description: The legacy ERP systems that once drove competitive advantage now creates technical debt and blocks innovation and yet modernizing it remains complex, costly, and risky. In this panel, discover how AWS AI services are changing the economics of SAP modernization, making it possible to transform business processes by through AI-powered automations, while delivering breakthrough performance, cost savings and innovation.

title: Accelerating Auto Manufacturing with NVIDIA Omniverse: VW's GS7 Battery Digital Twin (sponsored by NVIDIA)
description: Deloitte helped Volkswagen Group Components design and deploy a cloud-native, AI-ready digital twin on AWS, powered by NVIDIA Omniverse and the OpenUSD standard, for the GS7 battery production environment. By consolidating fragmented factory data — CAD models, robot programs, camera configurations, and defect imagery — into a photorealistic, simulation-ready scene on AWS, the team enabled virtual commissioning, synthetic inspection data generation, and earlier production validation. The result is a reusable, scalable platform built on AWS infrastructure and NVIDIA's industrial metaverse stack that reduces physical trial effort, accelerates line ramp-up, and creates a foundation for AI-driven quality inspection at scale. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Accelerating AWS Graviton migrations at scale with AI
description: In this session, we explore how agents accelerate AWS Graviton migrations, improving price/performance for workloads across every phase from migration planning, compatibility validation, to performance testing and optimization. We’ll examine various agentic tools where attendees will learn how to choose the right solution and practical steps to implement the tools in their environments. Participants will leave with actionable strategies to reduce manual overhead and harness AI to unlock Graviton’s benefits at scale.

title: Accelerating Fusion Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS HPC, Analytics, and Agentic AI (sponsored by AMD)
description: Learn how Pacific Fusion is leveraging AMD EPYC-powered AWS infrastructure to build a scalable platform for high-performance computing, advanced analytics, and agentic AI. By unifying simulation, data processing, and AI-driven research workflows, Pacific Fusion can accelerate scientific discovery while optimizing cost and resource utilization. Discover how AWS elasticity and AMD EPYC performance enable researchers to rapidly scale from compute-intensive simulations to data-rich analytics and intelligent automation, helping transform scientific data into actionable insights and accelerating the path toward commercially viable fusion energy. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

title: A day in the life of a Serverless builder
description: In this code talk, follow a Serverless application from first line of code to production deployment, all live. Start with an AI coding agent generating infrastructure and function scaffolding, iterate locally with hot reload, deploy in one command, then debug a failing request by tracing it across Lambda, EventBridge, and DynamoDB using native OpenTelemetry. Along the way, see how recent Serverless launches change the workflow: faster deploys, built-in observability, and simplified local testing. No slides, no diagrams. Just a terminal, an editor, and the workflow a Serverless developer uses in 2026.

title: A day in the life of a SPIFFE SVID
description: Workloads across AWS, on premises, and other clouds need verifiable identity without long-lived secrets, and SPIFFE provides it. In this lightning talk, we show how to issue SPIFFE SVIDs and how they flow into AWS. You follow one SVID through SPIRE attestation, cross-cloud federation, exchange for STS credentials through IAM Roles Anywhere or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and presentation to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity for AI agent tool access.

title: A Day Without Handoffs: Telecom Operations With Amazon Quick
description: See how telecom employees use Amazon Quick to handle billing disputes, automatically address network issues, and manage service requests from a single workspace. Pulled from real-world use cases at telecom companies around the world, these demos pull context from OSS/BSS, run complex workflows, and close the loop without handing off to another team!

title: Adding agentic AI to your legacy app without a rewrite
description: Full legacy application rewrites take years. Agentic AI lets you deliver value now. In this code talk, we build an AI agent that wraps an existing legacy application without changing the core system. You'll see how the agent understands user intent, calls existing application functions, and helps users complete business tasks through a modern conversational experience. Ask questions as we go from legacy to AI-assisted workflow in real time. You'll leave ready to put agentic AI in front of your legacy application today.

title: Aflac’s Modernization journey to a resilient and innovative future (sponsored by Kyndryl)
description: Modernizing critical systems is never just about technology. In this executive panel, leaders from Aflac, Kyndryl, and AWS share the real-world experience behind Aflac’s transformation journey, from overcoming operational challenges and reducing downtime risk to enabling future innovation & continuous modernization. Learn how a strong customer-partner relationship helped balance transformation with business continuity, security, and regulatory requirements. Gain insights into managing large-scale transformation, avoiding common pitfalls, and building a roadmap that delivers measurable business value while preparing for the next generation of cloud and AI-driven innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Kyndryl, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic advertising with privacy-enhanced data collaboration
description: Programmatic advertising is shifting from rule-based heuristics to autonomous agents that plan, orchestrate, and bid inside the millisecond bidstream. This Lightning Talk shows three AWS building blocks combining into one agentic ad tech stack: multi-agent collaboration on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for media planning and inventory optimization; ARTF-compliant containers running deep-learning models on NVIDIA Triton and Amazon EKS for real-time bid shading, audience activation, and deal management; and AWS Clean Rooms ML as the trust layer, training lookalike models on collective data without exposing underlying records. Leave with a reference architecture for where inference, orchestration, and privacy all work together.

title: Agentic AI Control Plane on AWS: govern agents at enterprise scale (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
description: Enterprises are moving from a handful of agents to hundreds. Without a shared layer for identity, policy, orchestration, and observability, that growth stalls. In this 20-minute launch session, we introduce the Agentic AI Control Plane on AWS: a governed foundation for building, deploying, and running agents across business and IT workflows. See how it handles agent onboarding, guardrails, cost and performance visibility, and human oversight, with a live look at the platform. Built for CIOs, data and AI leaders, and platform and risk teams who need agent fleets to scale safely, with the controls their auditors expect. This presentation is brought to you by Tata Consultancy Services, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI for manufacturing: Build a cross-domain digital thread
description: Manufacturing data lives in silos — from engineering systems through production lines. In this workshop, build an agentic digital thread: a knowledge-graph-powered AI system that unifies OT and IT data across the product lifecycle and answers cross-domain questions in real time. Using Amazon Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS IoT SiteWise, deploy agents that autonomously traverse connections from product design through production operations — linking engineering changes to equipment assets to quality events — without point-to-point integrations. Leave with a deployable reference architecture adaptable to any manufacturing environment.

description: A federal agency achieved 3x faster document analysis using Agentic AI with autonomous reasoning. This chalk talk explores how AI agents orchestrate mission-critical tasks in high-side environments while meeting IL4/IL5 compliance and zero-trust requirements.

title: Agentic AI for Security: How AWS CIRT reduced triage time to minutes
description: When a security event hits a customer account, every minute counts. Learn how AWS CIRT built an agentic AI system using Amazon Kiro that performs investigation workflows autonomously: ingesting case data, baselining environments, analyzing indicators, and producing triage assessments. We cover architecture decisions for AI agents with live AWS API access, evaluation frameworks measuring accuracy against expert answer keys, and guardrails keeping humans in the loop. Leave with patterns for applying agentic AI to operational workflows where accuracy is non-negotiable.

title: Agentic AI for software-defined vehicles: Compress the V-Cycle with Kiro
description: Automotive embedded software teams face complex V-Cycle workflows, safety standards, and competitive pressure to ship faster. In this workshop, experience how agentic AI transforms the embedded software V-Cycle — compressing timelines from weeks to hours without sacrificing quality or traceability. Attendees build a remote start/stop feature for an autonomous mower platform, using Kiro to orchestrate agents across requirements engineering, code generation, virtual-target testing, and test automation.

description: As agentic AI expands into regulated industries, autonomous decisions must meet compliance before production. This session gives partners a governance framework spanning technical and non-technical requirements — not just architecture. We demo a working multi-agent system and share the code.

title: Agentic AI governance tabletop experience
description: Navigate AI-driven security threats as they escalate in real time. In this immersive executive tabletop, participants allocate a constrained governance budget, then respond to live crisis events scored across six dimensions. Practice navigating high-stakes scenarios including autonomous AI deployment failures, third-party security incidents, and emerging regulatory obligations. Confront real attack techniques, compliance frameworks, and enterprise liability exposure while aligning cross-functional teams under pressure. This experience sharpens governance instincts and crisis fluency—equipping leaders to govern Agentic AI risks, enforce accountability, and make decisive resource allocation calls before a real crisis demands it.

title: Agentic AI in Production: Natera Saves Lives, Cuts Costs, Grows Revenue
description: Natera, a global leader in cell-free DNA testing for oncology, women's health, and organ health, built reusable agentic infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to power multiple internal platforms from a single framework. Natera's VP of Engineering will share the technical decisions behind this infrastructure and provides a blueprint for building once and scaling across your organization. See a live demo of one platform built on this foundation for revenue cycle management, cutting prior-authorization denial rates 6x, reducing touchpoints by 5x, and enabling new use cases to go live in less than a week.

title: Agentic AI Jam - sponsored by Nvidia
description: Come with your team of four or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Are you ready to build and deploy agentic AI solutions on AWS? We provide hands-on environments where you can architect intelligent and production-ready agents. How do you orchestrate multi-step agent reasoning with tool use? How can you design agents that plan, act, and self-correct autonomously? Whether you are new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this Jam is your chance to demonstrate your skills and learn new ones. Structured for all experience levels, our sessions include guided exercises, helpful clues, and support from AWS experts to accelerate your agentic AI expertise. Team up, compete with others, climb the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. With expert guidance every step of the way, all you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.

title: Agentic AI Jam - sponsored by Nvidia
description: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Solve real-world Gen AI and Agentic AI scenarios using Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker AI & Kiro - including a sponsored challenge from NVIDIA to build and optimize GenAI workloads using NVIDIA's accelerated computing and AI inference stack on AWS. Challenges suit all skill levels, with AWS experts and helpful clues throughout. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Agentic AI Meets ‘Human-Guided-Autonomy’ (sponsored by Terra)
description: AI is accelerating how fast code ships and how fast attackers find exploitable weaknesses, and annual pentests cannot keep pace. This session looks at what it takes to make security validation genuinely continuous rather than just more frequent, tracking what changed instead of retesting everything from scratch. Self-driving cars, robotic surgery, and other sensitive actions all became viable the same way: not by removing the human, but by defining exactly which actions the machine takes on its own and which ones need a hand on the controls. This talk will cover the delegate balance between autonomy, safety and control in Offensive Security. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI Meets the Line-of-Business Buyer
description: Budget authority is migrating from CIOs to line-of-business leaders - CFOs, Chief Medical Officers, Heads of Manufacturing - who buy outcomes, not infrastructure. At the same time, agentic AI is making it possible to automate entire business processes end-to-end, not just assist them. The partners who win are the ones who can connect these two shifts: framing autonomous agents as measurable business outcomes (revenue acceleration, cost compression, speed-to-market) in the language LOB leaders understand.

title: Agentic commerce in production: multi-agent orchestration on AgentCore
description: A single agent that both advises and sells gets fragile fast. This session shows a production multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents, running for real Shopify merchants, where an orchestrator coordinates two specialists: a wellness advisor in a regulated domain and a commerce agent that owns decision and checkout. We walk the decisions that matter: orchestration topology, intent routing and handoffs, shared versus isolated memory across agents, where the action boundary and per-agent guardrails live, and the latency and token cost that coordination multiplies. A demo follows one conversation from advice to checkout. You leave with an orchestration pattern, and the code to implement it directly in your online store.

title: Agentic commerce: shopping assistants to agent-ready infrastructure
description: AI agents are reshaping how consumers discover and purchase products, and retail and CPG brands have a massive opportunity to meet them where they are. This chalk talk covers both sides of the agentic commerce stack. First, we walk through how retailers can launch conversational shopping customized to their catalog and brand voice in weeks with the Agentic Shopping Assistant on AWS, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and inspired by Amazon's own AI shopping experience. Then we explore how to make your platform discoverable by external AI agents through structured product feeds, headless APIs, and payment orchestration for machine-initiated transactions.

title: Agentic developer experience with Amazon EKS
description: Transform your Kubernetes development workflow using generative AI. In this workshop, use Kiro CLI and the EKS MCP Server to automate complex operations, troubleshoot applications through natural language, and deploy micro services on Amazon EKS — all with AI-powered assistance. Work through hands-on labs: explore clusters using natural language, fix connectivity and ingress issues by orchestrating EKS MCP with Terraform MCP, and deploy new application components using AI-guided analysis. Leave with practical skills to integrate AI-powered automation into your existing Kubernetes workflows and dramatically improve developer productivity.

title: Agentic development with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
description: AI coding agents can write application logic, but can they provision your infrastructure too? In this chalk talk, explore AWS Cloud Development Kit's (AWS CDK) latest capabilities—Mixins, the CDK Toolkit Library, and programmatic synth/deploy APIs—make CDK a first-class target for agentic workflows. See how agents reason about constructs, compose infrastructure from natural-language intent, and validate results before deployment. We'll discuss patterns that work, guardrails that keep agents safe, and where human judgment still matters. Bring your questions—this is an interactive session for anyone curious about the intersection of AI agents and infrastructure as code.

title: Agentic development with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
description: AI coding agents can write application logic, but can they provision your infrastructure too? In this chalk talk, explore AWS Cloud Development Kit's (AWS CDK) latest capabilities—Mixins, the CDK Toolkit Library, and programmatic synth/deploy APIs—make CDK a first-class target for agentic workflows. See how agents reason about constructs, compose infrastructure from natural-language intent, and validate results before deployment. We'll discuss patterns that work, guardrails that keep agents safe, and where human judgment still matters. Bring your questions—this is an interactive session for anyone curious about the intersection of AI agents and infrastructure as code.

title: Agentic-Led Modernization: First Movers' Winning Formula with AWS Transform
description: Continuous modernization isn't optional — it's the engine of speed and competitive advantage. In this session, hear what early-adopter AWS Partners discovered building on AWS Transform, how composability lets them embed their own IP while harnessing AWS's customer reach, funding, and brand, and where the roadmap

title: Agentic Modernization with AWS Transform
description: AWS Transform orchestrates AI agents that analyze, refactor, and convert legacy applications without manual line-by-line rewrites. In this bootcamp, set modernization objectives, let AI agents decompose and transform .NET Framework code to cross-platform .NET on Linux, then migrate a SQL Server database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Practice agentic assessment, wave planning, code transformation, and schema conversion end to end.

title: Agentic Powered AWS Frontier Agents
description: Application failures and security vulnerabilities demand fast answers to reduce downtime. In this bootcamp, learn how to setup AWS DevOps Agent and automate investigation failures through logs, metrics, and code changes, then generate remediation plans. Learn how to use AWS Security Agent to configure domain-scoped penetration tests, monitor real-time execution, and interpret severity-rated findings. Gain hands-on experience with two agents that compress hours of investigation into minutes.

Gain hands-on experience with two agents that compress hours of investigation into minutes.

title: Agentic Process Transformation at Enterprise Scale
description: Your customers don't need another automation tool, they need the leap forward they're actually looking for with AI. Agentic Process Transformation (APT) is the framework partners use to help customers move past isolated task automation and into enterprise-wide process reinvention: redesigning entire processes from the ground up to grow revenue and improve the bottom line at a scale automation alone can't reach. We'll share how to spot these transformation opportunities and the architectural patterns that turn them into production solutions. Leave with a concrete strategy for helping your customers make that leap today.

title: Agentic Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) with the UK Home Office (sponsored by Capgemini)
description: The UK Home Office is tasked with keeping the UK Safe and Prosperous. Capgemini is working with the Home Office to increase effectiveness and efficiency of its digital and cloud services. Key areas include case management, legacy modernization and SDLC efficiency. This is being delivered in collaboration with AWS and Anthropic. Using Claude agents via AWS Bedrock, this capability is forecast to deliver >30% cashable savings compared to existing processes and improve quality by >20% through better informed decisions. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: Agents at the Edge: Global AI on Cloudflare + Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Cloudflare)
description: Most AI apps put the model and the user on opposite sides of the planet. This talk shows a better pattern: run inference on Amazon Bedrock, and run the agent itself on Cloudflare's edge, within ~50ms of 95% of the world's users. We'll walk through building a working agent with Workers (0ms cold starts), the Agents SDK, and Durable Objects for memory, with AI Gateway in front of Bedrock for caching, rate limiting, cost control, and observability. You'll leave with a reference architecture for shipping fast, cheap, and observable AI to a global audience. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudflare, an AWS Partner.

title: Agents at the Gate: Governing AI in EC2 Image Builder
description: EC2 Image Builder pipelines sprawl fast, and frontier agents that run for hours unattended need guardrails. In this builders' session, decompose Image Builder operations into reusable agent skills run via Kiro, Claude Code. Author AWSTOE components and orchestrate workflows, then harden images and scan for CVEs. Mid-build, a WaitForAction step pauses the pipeline and hands the image to AWS Security Agent to pentest; what it finds decides whether the build ships, bounded by severity, iteration caps, and human approval. Leave with a reusable skill library and governance pattern.

title: Agents can delete your data lake. Can you recover it? (sponsored by Rubrik)
description: AI is multiplying the identities and agents that can change your AWS data. One over-scoped role or runaway agent can delete or overwrite the data your models depend on, in an S3 lake or Iceberg lakehouse. Replication copies a bad write, versioning is often off. How do you recover without a valid backup? Learn where recovery breaks across S3, Glue Data Catalog, S3 Tables, and databases and pipelines around them, then how Rubrik recovers petabytes in hours, restoring only what changed, critical data first, within your RTO. Resilience spans your estate. Hear how TGS built a ransomware-resilient platform with Rubrik. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

title: Agents demand context. Build them a Streamhouse. (sponsored by Confluent)
description: Your agents can't act on yesterday's data. In this session, see how to connect streaming events, governed data, and agent orchestration into one production-ready streamhouse architecture on AWS. Learn how to build a complete, performant, and open streamhouse that delivers real-time context, elastic scale, and mission-critical reliability across every cloud and private environment without data silos. You'll leave with practical patterns for moving from brittle data pipelines to AI built on data streams, designed for speed, trust, and scale. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.

title: Agents need names too: Open standards for agent discovery
description: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. This session explores how AWS contributes to open source projects like DNS-AID (IETF/Linux Foundation) and AI-Catalog (Linux Foundation) to define the agent discovery layer atop existing DNS infrastructure. We'll walk through the specs — SVCB records, W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, HTTP Message Signatures — and show how anyone can resolve and verify an agent with off-the-shelf libraries and a single DNS query. No vendor lock-in. Standards in, standards out.

title: Agents run at the edge. The blast radius lives in the cloud (sponsored by Sysdig)
description: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. Bring your own agents. Ask us what they can reach. This presentation is brought to you by Sysdig, an AWS Partner.

title: Agents under oath: HIPAA-compliant agentic AI on AWS
description: AI agents in government healthcare don't just query databases. They reason, remember, and act. Each of those capabilities opens a new surface where protected health information (PHI) can leak model responses, persistent memory, tool calls, RAG retrieval, and agent traces. Traditional RBAC and encryption were not built for this. In this chalk talk, we will walk through a real prior authorization determination scenario together, map where PHI bleeds through an ungoverned agent and then redesign the architecture as a group — four trust zones, sixteen controls, all mapped to HIPAA Security Rule safeguards. Come ready to draw and debate.

title: Agents Under Oath: HIPAA-compliant agentic AI on AWS
description: Agents expose PHI across five surfaces RBAC can't see: model responses, persistent memory, tool calls, RAG retrieval, and agent traces. This chalk talk walks a HIPAA-compliant reference architecture on AWS: four trust zones, sixteen controls mapped to Security Rule safeguards. Bring questions.

title: AI-accelerated migration from self-managed Kubernetes to EKS Auto Mode
description: Most teams start with one or two Amazon EKS clusters and grow into a fleet. AWS manages the control plane, but on standard EKS your team still owns version upgrades, add-ons, node lifecycle, and operational efforts. This session shows how to move that undifferentiated work to Amazon EKS Auto Mode, and how AI accelerates the migration itself. See how agentic tooling inventories your EKS clusters, translates node and add-on configuration, and flags what must change before you cut over. Learn patterns for enabling EKS Auto Mode with minimal disruption, then scaling the migration across your fleet in a fraction of the time manual work takes.

title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
description: AI agents are the new web visitors, but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

title: AI agents for HPC operations
description: Managing HPC infrastructure shouldn’t slow down science and engineering. Learn how AI-powered agents with AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) automate workload placement, detect and recover from failures, and simplify day-to-day cluster operations. Through practical examples, we’ll show how intelligent automation reduces operational overhead, improves resource utilization, and enables platform teams to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time supporting research and innovation.

title: AI agents for PostgreSQL replication and partitioning
description: Recent PostgreSQL releases introduced transformative capabilities for logical replication and partitioning, including filtering, parallel apply, sequence replication, and improved planning for partition-heavy workloads. These features are powerful, but tuning them for a specific environment remains complex. In this session, learn to build agents for these core PostgreSQL concepts on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: one that analyzes workloads to recommend optimal logical replication configuration, and a partitioning agent that evaluates query patterns and table bloat to guide table partitioning strategy.

title: AI-assisted data modeling for Amazon DynamoDB
description: In this session, learn practical Amazon DynamoDB data modeling through an AI-assisted approach. Architect complex data models using sophisticated techniques right inside an AI-powered IDE, then go from modeling to production, building a full-stack, serverless application powered by DynamoDB and other AWS services via a coding agent of choice. Optimize access patterns, leverage secondary indexes, and express application requirements in natural language to generate and refine a complete solution built on DynamoDB. Discover how AI-assisted database design accelerates complex NoSQL decisions at every stage of development. Bring your laptop to participate.

Optimize access patterns, leverage secondary indexes, and express application requirements in natural language to generate and refine a complete solution built on DynamoDB. Discover how AI-assisted database design accelerates complex NoSQL decisions at every stage of development. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: AI at Lennar: Driving 80,000 Home Deliveries with Bedrock & Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
description: Lennar is bringing AI into the everyday work behind more than 80,000 home deliveries a year, from land research and acquisition to construction, customer engagement, and sales. Join Ralph Gootee, CTO of Lennar, and Ariel Assaraf, CEO of Coralogix, for a practical look at moving AI from experimentation into production. They’ll share how Lennar is building and scaling AI agents on Amazon Bedrock, using AWS inference services and open-source models, and how Coralogix helps teams understand adoption, performance, cost, and business impact. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
description: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.

title: AI discipline: UCLA's data foundation and framework for saying no
description: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) invested in their data foundation first. Their large-scale data modernization—Bruin Cloud and the campus Data Hub—created a unified, governed data environment across a sprawling research university, but it wasn't enough. As AI demand surged, Deputy CIO Veronica Garcia and her team built a disciplined product management approach to evaluate, prioritize, and scale AI use cases against UCLA's mission. Learn how UCLA’s technical architecture accelerated data modernization, the framework used to determine AI priorities, and the governance model that keeps it all aligned that launched high-impact use cases from increasing fundraising, advancing research, and supporting student safety and success.

title: AI-driven optimizations for HPC configurations on AWS
description: Choosing the right HPC configuration often requires extensive benchmarking across instance types, MPI implementations, core counts, and application-specific settings. Learn how AWS uses AI to predict optimal HPC configurations from historical workload data, helping engineers make informed decisions before launching large-scale jobs. We’ll cover the models behind these recommendations and demonstrate how AI reduces trial and error while improving performance, cost efficiency, and time to solution.

title: AI flight plan: How British Airways’ parent builds and measures AI ROI (sponsored by NTT DATA)
description: British Airways’ parent, International Airlines Group (IAG), has moved rapidly from AI experimentation to production deployments delivering measurable results. This session explores how IAG and its partner NTT DATA assess AI opportunities by giving business units ownership of value realization, build momentum by prioritizing high-impact use cases, and operationalize AI through scalable technology, operating models, governance and change management. Attendees will learn how to connect AI strategy to top- and bottom-line impact through real-world examples, including procurement optimization, contract leakage detection and citizen-developed agents that accelerate safe, responsible AI adoption across the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NTT DATA, an AWS Partner.

title: AI for Impact: Elevating human potential through inclusive innovation
description: Learn how California's Department of Developmental Services (DDS) is leveraging AWS to modernize legacy systems and unify data for half a million individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities across 21 regional centers and acute care hospitals. See how this aligns with HR.1 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) requirements for government modernization within CA Health and Human Services. Explore responsible AI agents with fairness scoring and bias detection that improve equitable service delivery. Discover how multi-agent architectures on Amazon Bedrock enable transparent, auditable decisions for vulnerable populations — a replicable blueprint for ethical AI at scale.

title: AI Governance: The Framework, The Pitfalls, The Playbook (sponsored by Vanta)
description: The AI revolution is upending organizations’ security and GRC programs. Shadow AI is exploding as employees adopt new agent harnesses, workflows, platforms, and plugins. Even sanctioned AI poses new challenges that don’t yet have standardized solutions. Meanwhile, developers are moving AI applications from experimentation to production, introducing new risks. This session will break down what AI Governance is all about, cover common concerns that it’s meant to resolve, and provide attendees with practical tips for solving some of their most pressing AI Governance challenges. What you’ll learn. What AI Governance entails, from practical policy to active protections. How to solve AI Governance concerns across different layers of the AI stack. This presentation is brought to you by Vanta, an AWS Partner.

title: AI innovations across network monitoring and operations
description: Join us to explore how AI is transforming network monitoring and observability. This session dives into new capabilities for traffic analysis, network health monitoring, and faster issue resolution that shows how intelligent, automated tooling helps you move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive insight. Whether you want to cut time-to-resolution or get a clearer, real-time pulse on your network's health, come see what's new and what's on the horizon.

title: AI is Breaking Data Security… And Fixing It (sponsored by Concentric AI)
description: AI is rapidly becoming one of the biggest drivers of productivity and innovation in the enterprise — and one of the fastest-growing sources of data security risk. As copilots, assistants, and public AI tools become integrated into daily work, sensitive data is flowing into systems that most security teams can’t fully see, understand, or control. The problem is that traditional data security controls were never built for this. In fact, many organizations were already struggling to operationalize data security before AI accelerated the challenge. The good news? AI isn’t just creating the problem — it’s also enabling a smarter, more effective way to solve it. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how AI is reshaping data security — and how they can use that same technology to gain control, minimize exposure, and support safer AI adoption across the business. This presentation is brought to you by Concentric AI, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Is Getting Smarter. AI-Generated Code Isn’t Getting Safer. (sponsored by Veracode, Inc.)
description: AI-generated code is scaling fast, but its security performance is not keeping up. Across more than 100 models tested since 2023, the average security pass rate remains stuck at 56%, even as syntax performance approaches perfection. For security leaders, this is no longer a developer tooling discussion. It is a verification, release-control, and accountability issue. In this session, Veracode leaders unpack the findings from the 2026 GenAI Code Security Report and turn them into practical actions for secure software delivery at scale. Whether you’re a developer, security lead, or business decision-maker, this session will help you navigate the real-world security implications of GenAI in your development workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Veracode, Inc., an AWS Partner.

title: AI Meets Production: The New Reliability Playbook for Financial Services (sponsored by Traversal)
description: Financial services depend on software that needs to be available around the clock. When that software fails, the consequences can affect millions of customers and create regulatory, financial, and reputational risk. This panel brings together technology leaders from some of the world’s largest financial institutions across banking, payments, and investment management for a conversation moderated by Anish Agrawal, CEO & Cofounder of Traversal, the AI SRE helping diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents across complex enterprise environments. Together, they’ll discuss how AI is changing production reliability across financial services, where it’s already being used, the emerging role of AI SREs, what teams look for when evaluating new approaches, and what it takes to deploy AI safely in highly regulated environments. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

title: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
description: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then apply Amazon Bedrock–powered agents for proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. See how AWS DevOps Agent extends this with autonomous remediation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days.

title: AIOps strategy: foundations before firefighting
description: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before deciding what they actually want it to handle, investment is racing ahead of maturity. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We map the two halves that teams miss: using AI to run operations and the operational foundations that let AI scale safely, such as cost, security, and organizational readiness. We discuss what to automate, what stays human, and where agents earn autonomy. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity checklist for your team.

The three hands-on labs give you practical experience to apply these skills immediately in your organization

Explore AWS services for automated optimizations, rightsizing, and savings plans. Gain experience with AI/ML and container workload cost allocation, multi-cloud reporting, and AI-powered spend analysis. Implement automated strategies using real workload data. Laptop required

title: AI-Powered Profitability: How Partners Are Winning with AWS
description: AI is reshaping partner economics. Hear from AWS VP Julia Chen about how to build a profitable AI-first business. This session covers the evolution of AWS Partner Programs, from transactional resell to outcome-driven partnerships, and reveals which programs, incentives, enablement, and tools deliver the highest ROI. Discover how AI-powered differentiation lowers your cost of sales, attracts high-value customers, deepens relationships, and enables innovation at scale. You'll leave with insights about where to invest and pathways for growth.

title: AI Spreadsheets and the Modern Data Stack: An AWS Story (sponsored by Row Zero)
description: AWS relies on spreadsheets for planning, forecasting, business intelligence, and self service analytics. To improve self-serve data analysis, AWS rolled out Row Zero, a cloud-based AI spreadsheet that can open billion row datasets, connect directly to data warehouses, and provide enterprise grade security controls. This session covers how AWS solved their legacy spreadsheet problems that are constrained by the compute and memory resources of employee laptops and a 1 million row limit. By adopting Row Zero, business users can derive insights and have secure access to governed data in Amazon S3, Redshift, or Athena at massive scale. This presentation is brought to you by Row Zero, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
description: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profile kernels, tune collectives, feed the GPUs, and survive the failures that compound with scale. In this workshop, you walk the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances — compute, network, and storage; the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks — and stand up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer: measure, attribute, fix with the tool that sees inside. Leave with dashboards you built yourself and a goodput methodology for your training clusters.

title: AI That Answers: Customer Experiences Reimagined with Amazon Connect (sponsored by PwC)
description: Join PwC and four leading clients across industries to hear real examples of how Amazon Connect is transforming customer experience and delivering business outcomes. This session showcases cutting-edge omnichannel solutions across voice, chat, and messaging, along with agentic AI capabilities driving automation in areas like order management and real-time updates. Hear how organizations are deploying next-generation, AI-powered voice solutions in production, with new innovations continuing to emerge. Discover how these advancements deliver measurable business value, backed by PwC's outcome-based approach that ties technology investment directly to efficiency gains and improved customer and business performance. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Threat Readiness: Securing AWS Workloads at Machine Speed (sponsored by Wiz)
description: As AI accelerates development in the cloud, it’s also increasingly expanding the cloud attack surface. With autonomous agents accelerating both software deployment and vulnerability exploitation, traditional security workflows can no longer keep pace. Organizations need a new operating model for AI Threat Readiness inside high-velocity AWS environments that builds agentic trust without slowing innovation. This session explores how combining full AWS visibility with agentic workflows, including Wiz Red, Green, and Blue Agents, transforms reactive cloud security into proactive, machine-speed defense across Amazon Bedrock, containers, and serverless architectures. This presentation is brought to you by Wiz, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Transformation: Redesigning How Work Gets Done (sponsored by Lucid Software)
description: Every major technology shift starts the same way. We use new technology to do the old thing. Early factories replaced steam engines with electric motors, but real transformation came when they redesigned the factory around what electricity made possible. We’re doing the same thing with AI. AI transformation isn’t about adding agents to existing workflows. It’s about redesigning how work gets done. That starts with context. In this session, we’ll show how teams can make work visible, give humans and AI a shared understanding of it, redesign workflows around agents, and turn that understanding into action. This presentation is brought to you by Lucid Software, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Writes the Code. Who Reviews the Reviewer?
description: AI coding assistants now write, refactor, and even review code at scale but who's actually accountable when something breaks in production? This session explores how AI has reshaped the code review process: faster first-pass reviews, AI-generated suggestions, and agentic tools running directly in CI/CD pipelines. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.

title: A leader's guide to advanced teams models in an agentic world
description: Agents made execution cheap. The work did not disappear. It moved into deciding what should exist, checking what agents produce, and owning it when something breaks. Most team designs were not built for that. This session gives you four questions to ask of any piece of work: what is it for, what does it touch, how will we check it, and whose name is on it. Then we walk through the team models leaders reach for, what each gets wrong, and where the pager and the name should sit. You leave knowing who does what now.

title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
description: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

title: A leader’s guide to governing AI, on behalf of humans
description: AI deployments can reason, problem-solve, and act with increasing agency. Leaving governance models built for deterministic software no longer sufficient. AWS Executive in Residence Ryan Seaman and Dr. Bernadette Han, organizational psychologist at the American Psychological Association (APA), bring technology and human behavior into one governance conversation. As AI interacts with people, influences decisions, and takes actions, governance must address not only what AI can do, but how it behaves with people and what happens as a result. Bernadette introduces the EEI-AI Behavioral Architecture™, translating psychological science into behavioral requirements organizations can design for, test, observe, and govern responsibly.

title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
description: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
description: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

title: A leader's guide to moving from AI investment gridlock to acceleration
description: Fund the platform or the use case? Demand proof before investing, or invest to generate the proof? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and can't wait for the annual budget cycle. To move at the pace of AI, the CIO and CFO must be in lockstep. Two former operators share how the best pairs manage AI like a venture portfolio: bets in the face of uncertainty, recycling of wins into the next ones, and governance that scales across the portfolio rather than project by project — plus the key questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

title: A leader's guide to predicting and proving AI value
description: Every organization faces the same AI questions: How do we predict and manage costs? How do we prove value when outcomes are hard to measure? How do we move fast without losing control? Two finance leaders, one advising enterprise executives and one managing AI economics at scale inside Amazon, share what is working, what is not, and where teams go wrong. Learn how to measure AI cost and value in terms finance and technology leaders agree on, which guardrails to set as investment grows, and how to make the case for AI value to your board.

title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
description: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
description: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.

title: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
description: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.

title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
description: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

title: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
description: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.

title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
description: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

title: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
description: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
description: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
description: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.

title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
description: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
description: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
description: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
description: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. title: Answering CX questions 10x faster with Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Quick
description: Amazon Connect Customer generates a deep set of signals from every customer interaction. Sentiment, intent, conversation analytics, resolution outcomes. It's all there and Connect Customer gives you built-in tools to explore it. But we wanted to go further. We wanted anyone in the organization to ask questions about customer interactions in plain language and get answers instantly. So we paired Connect Customer's analytics data lake with Amazon Quick. In this session, we walk through how we did it, including how we handled cross-account Lake Formation access, and show how our broader team now asks questions and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster from question to action.

title: Aon: Turning raw exposure data into faster underwriting
description: Insurers and brokers process thousands of Statements of Values annually, complex unstructured documents that require manual extraction and validation and delay quoting and bind decisions. In this lightning talk, learn how Aon built an AI-powered exposure data ingestion platform on Amazon Bedrock using Anthropic Claude, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. See how the platform transforms unstructured data into standardized, risk-ready information with improved address quality, geocoding precision, and hazard identification, reducing document processing from days to minutes and feeding higher-quality inputs to catastrophe models.

title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
description: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. In this builder session, use Kiro — AWS's AI-powered development environment — to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one — no more tribal knowledge walking out the door.

title: Apply Amazon's frontier team playbook to your organization
description: AI coding agents sped up code generation, but not how fast it reaches customers. Teams seeing 4.5x to 10x gains aren't just adopting tools. They've redesigned how they work. In this chalk talk, learn what these "frontier teams" do differently: investing in agent context and steering files, making intent explicit before code is written, feeding agents well-scoped work instead of babysitting them, shifting testing left so agents self-correct before they reach the pipeline. We'll unpack real examples from teams across Amazon and talk through how to run your own pilot. Bring your questions about making AI work in your organization.

title: A practitioner’s guide to data for agentic AI
description: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.

title: Architecting Enterprise Agents on Bedrock
description: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.

title: Architecting firewalls on AWS: a layered defense strategy
description: With automated traffic now more than half of the web, a single firewall layer can't separate good bots from L7 attacks. This chalk talk covers how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including firewall patterns attached to AWS Transit Gateway. Then we dig into the tradeoffs, including centralized versus distributed inspection, cost versus latency, and when one service can carry the load and when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we whiteboard a design for your environment.

title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
description: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

title: Architect, launch, and optimize solutions with AWS Marketplace
description: Discover how new AWS Marketplace capabilities can help turn your solutions into scalable commercial offerings including AI-powered and multi-product offerings. In this interactive workshop, explore key decisions across architecture, packaging, deployment, pricing, and launch readiness. Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. Leave with practical guidance and an actionable plan to accelerate launch, drive recurring revenue, and improve customer retention.

title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
description: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.

title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
description: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything.
