title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
description: Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
description: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

title: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
description: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.

title: Ask the News: Making Decades of Publisher Content Instantly Searchable (sponsored by MongoDB)
description: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. Featuring ArcXP, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
description: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.

title: At Petabyte Scale: Building an AI Telemetry Lake with Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
description: The Access Group is turning petabytes of telemetry from hundreds of teams into an engine for business performance. Its telemetry lake gives teams a clearer view of product health, helping them spot risks sooner, solve problems faster, and understand how technology shapes the customer experience. Join The Access Group CTO Thad Széll and Coralogix CEO Ariel Assaraf to learn how unified telemetry is moving the business from reactive troubleshooting to continuous product improvement. Hear how it is sharpening decisions, focusing teams on what matters most, and creating the trusted data foundation needed to advance The Access Group’s AI ambitions. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

title: A Unified AWS Data and AI Strategy for SAP Customers
description: Explore how AWS and SAP customers can unlock value through converging data and AI strategies. From zero-copy integration with SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon S3, to enterprise AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, learn practical approaches to automate SAP processes and accelerate innovation at scale.

title: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
description: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

title: Automate AI governance and risk management with John Deere
description: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. Walk through AWS Responsible AI best practices for governing AI across the full development lifecycle. Then see how John Deere applied these principles through AI Risk Intelligence (AIRI) to automate risk management. Learn how static checks verify controls at code and documentation level while dynamic checks analyze APIs and traces in real time, achieving over 30% reduction in assessment time and continuous visibility into AI risk posture. Learn what it takes to move from periodic manual assessments to continuous, automated governance.

title: Automate and Scale Cloud Operations with Purpose-Built AI Agents
description: Engineering teams lose time correlating telemetry, triaging alerts, investigating threats, and turning findings into fixes. This session explores how Datadog’s purpose-built AI agents can reduce that operational burden by applying organizational context and production telemetry to focused developer, SRE, and security workflows. Using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, we’ll examine where agents can improve operational excellence, reliability, security, performance efficiency, and cost optimization.

title: Automated compliance evidence from day one
description: Your compliance team spends weeks collecting evidence manually before every audit. Automated evidence collection eliminates that burden from day one. In this builders' session, you'll learn how to leverage AWS GRC services, including AWS Config, AWS Organizations, AWS CloudTrail, and Control Catalog, to configure automated evidence collection, map controls to your target framework, use the AI compliance agent to validate both technical controls and procedural policies, and build continuous drift detection that alerts you before your next audit finds the gap.

title: Automate disaster recovery with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: Financial institutions face stringent regulatory requirements for operational resilience, demanding reliable disaster recovery with tight RTO/RPO targets across complex application portfolios. Yet failover procedures often remain manual and prone to error under pressure. In this chalk talk, we explore how to design a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates end-to-end disaster recovery automation for regulated workloads. We’ll walk through how a coordination agent delegates to specialized sub-agents for readiness verification, infrastructure operations, Terraform code generation, Git operations, and deployment validation—each with human-in-the-loop approval gates.

title: Automate dispute resolution with Amazon Connect and Amazon Bedrock
description: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.

title: Automate Investigations to Resolve Application Failures with AWS DevOps Agent
description: Every minute of downtime is a minute your customers notice. What if an agent could correlate your logs, metrics, and change history the moment an application fails? In this hands-on lab, use AWS DevOps Agent to autonomously investigate operational issues across your AWS environment. Trigger investigations from simulated application failures, observe the agent correlate logs, metrics, and change history in real time, and review root cause analyses with actionable mitigation plans.

title: Automate patching and compliance with AI-powered visibility
description: Tracking patch compliance across hundreds of accounts is manual, slow, and hard to prove to auditors. In this hands-on builders' session, you automate patching and continuous compliance in your environment, then let AI do the heavy lifting: generate a multi-account compliance dashboard with Apps in Amazon Quick and answer compliance questions with natural language instead of hand-building reports. By the end, you'll know how to turn raw patch data into audit-ready answers on demand.

title: Automate Penetration Tests with AWS Security Agent
description: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Security Agent. Set up an Agent Space with VPC networking, verify target domains, scope tests by risk type, and monitor execution in real time. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams.

title: Automate your AWS partnership with a unified agentic operating model
description: Getting the most from your AWS partnership requires thoughtful and sustained engagement from both sides. Instead of heavy manual lifts, an agentic partner operating model supports this engagement at scale through strategic automation, delivering the right guidance, insight, and capabilities to team members who need them most. In this workshop, build a unified agentic operating model that connects pipeline, co-sell coordination, and AWS consumption measurement into a single orchestration layer using your CRM, AWS Partner Central, and Amazon Quick, enabling all team members to easily leverage AWS tools, insights, and investments from one agentic surface to increase your AWS engagement.

title: Automating Serverless migrations at scale with AWS Transform
description: Runtime deprecations pile up. API migrations stall. Legacy code sits untouched because manual upgrades across hundreds of functions take weeks your team doesn't have. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to assess, plan, and execute Lambda runtime upgrades and API migrations at scale. Working hands-on, you'll run the full agentic loop: codebase assessment, transformation planning, incremental code changes committed to Git, and self-validating test execution. You'll scale transformations across hundreds of functions in parallel using AWS Batch and Fargate. Walk away with patterns for automated, large-scale modernization. Bring your laptop.

title: Autonomous AI Ops with AWS DevOps Agent and New Relic Autopilot (sponsored by New Relic)
description: Incident investigation still consumes 1-2 hours of engineering time per event. See how New Relic's Intelligent Observability Platform integrates with AWS DevOps Agent to: Autonomously triage incidents, pinpoint root cause, and deliver actionable remediation with no custom tooling required. Investigate incidents agentically correlating telemetry, code, and deployments across AWS, multi cloud, and on-prem environments. Demonstrate how this innovation proactively prevents future incidents by analyzing patterns and recommending improvements. Learn how customers are cutting MTTR by 75% and shifting from firefighting to prevention, and walk away ready to get started. This presentation is brought to you by New Relic, an AWS Partner.

title: Autonomous DBOps: Agentic AI for maintaining databases
description: Maintaining performance for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS often requires manual effort, such as tuning queries, managing indexes, and handling alerts. In this builders' session, learn how to leverage agentic AI solutions implementing LLM-powered autonomous agents to monitor, diagnose, and optimize relational databases in real time. We will demonstrate how AI agents can analyze slow query logs, recommend or apply tuning actions, and trigger intelligent alerts using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Cloudwatch, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Systems Manager. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Autonomous Multi-Agent system for Manufacturing: Live Demo with Kiro
description: To achieve the operational agility markets require, manufacturers are turning to AI agents that can reason and act autonomously across the product lifecycle. This session demonstrates how to rapidly build autonomous multi-agent systems using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Kiro that connect CMMS, MES, and ERP systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP). Watch a live demo where we use Kiro to develop specialized manufacturing agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root causes, and orchestrate corrective actions autonomously. Discover how Kiro's spec-driven development workflow compresses multi-agent system development from months to days. Leave with proven architecture patterns that you can apply to transform your production planning, supply chain optimization, and anomaly management processes.

title: Autonomous operations: reducing MTTR at scale, feat. BMG Bank
description: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.

title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
description: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.

description: Simulate commanding autonomous drone fleets for search-and-rescue using Amazon Bedrock Agents, IoT Greengrass, and SageMaker. We demo a Human-Machine Teaming architecture where AI operates autonomously within trust boundaries, escalating to humans via configurable confidence thresholds.

title: AWS AI agents accelerate SAP migration and modernization on AWS
description: The legacy ERP system that once gave you a competitive edge may now be limiting your ability to innovate. Modernizing SAP can be complex, expensive, risky, and every delay is a missed opportunity to innovate. In this Chalk Talk, you will learn how AI Agents can make it possible to upgrade to SAP's Cloud ERP safely and cost-effectively in weeks, not months. Whether you're running SAP ECC, moving to RISE with SAP, modernizing ABAP and PI/PO, or migrating SAP Business Warehouse (BW), discover how AI-powered agents can take on the heavy lifting for you

title: AWS AI Factories: Bring production scale AI to your data center
description: Data sovereignty, data gravity, and latency requirements prevent many organizations from running all AI workloads in the public cloud. AWS AI Factories bring AWS and NVIDIA AI infrastructure directly into your data center, fully operated, maintained, and continuously updated by AWS. Run leading foundation models on premises for training and inference without building and managing AI infrastructure yourself or negotiating separate agreements with model providers. In this session, learn how organizations are accelerating AI adoption, reducing time to value, and maintaining full control of their data while benefiting from the AWS experience in their own facilities.

title: AWS AI from chips to agents: The end-to-end production AI foundation
description: The AI experiment is over. Now it has to work. This session walks through the AWS AI Platform end-to-end, starting at the chip layer with AWS Trainium and AWS Graviton delivering up to 40% better price performance. From there, model inference and customization through Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Then production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Every layer co-designed so workloads move across the stack without rearchitecting. You will leave knowing which service handles which job, where the layers connect to accelerate production timelines, and how to keep your architecture open as your AI strategy evolves.

title: AWS CDK - Contributing AI safety tooling to the IaC ecosystem
description: AI agents generate infrastructure-as-code that looks correct but fails 38% of the time at deployment. The open source Agent Toolkit for AWS provides skills for validation, linting, and security checks that any MCP-compatible AI tool can consume before deploying. This chalk talk covers how we contributed these capabilities as open source tooling that works across cfn-lint, Checkov, and cdk-nag, improving first-deploy success from 62% to 82%. Attendees discuss how to build similar validation layers for their own IaC tools and the tradeoffs between blocking vs advisory checks in agent workflows.

description: Prepare for AWS Certified AI Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Generative AI knowledge unlocks doors here. Enter a narrative-driven 3D world, choose your avatar, and tackle progressively harder puzzles tied to AWS Certified AI Practitioner exam domains. Each locked room blends exam-style questions with hands-on labs covering foundation models, responsible AI, prompt engineering, and agentic workflows. Collaborate with teammates, solve challenges under time pressure, and race to escape before your peers to top the leaderboard.

description: You became a DBA, and now someone's asking you to be a cloud architect too. With over 240 AWS services, knowing where to start is half the battle. We'll also explore how AI-powered tools like Kiro and AWS Transform can accelerate your ramp-up, from intelligent code generation to modernizing .NET and SQL Server workloads. You'll leave with a clear path to choosing, securing, and cost-optimizing the right services. Come with questions.

description: Join us for an immersive, collaborative learning exercise to build practical skills in deploying and monitoring AI-powered applications on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll engineer production-ready AI systems and ensure reliability through comprehensive observability. Leverage Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock Agentcore, foundation models, AI agents, prompt engineering, model evaluation, and ML pipeline monitoring as you build and operate AI workloads end-to-end. Face challenges demanding both engineering excellence and operational awareness for AI systems in production! Whether you're an experienced ML engineer or just starting to build with AI, this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with New Relic. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS GameDay - Application Security & AI-Powered Penetration Testing
description: Join us for an immersive, collaborative exercise to develop practical skills in application security on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll configure security agents, launch AI-driven penetration tests, and remediate critical vulnerabilities before the biggest production launch of the year for Unicorn.Rentals. Build skills in agent-based security assessment, OWASP Top 10 vulnerability identification, and shift-left security practices. Every unpatched vulnerability is an open door. You and your AI-powered security agent are the only things standing between your application and compromise! Whether you're a security engineer, DevOps practitioner, developer, or cloud architect, security is your responsibility, and this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS Jam: All-in Builder Showdown
description: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Dive deep into AWS with our All-In session — hands-on environments covering AI-powered solutions, DevOps automation, and cloud security. Explore cutting-edge AI services, streamline deployments, and implement security best practices. Challenges are designed for all skill levels, with helpful clues and AWS expert support throughout. Work solo or as a team on real-world scenarios, expand your AWS expertise, and connect with fellow cloud enthusiasts. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: AWS Jam: All-in Builder Showdown - sponsored by Vonage
description: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Tackle AI, DevOps, and security scenarios across AWS services - including a sponsored challenge from Vonage to add real-time voice, video, and messaging to applications using Vonage communications APIs. Challenges suit all skill levels, with AWS expert guidance and helpful clues throughout. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs: Strong isolation for agents & beyond
description: Agents running generated code, multi-tenant platforms, and untrusted workloads all need strong isolation, but each traditional compute option forces a tradeoff. VMs isolate well but start slowly. Containers are fast but share a kernel. Functions scale to zero but limit state. Teams close the gaps with isolation logic they build and maintain themselves. Lambda MicroVMs offer sandboxes with VM-level isolation for each agent, tenant, or task: state that persists across invocations, automatic suspend on idle, resume on demand. This session covers how MicroVMs work, the security and isolation model, lifecycle management, and patterns for agentic sandboxing and untrusted code execution.

title: AWS migration agents fast-tracking SAP modernization
description: AI agents built on AWS are fast-tracking SAP migration and modernization from months to days. Learn from our marquee customers how they are deploying agentic fleets on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore spanning SAP landscape, auto-resolving complex workflows same-day that previously took days across multiple teams, saving thousands of hours and millions in operational costs. A reusable framework means each new agent inherits production-grade infrastructure from day one. In this session, learn how AI-powered migration agents de-risk ECC-to-S/4HANA transitions, accelerate RISE with SAP adoption, and modernize ABAP and BW workloads.

title: AWSome Automation: From Project Brief Prompt to Landing Page (sponsored by Storyblok)
description: Building a product-launch agent means solving several problems at once: assembling content from approved components, enforcing brand guidelines, localizing across markets, and ensuring a human has final say before anything reaches production. This session examines how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Storyblok handle each of those concerns without requiring a separate governance layer. Explore why a custom Strands agent made more sense than the no-code harness, how Cedar policies, Storyblok's component whitelist, brand guidelines, and publishing workflows form complementary guardrail layers, and how the architecture takes a brief to a reviewed, localized landing page in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Storyblok, an AWS Partner.

title: AWS Partner: Agentic AI workflows for business users on Amazon Quick
description: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. Walk through a hands-on business scenario using Amazon Quick, the agentic AI workspace that connects to your tools and learns your workflows. Create knowledge spaces, run deep-research agents, connect external APIs, automate multi-step processes with Flows, and build a custom AI agent in a browser. Leave able to help customers put agentic AI to work across their teams and business applications. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AWS Partner: Build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption
description: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. AI workflows fail in ways that don't show up until production: a human misses the deadline, an external system says no, a sub-workflow loses state mid-flight. Fix it. Combine Step Functions, Lambda durable functions, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore into a three-layer stack that routes decisions, checkpoints execution, and reasons through uncertainty. Run real scenarios through the Simulator Panel and trace every layer live. Leave ready to build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AWS Partner: Build the AgentCore agent your demo pretends to be
description: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. A good prompt gets you a chatbot. Everything else on AgentCore turns it into an agent. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add persistent memory so it stops forgetting, tools through Gateway to reach real data, and Cedar policies that enforce boundaries, plus production traces, quality evaluations, and AI-driven optimization with A/B testing. Leave with hands-on experience on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and ready to show customers what separates a chatbot from an agent worth paying for. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Become an AWS AI Business Strategist
description: Turning an AI idea into enterprise reality requires more than technical knowledge. In this bootcamp, you apply the Discover, Design, Deliver framework to diagnose business problems, assess organizational readiness, and scope AI pilots with clear success criteria. You navigate responsible AI tradeoffs, lead change management across cross-functional teams, evaluate agentic AI architectures for autonomy versus control, and build phased scaling strategies from proof of concept through production deployment.

title: Benchmarking Bedrock knowledge bases for agents in production (sponsored by Braintrust)
description: In this talk, we’ll walk through an independent eval of Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which manages the ingestion, parsing, and retrieval steps in a RAG application. In the first half, we’ll cover our methodology, including how we developed a dataset that queries documents such as tickets, wiki pages, and product docs, and what we decided to score: latency, cost, relevance, and citation support. We’ll also cover how we analyzed the results with research rigor, including p50 and p95 latency and confidence intervals around our metrics. In the second half, we’ll expand this into a conceptual understanding of evals and observability: why they’re important, how other companies are implementing them in production, and the terminology you need to know. This presentation is brought to you by Braintrust, an AWS Partner.

title: Best path forward: Rehost & replatform to containers with AWS Transform
description: Not every app needs the same migration path, and figuring out which ones to rehost versus containerize is where teams get stuck. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to plan a combined migration and modernization across your application portfolio, then execute a mix of container and rehost migrations deploying to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll work through the full lifecycle. Learn how to order waves and coordinate cutover across a mixed portfolio. Leave with a realistic multi-wave plan you can apply to your own environment. Laptop required.

title: Best practices for building an observability strategy in the age of AI
description: Most observability strategies were built for a pre-AI world and are no longer enough. Your data foundation remains critical, but the way you use that data is changing fast. In this chalk talk, we explore what stays the same, what must evolve, and what's new as AI reshapes observability. We'll cover the shift from static dashboards to dynamic experiences, from reactive alarms to AI-driven insights, and the new questions you need to answer, like how well your agents are performing. Join us as we share what AWS is learning as we embrace AI-led observability.

title: Best practices for making coding agent orchestration more deterministic
description: As agents work on longer, more complex tasks, the context window fills up and the agent can lose track of its plan and execution steps. The manual setup required to get multi-agent orchestration to reliably complete these kinds of tasks can be complex and brittle. In this chalk talk, we will walk through best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale multi-agent workloads. Bring questions, challenges, or edge cases you ran into and we'll walk you through how to approach them to improve reliability.

title: Best Practices for .NET modernization with AWS Transform
description: As organizations look to reduce tech debt for their .NET applications, builders are looking to accelerate modernization with AI tools. In this hands-on session, we'll explore best practices for modernizing .NET Framework applications with AWS Transform. You'll learn how to work alongside the agent to reach a desired outcome. Together, we will apply plan customizations, steering documents, checkpoints, and iteration. Come ready to share your use cases and leave with practical steps to efficient, cost-effective modernization. Bring your laptop with Visual Studio and an AWS account onboarded to AWS Transform.

title: Beyond AIOps: Operating safely in the age of agent sprawl
description: As organisations move from a small number of AI assistants to a distributed ecosystem of agents that can discover tools, make decisions, and act, operational excellence must evolve. Drawing on HMRC’s work to develop a governed platform model for agentic systems, this session explores a practical maturity model spanning inventory, ownership, identity, delegated authority, observability, blast-radius controls, evaluation, and human accountability. Learn how existing platform engineering, SRE, security and service-management practices can be extended across cloud and SaaS ecosystems without creating a separate governance regime for every agent or vendor. Designed for platform leaders, SREs and architects preparing to scale agents safely in complex, regulated environments.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
description: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.

title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
description: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.

title: Beyond code generation: accelerating the entire SDLC on AWS
description: Teams pour AI into code generation and wonder why they're not shipping faster. In reality, accelerating one stage just moves the bottleneck downstream. This session follows a single task across its entire lifecycle and shows where AI compounds. We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent), ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. Come see our vision for an SDLC where every stage moves at the same speed.

title: Beyond Evals: Setting up your agents and your enterprise for success (sponsored by LangChain)
description: We are witnessing models and agents continually becoming more capable,  all while the process of meaningfully evaluating them continues to be a challenge. In this session, we will dissect eval best practices observed both in the field and internally at LangChain. This session will go beyond just your technical evaluation toolkit and provide practical organizational and process takeaways and a better understanding of what future capabilities are unlocked downstream of good evaluation. This session will be especially relevant to teams deploying agents in cross-functional domains. This presentation is brought to you by LangChain, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium
description: Supervised fine-tuning enables your model to follow instructions, but teaching it to reason requires reinforcement learning. RL workflows demand iterative loops that multiply compute costs — making AWS Trainium's purpose-built price performance critical. In this chalk talk, we explore what techniques like RLHF and GRPO bring to the table and how to run them on Trainium with the AWS Neuron software stack, Torchtitan, HuggingFace TRL, vLLM, and native PyTorch. We compare co-located vs. disaggregated RL architectures. You'll leave ready to implement cost-effective RL loops that train agents to reason.

title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium

title: Beyond pilots: agentic AI transforming mortgage operations and IT at scale (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
description: Mortgage lending still runs on handoffs, exceptions, and manual review. See how a leading US mortgage lender is rebuilding origination and servicing with agentic AI on AWS, cutting cycle times while keeping controls and auditability intact. We will also show how the same agent patterns reach IT operations, resolving incidents before customers feel them. Tata Consultancy Services shares the reference architecture, guardrails, and adoption model behind both. Built for financial services business and operations leaders, CIOs and IT operations heads, and data and AI leaders, this session gives you a practical path from promising pilots to production at enterprise scale. This presentation is brought to you by Tata Consultancy Services, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond Prompts: Crafting Production GenAI from Scratch
description: Building reliable GenAI applications requires deliberate systems engineering, not just prompt engineering. After collaborating with AWS Professional Services on an enterprise client, I learned how to build production-grade web apps the official AWS way. Bypassing basic buzzwords, we map a compound serverless conversational assistant engineered from scratch using AWS CDK, CloudFront, Cognito, API Gateway, and ⁠Amazon Bedrock. Examine how to handle real-world token streaming failures, manage state in DynamoDB, and implement strict Infrastructure as Code. Leave with complete source code and a concrete approach to balancing model performance against infrastructure cost in highly concurrent production environments.

title: Beyond the Build: Scaling and Governing AI Agents with Dataiku and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Dataiku)
description: As enterprises move from experimenting with AI agents to deploying them at scale, the challenge is no longer just how to build agents, it’s how to maintain visibility, performance, and control across the growing agent ecosystem. This session will explore how Amazon Bedrock and Dataiku Agent Management support the agent lifecycle from creation through enterprise-wide management. Attendees will see how organizations can build and deploy agents with AWS while using Dataiku to discover agents, monitor performance, and identify risk across environments, helping teams scale agentic AI with greater confidence and governance. This presentation is brought to you by Dataiku, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
description: When AI workloads need scale or speed, the instinct is to add more compute, but GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. From training to inference, storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, and accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference workloads. Learn how Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.

title: Beyond the IDE: autonomous development with Kiro web and mobile
description: Kiro web and mobile bring agentic development to your browser—every session in an isolated cloud sandbox, no local setup, accessible anywhere you have an internet connection. In this hands-on workshop, you'll work with Kiro two ways. First, iterate interactively: connect a repo, explore the codebase, and shape changes in real time. Then go hands-off: assign a task from a tracked issue, let Kiro plan and implement autonomously, and review the pull request it opens. Sessions run in the cloud and keep going after you close your laptop—check in and review diffs from your phone with the Kiro iOS app. You must bring your laptop to participate.

In this hands-on workshop, you'll work with Kiro two ways. First, iterate interactively: connect a repo, explore the codebase, and shape changes in real time. Then go hands-off: assign a task from a tracked issue, let Kiro plan and implement autonomously, and review the pull request it opens. Sessions run in the cloud and keep going after you close your laptop—check in and review diffs from your phone with the Kiro iOS app. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Beyond the pilot: How customers scaled Kiro and proved the value
description: Adopting a coding agent is as much an organizational challenge as a technical one. In this panel, engineering leaders from companies that deployed Kiro at scale share what worked: rollout strategies that drove adoption, training approaches that met developers where they were, governance guardrails that satisfied security teams, and the metrics they use to measure productivity impact. Bring your questions—this is an open conversation about the patterns, pitfalls, and payoffs of making AI-assisted development the default across an engineering organization.

title: Boost Performance: Salesforce, Slack and AWS Headless Connectivity (sponsored by Salesforce)
description: Disconnected systems slow teams down. See how Agentforce, Slack and AgentCore Bedrock enable your Headless agentic strategy to unlock seamless collaboration and boost productivity across teams in real time. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

title: Break free from Oracle licensing and modernize to Aurora PostgreSQL
description: Oracle modernization promises freedom from licensing, lock-in, and operational overhead, yet projects stall on PL/SQL packages, schema quirks, and application logic that resists automated translation. In this workshop, you'll migrate a live Oracle workload to open-source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL end-to-end and tackle the hardest schema conversion challenges that derail real-world projects. You'll work through PL/SQL translation, dependency resolution, and validation using AWS agentic AI.

title: Breaking down batch inference with Ray Data on Amazon EKS
description: Batch inference is more than running a model over a large dataset. In this interactive chalk talk, we build an end-to-end batch inference architecture on Amazon EKS one component at a time. We examine when to use Spark with Ray Serve and when Ray Data can unify preprocessing and inference. Along the way, we address data sharding, storage and data movement, GPU scheduling, autoscaling, batch sizing, checkpointing, retries, observability, security, isolation, and cost. Attendees will leave with a practical decision framework and a production architecture for operating reliable, scalable batch inference with Ray Data and the KubeRay Operator.

title: Breathing Life into Game Worlds with Amazon Neptune & GraphRAG
description: Static NPC dialogue can't unlock rich game worlds. This session shares a production pattern using Amazon Neptune, Bedrock GraphRAG, and the "Entity as Agent" approach. We will live-demo natural-language character relationship search, in-character AI dialogue, and in-game party composition recommendations.

title: Bring your S3 data to your compute with S3 Files
description: S3 Files makes the data in your S3 buckets available to your compute as a high-performance file system, so any POSIX-based tool or workload can work with S3 objects in place. We will work through the two ways customers use it: giving established file-based applications direct access to data already in S3, and giving agents and other short-lived compute a durable, isolated file workspace they can leave behind. We'll whiteboard the decisions that matter: connecting compute to S3 Files across VPCs, accounts, and on-prem; tuning for price and performance; and securing access with IAM, POSIX permissions, and encryption.

title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
description: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: British Airways: Agentic AI for Java modernization at 48% lower cost
description: You have hundreds of services stuck on aging infrastructure, and your engineers are spending more time maintaining them than building new experiences. British Airways faced the same challenge with 590 Github repositories and 200 business services on EC2. Using AWS Transform custom, they built an agentic AI platform that autonomously migrates services to ECS Fargate on Graviton, cutting costs by 48% without compromising business logic. They also extended it to improve test coverage and patch security vulnerabilities continuously. In this session, you'll learn how to build a repeatable transformation engine and give your engineers time back.

title: Build a backend before your coffee gets cold with AWS Blocks
description: What if you could stand up a full application backend—database, auth, real-time messaging, file storage, even an AI agent—in TypeScript, running locally, with no AWS account required? AWS Blocks is an open-source framework where each "Block" bundles your app code, a local dev implementation, and production AWS infrastructure. Compose the Blocks you need, run one command to develop locally, then deploy the same code to AWS unchanged. Built for a world where AI agents write the code, Blocks ships steering files that guide agents to correct architecture from the start. In this lightning talk, see how fast full-stack can be.

title: Build a community portal with Connect Customer agentic voice in 60 minutes
description: City governments face rising citizen expectations with shrinking staff. In this builders' session, learn how to deploy a fully functional AI-powered community engagement portal using Amazon Connect Customer agentic voice in under one hour. See how to build a voice agent that answers common citizen inquiries about permits, utilities, parks, and city services, routes callers to the right department, and seamlessly escalates to live agents with full conversation context when needed. Walk away with a production-ready reference architecture that operations team can configure, deploy, and manage independently.

title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU
description: In this hands-on workshop, you build a production-ready multi-agent system that splits workloads between CPU and GPU EC2 instances — the best of both worlds. Starting with an autonomous customer-support pipeline, you deploy reasoning agents on GPU and orchestration, tool-calling, and retrieval agents on CPUs. You profile each stage, measure latency and cost per agent call, and implement routing policies that dynamically assign tasks to the optimal compute tier. By the end, you have a hybrid deployment with a live cost dashboard showing 30–45% savings vs. GPU-only baselines.

title: Build a data-driven migration plan with AWS Transform
description: You're planning a data center exit and need leadership to say yes. That means persuasive data, realistic cost estimates, and a proposal that makes financial sense. In this builders' session, you'll use AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities paired with Discovery Agent data to assess your existing environment, generate cost estimates, and build a compelling business case for migration. You'll work through the end-to-end workflow from discovery and analysis to financial modeling, and leave ready to present a data-driven migration proposal to your stakeholders.

title: Build Agentic AI That Understands Your Business with SAP and AWS (sponsored by SAP)
description: Enterprise AI falls short when agents lack live business context. See how SAP's Business AI Platform and AWS solve this: Joule Studio enables developers and business users to build and deploy custom AI agents grounded in SAP's process knowledge, while bidirectional, zero-copy integration between SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon Athena gives AWS services secure access to trusted SAP data. Watch a live demo of building agents that reason with business context, collaborate across SAP and AWS, and act across enterprise processes with governance. This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.

title: Build agentic fraud detection with a transaction foundation model
description: Organized fraud rings exploit the gaps between siloed detection systems, making them invisible to traditional rules-based approaches. In this workshop, you’ll construct a fraud detection optimization system that tackles them at scale. Load 24M transactions into Apache Iceberg, build a knowledge graph with Amazon Neptune to reveal hidden fraud networks, and train an ensemble combining transaction foundation model embeddings with graph embeddings for measurable score improvement. Then deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that autonomously investigates patterns, expands fraud rings, and creates validated detection rules. Leave with an end-to-end working system you can replicate in your own environment.

title: Build agentic GraphRAG apps with Amazon Neptune
description: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships between concepts, entities, and underlying content. Agentic GraphRAG takes this further, allowing agents to autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use to achieve information goals. In this session, build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit. You will transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools to enable agents to answer multi-faceted questions that require context from multiple distinct knowledge sources to provide a contextually complete answer. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
description: What if your agent's most convincing answer rests on the wrong evidence? Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Aurora PostgreSQL across more than 500,000 product listings in three connected hands-on labs. Debug SQL combining full-text search, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, and pgvector semantic search under shared filters. Repair reciprocal rank fusion, inspect Amazon Bedrock reranking, and compare retrieval settings against judged queries. Then build a Strands agent, connect its retrieval tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, and deploy it to AgentCore Runtime. Trace its searches to cited specifications and reviews, and test what happens when requirements change. Leave with reusable retrieval SQL and working agent code.

title: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
description: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

title: Build Agentic Video Streaming Observability Using Kiro and Bedrock
description: Media operations teams struggle to correlate issues across complex live streaming pipelines. In this hands-on session, build an agentic video observability and analytics application using Kiro and Amazon Bedrock that monitors the entire live streaming chain using AWS Elemental MediaConnect, MediaLive, MediaPackage, MediaTailor and Amazon CloudFront. Deploy AI agents using Strands Agents SDK and MCP servers to ingest, visualize, and investigate end-to-end QoE/QoS analytics across three layers: origin health, CDN performance, and client-side CMCD telemetry. Learn how to create a unified dashboard and natural language interface for streaming quality investigation across every pipeline stage.

title: Build a governed semantic layer with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP
description: Financial services organizations struggle with inconsistent metric definitions, AI hallucination risks, and analyst bottlenecks. In this session, you’ll build a governed semantic layer with three key pillars (accuracy, consistency, and explainability) essential for agents to operate securely at scale. You’ll then connect to AI agents powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that query, interpret, and act on financial data via MCP, enabling natural language access to complex financial metrics. Your agents reason rather than guess, with full auditability for financial regulators. Leave with a production-ready architecture pattern that goes beyond "chat with your data" demos.

title: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
description: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.

title: Build AI agents to operate desktop and mainframe apps on WorkSpaces
description: You rely on desktop and mainframe applications for critical workflows, but these interfaces remain inaccessible to AI agents. Your Robotic Process Automation efforts have struggled to keep pace as applications and configurations constantly change. Amazon WorkSpaces lets AI agents securely operate the same desktop and mainframe applications your employees use, without any application modernization. WorkSpaces supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it works with any agent framework. In this workshop, connect to a pre-provisioned WorkSpace, build a custom agent, run agents that complete desktop workflows, and monitor agent sessions with CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Bring laptop to participate.

title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
description: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.

title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
description: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB)
description: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. No repo setup, no infrastructure work. You'll touch the full stack, generation, database, and deployment, and walk away with a functional prototype. Then we open up the system behind it: planning, safety checks, a durable job queue, containerized workers on Amazon EC2, automated testing, targeted repairs, and deployment. We'll unpack what makes it repeatable, like isolating generated code, keeping credentials at trusted boundaries, and preserving state across restarts with Atlas. A MongoDB Build Lab workshop, with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Build a multi-agent system for hyper-personalized customer journeys
description: Delivering personalized experiences across complex customer journeys requires agents that understand intent, maintain context, and coordinate across systems. In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI personal banker using a home buying scenario as the example. Your agents extract intent from natural conversation, build dynamic customer profiles, and orchestrate workflows across internal banking systems and external ecosystem APIs. Implement multi-agent patterns for shared memory, readiness signals, and coordinated decisioning using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents Framework, and MCP. Walk away with reusable orchestration patterns you can apply to any personalized customer experience.

Build four specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock including a planner, media buyer, analyst, and creative generator that turns campaign parameters into audience targeting, budget allocation, performance forecasts, and localized creative grounded in your brand guidelines and historical data. Activate campaigns through Amazon Ads DSP, then add an optimizer agent with human-in-the-loop approvals that reallocates budget across channels as performance shifts. You'll build a running multi-agent workflow and take away the Bedrock agent definitions to adapt for your own campaigns.

title: Build an agentic AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
description: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that serves every model on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: a fine-tuned intent router and a fine-tuned embedding model for vector search (both ONNX, trained on CPU), a cross-encoder re-ranker for retrieval quality, and a quantized generative analyst served with llama.cpp and grounded by RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock generates the synthetic training data, judges every answer through a faithfulness gate, and answers the edge cases the small models cannot. You'll finish by running the control test that puts a frontier LLM in the same seat, so you know whether the small model is good enough on your workload. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
description: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.

True transformation happens when autonomous AI operates across systems using trusted data, flexible models, connected applications, and a unified, agentic control plane. By bringing knowledge workers and technical builders into a shared agentic environment, teams move faster without sacrificing governance. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud unifies enterprise context, model choice, and app connections into a single architecture. Discover how to turn enterprise data into reliable, autonomous action and long-term competitive advantage in your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

title: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
description: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.

description: Education institutions field thousands of student inquiries each semester across enrollment, financial aid, and academic support. You’ll configure a knowledge base with university content and connect it to Connect Customer for real-time AI-generated recommendations during live calls, then deploy a self-service experience that resolves common inquiries over voice and chat. title: Build an AI Student Advisor: Agents for Education
description: Universities lose students to inadequate academic advising often because a single advisor carries unsustainable caseloads and response times stretch to days. In this chalk talk, we explore the architecture of an AI student advising agent built with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands, connected to student record systems via MCP, with guardrails for sensitive student welfare queries, and embedded in an existing LMS through Amazon Quick. We'll whiteboard real-world advising scenarios (Course selection and degree planning) and discuss when the agent should hand off to a human advisor and how to design that escalation path.

title: Build an AI testing safety net before you modernize
description: Modernizing applications is risky without comprehensive test coverage, and most apps that need modernization don't have it. In this workshop, you'll build an AI-powered testing safety net before touching a line of production code. Starting with a deployed insurance application, you'll use Kiro to generate spec-driven tests from source code and Nova Act to discover UI tests through autonomous exploration. Then you'll apply AWS Transform to modernize the codebase and re-run your AI-generated test suite to prove functional equivalence. You'll leave knowing how to de-risk modernization by letting GenAI build your safety net first. Laptop required.

title: Build and Deploy an eve Agent with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
description: Build and deploy a personalized eve agent with Vercel and AWS in this hands-on innovation lab. You'll start from zero, scaffold an open-source eve.dev agent framework, configure it with your own instructions, connect it to Amazon Bedrock through Vercel Al Gateway, and deploy it to Vercel. The lab is designed for a range of builders: beginners and non-technical users can quickly build and launch a functional agent, while more advanced engineers can explore how the same agent architecture can connect to AWS services and enterprise data sources such as Aurora, S3, or DynamoDB using Vercel and AWS native integration and advanced Vercel networking. Along the way, you'll learn how Vercel and AWS work together to help teams move from Al prototype to production-ready application. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: Build an intelligent contact center with Zendesk and AWS (sponsored by Zendesk)
description: Contact center teams need to resolve issues consistently across channels while giving agents the information and tools to act. In this session, discover how Zendesk and AWS work together to create a native contact center experience within Zendesk that connects customer interactions, workflows, and systems in one connected environment. Learn how AI can enhance voice support by handling routine needs, guiding conversations, and helping customers reach resolution faster. See how human handoffs preserve the customer’s history, needs, and progress, giving agents the context they need to step in seamlessly, personalize the experience, and move each interaction toward resolution. This presentation is brought to you by Zendesk, an AWS Partner.

title: Build a payment-enabled agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments
description: AI agents that can autonomously transact open new possibilities in financial services—from purchasing market data to paying for risk scores in real time. In this builders' session, you'll configure an AI agent using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments with the open source x402 protocol. You'll set up payment managers, connect to data providers, define budget controls with IAM policies, and monitor transactions with Amazon CloudWatch. Leave with a working agent that autonomously transacts, reasons about costs, and delivers results end to end.

title: Build a per-tenant observability stack for Agentic SaaS
description: Multi-tenant ISVs need per-tenant observability that traditional dashboards can't deliver — aggregated metrics hide the tenant causing the problem, and shared traces don't tell you whose agent misbehaved. In this session, build a per-tenant observability stack for agents. You'll instrument agent invocations with tenant-aware traces and session replay, build tenant-scoped dashboards that surface noisy neighbors and latency outliers, and configure alerting that fires on per-tenant thresholds rather than aggregate signals. By the end, you'll have an observability setup that scales with your tenant count without a separate data pipeline — and patterns to extend it as your agent architecture grows.

title: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
description: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint - all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.
