title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
description: Teams deploying AI agents inherit two exposures. Any client reaching the endpoint can invoke the agent, and it can reach any destination its tools name. In this builders' session, learn to close both gaps with AWS managed controls. Put AWS WAF Bot Control in front of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to classify callers and admit only the classes you choose, then route the agent through AWS Network Firewall and use domain category filtering to decide which destination categories it may reach. Run each control in count or alert mode, then enforce it and verify the allowed and the refused path. Leave with a two-boundary pattern you can apply to your own agent deployments.

title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
description: AI agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore accept untrusted input and make outbound API calls, creating both ingress and egress attack surfaces. In this session, learn how to defend both paths using AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall. See how WAF authenticates callers, enforces rate limits, and blocks prompt-injection payloads before they reach your agent, while Network Firewall applies managed threat-intelligence categories to drop egress traffic to malicious destinations without maintaining custom deny lists. Walk away with a deployable defense-in-depth boundary pattern for your agentic AI workloads.

title: Build a team shared agent workflow from issue to tested PR
description: How do you let agents carry development work across teammates without handing over control? In this code talk, build an issue-to-review workflow that you can share with your team. Follow the code and configuration for setting up guardrails, permissions, shared workflows, logging, and best practices, so teammates can steer the implementation or review who requested or approved each action alongside the evidence the agent produced. Bring questions and follow along as we explain why each boundary exists and how to adapt the pattern to your toolchain and approval process.

title: Build a unified student insight platform on Amazon Quick
description: From advisors triaging at-risk students to deans auditing course difficulty to executives tracking retention trends, every role in a university needs student-success insights, but today they use disconnected tools. In this session, learn how Amazon Quick connects to your institutional data and delivers explainable, persona-aware insights through one unified architecture. Chat Agents explain early-warning signals with cited data, automated Flows trigger interventions, and Stories generate executive-ready narratives. Explore the architecture and take away patterns for explainable, natural-language analytics on AWS.

title: Build Autonomous Agents and Run AI-Powered AppSec on Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
description: Go hands-on with OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock across two builder tracks. First, stand up a fully managed autonomous agent with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents: define instructions and tools, wire action groups for API access, and ground responses in your own data through knowledge bases. Then shift to code security, using OpenAI's Codex Security to review a real vulnerable app by running scans, threat modeling, triaging findings, and fixing one with verified remediation. Throughout, inference runs securely on Bedrock under your account's controls. You'll leave with repeatable blueprints for building agentic OpenAI applications and for AI-assisted application security on AWS. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Build a Video Semantic Layer for Media Agent and Agent Harness on AWS
description: This workshop tackles a question most media organizations have yet to ask: your video pipeline extracts rich metadata for human search and discovery, but is it actually optimized for agents? In this hands-on session, you will build the semantic infrastructure that bridges that gap: multimodal embeddings tuned for machine recall, hybrid search that combines vector similarity with keyword precision, and an entity graph that maps content relationships into structures agents can reason over. By the end of this workshop, you will have a media agent harness that queries, enriches, and continuously improves their video understanding, making video content not just searchable by people but optimized at scale for agents.

title: Build better, review faster: AI-Powered Well-Architected reviews
description: Periodic reviews can't keep pace with infrastructure that changes daily. In this hands-on workshop, deploy an AI-powered agent for continuous, goal-driven architecture reviews across a multi-account environment. Configure agent profiles, cross-account role chaining, and business goals that prioritize across Cost Optimization, Security, Resilience, and Performance pillars. See how the agent enriches Trusted Advisor, Compute Optimizer, and Resilience Hub signals with cross-pillar trade-off analysis. Run pre-deployment reviews against CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform, then remediate through AI-generated SOPs. Wire recommendations into CI/CD via API. For architects, platform engineers, and operations leads who want always-on architectural governance in their delivery lifecycle.

title: Build Bidstream Agents and Simulate Auction with AgentCore
description: In this hands-on workshop, build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream, using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. You'll construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions to the ARTF specification, then orchestrate a multi-agent pipeline that simulates adversarial auction scenarios and scores your bidding strategy against the outcomes. Run interactive simulations that generate learning signals, and plug in your own bidding model to see how it performs. You'll leave with a working ARTF container and auction-simulation harness you can point at your own models.

title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
description: Every organisation's modernization journey is unique — we whiteboard how to build, deploy, and share custom transformation agents using the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit — from orchestrator architectures and MCP patterns to one-command Bedrock AgentCore deployment. Bring your challenges.

title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
description: Partners spent years building their modernization tooling. AWS Transform now meets them where they are, ATX agents exposed via MCP, callable from any partner-native orchestrator. We'll cover the integration pattern, agent-card model, and field-tested wins from GSI and ISV partners already in production.

title: Build durable AI agents with AgentCore and Temporal (sponsored by Temporal)
description: An AI agent completes five steps, waits for approval, and then its runtime is replaced. How does it recover without repeating costly tool calls or losing the business process? In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and Temporal combine AWS-native agent infrastructure with durable execution. We’ll build a production agent that preserves progress across failures, coordinates tools, agents, and people, and safely evolves while work is still running. You'll see how Temporal natively supports serverless compute infrastructure, complementing AgentCore Runtime with durable execution, preserving workflow progress across failures, approvals, runtime changes, and scale to zero, without pushing recovery and coordination logic into application code. This presentation is brought to you by Temporal, an AWS Partner.

title: Build eval-driven skills for Aurora PostgreSQL operations
description: Turn Aurora PostgreSQL runbooks into agent skills and test whether they improve an agent's advice. Work through three incidents on a live cluster: RDS Proxy session pinning that starves checkout connections, a payout job whose open transaction blocks checkouts, and stalled order delivery alongside a long-running transaction that holds back vacuum cleanup. Complete and refine skills that cover pre-flight checks, execution, validation and rollback. Freeze a grading rubric, then compare the same agent, hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, without and with your skill. Write Python recovery checks that reject incomplete fixes, perform the repairs yourself, and verify customer recovery using independent database and business records.

title: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
description: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build full-stack observability for agents and apps
description: When your applications include AI agents that reason, plan, and act autonomously, observability has to evolve too. Disconnected tools and siloed signals slow teams down right when speed matters most. In this chalk talk, we walk through real scenarios and trace an agent's chain of thought across services, correlating agent failures with infrastructure, and using natural-language investigation to cut resolution time. We diagram how service discovery, dependency mapping, evaluations, and IDE-native telemetry come together so you can ship agents with confidence.

title: Build GenAI-Powered Workflows with AWS Serverless and AWS AI Services
description: In this builders' session, design and deploy a workflow that chains AI service calls—document analysis, content generation, and decision routing—using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for checkpoint and recovery. Working in small groups, you'll implement error handling, human approval gates, and cost controls for AI-powered pipelines. Walk away with reusable patterns for production-ready GenAI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
description: Build an agentic retail assistant that answers from business facts under explicit controls. Across four connected labs, combine Aurora PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector with reciprocal rank fusion and Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock. Connect search and inventory tools to specialists built with the Strands Agents SDK, then deploy them to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Runtime, Memory, Gateway, and Policy. Protect customer records with identity binding and PostgreSQL row-level security, and enforce Cedar policies on Gateway tool calls. Approve a store credit, query the audit records, and verify denied calls don't execute and retries don't duplicate credits. Patterns are reusable across Aurora and RDS for PostgreSQL.

title: Build governed remediation workflows for Aurora database operations
description: AI-powered database intelligence can surface recommendations for slow queries, vacuum issues, index changes, and parameter tuning, but acting on those recommendations safely in production requires governance. In this session, build a governed recommendation-to-remediation workflow for Aurora PostgreSQL. Starting with a performance troubleshooting recommendation, learn to classify operational risk, validate the proposed change, apply policy-based approval gates, execute with scoped permissions, and capture an auditable trail from insight to action. Explore custom security controls, blast-radius reduction, human-in-the-loop governance, rollback planning, post-change verification across development, staging, and production environments, and integration with signals from your own agents. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build, Guard, Route: Trustworthy, Cost-Aware AI Agents with the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
description: Bring a laptop and build a governed multi-agent system on AWS, end to end. In this hands-on workshop you'll wire Strands SDK agents to inference on Amazon Bedrock and NVIDIA NIM-on-AWS, sandbox tool execution with OpenShell (Landlock, seccomp, eBPF, cgroups), and install signed skills, connectors, and runbooks from an open, versioned registry that federates with AWS AgentCore. You'll watch a five-layer enforcement spine crystallize in a run-DAG where every prompt, model call, tool call, and delegation becomes a visible, proven step. Then you'll graduate the same governance from laptop to AWS unchanged, with SPIFFE/SPIRE attesting which instance ran each step. You'll leave with a working reference deployment in your own AWS account and reusable patterns you can adapt to real agents. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Building a Cost Governance framework for AI that scales
description: AI spend starts with model tokens but often misses costs from agent runtimes, memory, data, and supporting services. In this chalk talk, we'll map an AI workload from architecture to bill, then apply a practical framework to measure, attribute, optimize, and govern its cost and value. Using AWS FinOps Agent as an example, we'll examine how its architecture creates costs across Amazon Bedrock and supporting services, and how to govern those costs. Bring your AI cost challenge and leave with a model that helps FinOps and engineering teams assign ownership, find waste, and set effective controls.

title: Building Advanced Agentic AI Systems on AWS
description: Multi-agent systems unlock powerful workflows, but production demands more than chaining agents together. This bootcamp covers advanced patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement agent-as-tool communication, share memory across agents, optimize context windows for cost and performance, and secure deployments with policy-based access control and VPC integration. Configure distributed tracing, build evaluation frameworks, and design deployment strategies that take your agentic systems from prototype to production-ready state.

title: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
description: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge for inter-agent communication. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
description: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge for inter-agent communication. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
description: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

title: Building a governed AI ready data foundation on AWS (sponsored by Fivetran)
description: Most data stacks were built for dashboards, not AI. Duplicated pipelines, competing definitions, and slow reporting make it difficult to deliver the fresh, trusted, governed data AI demands. Learn how a fast growing organization replaced engineering heavy operations with a self serve model built on AWS, Fivetran, and dbt. Understand how to standardize ingestion, apply governed transformations and semantic definitions, and cut pipeline development from months to days. You'll walk away with a practical approach to freeing engineering time, providing business teams with trusted access to data, and building a governed foundation that scales AI from experiments to production. This presentation is brought to you by Fivetran, an AWS Partner.

title: Building AI Agents with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
description: This session explores how Vercel and AWS work together to support the development and deployment of AI agents. You’ll learn about first party connectivity to AWS databases and services through the Vercel Marketplace, along with the backend capabilities agents need, including APIs, durable workflows, queues, cron jobs, and MCP servers. You’ll see how these building blocks, together with the EVE framework, can simplify agent development, followed by a live demo showing how to build an agent using Vercel and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: Building an AI Travel Assistant with AgentCore Gateway
description: Your agent handles conversations well, but to search for flights or check weather it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this SimuLearn session, you create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and register Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tool targets. You then deploy a travel planning agent using the Strands Agents SDK that connects to the Gateway, sequentially invokes flight search and weather tools, and synthesizes results into a trip recommendation through one secure MCP endpoint.

title: Building and scaling inference workloads on Amazon EKS
description: Kubernetes has become the platform of choice for production gen AI inference at scale. This builders' session covers deploying and scaling large language models on Amazon EKS with NVIDIA GPUs - from cluster setup optimized for GPU workloads to efficient model serving with vLLM, distributed inference with Ray, and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Real-world patterns address cost optimization and enterprise-grade reliability for teams moving beyond experimentation. Attendees leave with hands-on experience and best practices for running production-grade gen AI infrastructure on Kubernetes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
description: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.

title: Building a Zero Trust for Agentic AI Practice: A Partner Framework
description: AI agents create identity, authorization, governance, and tenant-isolation challenges that map directly to partner revenue streams. In this builders' session, you'll work hands-on with the Zero Trust Agent Maturity (ZAM) Framework and configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Gateway to enforce verifiable agent identities, auditable interaction chains, and centralized policy authorization that scopes every agent action to its tenant boundary. You'll run a live ZAM assessment on a sample multi-tenant deployment, revealing security gaps that become partner opportunities: red-teaming engagements, MCP security proxies, multi-tenant isolation reviews, and compliance automation. Leave with a repeatable assessment methodology to secure multi-tenant agent deployments.

title: Building better quantum computers with digital twins
description: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. To design better error-correction strategies, simulating how real quantum hardware operates is essential, yet computationally intractable. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

title: Building Context-Aware Agents with AgentCore Memory
description: Customers expect personalized service and context retention without repeating themselves every session. In this lab, you build a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that remembers each client across conversations. You create a Memory resource with Semantic, Summary, and User Preference strategies, deploy a Lambda-based agent backed by Amazon Nova Lite, and seed multi-turn conversations. The agent retrieves preferences and facts from long-term memory to personalize responses and recommend products from a DynamoDB catalog.

title: Building Cross-Enterprise AI Agents with MCP and A2A on AWS
description: Enterprises run hundreds of applications from ERP, CRM, supply chain, and beyond and yet orchestrating intelligent actions across these systems remains a challenge. In this chalk talk, learn how to architect and manage cross-enterprise agentic orchestration using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enable AI agents to seamlessly interact across application boundaries through a single, unified chat interface. Walk away with practical architecture patterns for connecting SAP and adjacent enterprise systems like SalesForce, ServicesNow etc into a cohesive, AI-powered automation layer

title: Building eval-driven observability for AI agents
description: Multi-agent systems fail in ways your dashboards cannot show: one agent hands off bad context, another retries, and the API still returns 200. In this live coding session, start with a multi-agent app on LangGraph, Strands, and CrewAI, and instrument it with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference. Trace it from the first prototype run, evaluate agents on demand with LLM-as-judge evaluators, A/B test prompt and model variants before promoting to production, pull production traces into a versioned dataset, reproduce the failure locally, and ship the fix. All from your IDE, without switching tools.

title: Building event-driven, multi-agent swarms on serverless
description: Multi-agent AI systems need communication that is decoupled, observable, and scalable. In this chalk talk, we show how to coordinate swarms of independent agents through event choreography on Amazon EventBridge. Each agent reacts to events and emits new ones rather than being told what to do by a central controller. We discuss how to handle multi-agent failure modes like cascading hallucinations and runaway event loops (circular delegation), and how to prevent independent agents from taking conflicting actions.

title: Building for Always-On: Resilient Trading to Agentic AI on Modern Data Foundation (sponsored by Cognizant)
description: Learn how LPL Financial built an always-on trading platform on AWS that supports 32,000+ financial advisors with resilient, multi-region architecture for mission-critical, latency-sensitive workloads. Discover how a unified data foundation across trading, brokerage, and custodial systems creates a trusted layer for innovation, and learn the realities of deploying agentic AI in a regulated broker-dealer environment. Gain practical insights into architecture patterns, governance, real-time data access, key tradeoffs, and lessons learned that can help accelerate your own modernization and AI initiatives. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.

title: Building multi-tenant RAG: Isolation, cost, and scale
description: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.

title: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
description: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Building optimized enterprise HPC systems for CAE and CFD
description: High-fidelity Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations require significant compute infrastructure. We’ll discuss how organizations are migrating CAE and CFD workloads from on premises to AWS, combining scalable HPC infrastructure with cloud-native engineering applications to accelerate product development. Learn how to architect your enterprise HPC system to optimize cost, queue wait times, and throughput with Amazon EC2 HPC-optimized instances, Savings Plans, and Amazon FSx.

title: Building production-ready agents securely: lessons from AWS at scale
description: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.

title: Building Proprietary Multi-Agentic AI Workflows for Low Latency and High Reliability (sponsored by Capital One)
description: Enterprise AI requires scalable, multi-agentic workflows capable of handling complex reasoning without sacrificing real-time speed. This session explores how Capital One designs proprietary multi-agent systems on AWS, optimized for governance, performance, and reliability. You’ll hear how state-of-the-art serving frameworks like vLLM, efficient distributed serving platforms like llm-d, and advanced agentic inference optimization techniques can enhance latency and boost throughput. We’ll showcase these principles through real-world applications, including complex real employee- and customer-facing banking use cases while meeting rigorous business standards around accuracy, reliability, and risk management. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

title: Building searchable live sports with AWS Elemental and Amazon CloudFront
description: Live sports fans no longer watch one feed and wait for the recap. They expect every angle live and every key play instantly findable. In this session, see how you turn live sports into searchable fan moments on AWS. Using AWS Elemental inference, the platform generates highlight clips in real time and pairs them with conversational AI powered by Amazon Bedrock, so fans can ask for "the catch in the third quarter" and get it in seconds instead of hours. Then go deeper into the delivery workflow: composing multi-view experiences so viewers follow simultaneous matches and camera angles, enriching clips with AI-generated titles and captions, and delivering live feeds and clips globally through a single Amazon CloudFront architecture.

title: Building Serverless AI agents
description: AI agents need more than an LLM and a prompt. Production agents require tool execution with least-privilege isolation, orchestration that recovers from partial failures, and observability that tracks token spend alongside function duration. In this chalk talk, we discuss architectural patterns for Serverless AI agents: model routing across providers and cost tiers, fault-tolerant orchestration with Step Functions and Lambda durable functions, isolated code execution using MicroVMs, and state management for long-running multi-step workflows. We whiteboard the decisions that matter for your workload shape and where each pattern introduces complexity you may not need.

title: Building Serverless applications at AI speed
description: Manually wiring up Lambda functions, API Gateway routes, and IaC templates for every new service is repetitive work that AI handles well. In this builders' session, use Kiro to go from natural language specifications to a deployed serverless application. You'll configure MCP tool servers to give the AI agent access to AWS APIs, author steering documents that produce consistent output, and iterate on generated infrastructure until it passes validation. Walk away with techniques for getting reliable, production-ready code from AI-assisted workflows. Bring your laptop.

title: Building stateful AI workflows with Serverless orchestration
description: AI workflows need state such as conversation history, intermediate results, and human approvals, but managing it shouldn't require a database and custom recovery logic. In this builders' session, build a stateful AI workflow that checkpoints progress, recovers from failures automatically, and pauses for external callbacks. Working hands-on with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-step reasoning chains with retry semantics, compare orchestration approaches for different workflow shapes, and deploy a working agent pipeline. Walk away with patterns for choosing the right orchestration tool for your workload. Bring your laptop.

title: Building the Construction Cloud: How Procore AI &Amazon Bedrock Power the Built World (sponsored by Procore)
description: Construction generates massive volumes of structured and unstructured data, such as drawings, RFIs, and safety reports, that most AI infrastructure isn't built to handle. In this session, we'll break down how Amazon Bedrock's model access, guardrails, and enterprise controls power Procore AI, and why that combination is what makes construction-specific AI viable at enterprise scale. You'll leave with a clear picture of the architecture, and why we think this is the first real blueprint for AI in the built environment. This presentation is brought to you by Procore, an AWS Partner.

title: Building the data architecture that survives agentic analytics (sponsored by Edelbyte)
description: Human queries are bounded, repeatable, and predictable, so techniques like caching, sampling, and precomputation keep them fast and affordable. AI agents are none of those. One prompt becomes dozens of novel, complex queries at machine speed, so caching an agent's curiosity is nearly impossible. At a leading automotive R&D group, 1,400 engineers and their agents query 200 petabytes of vehicle telemetry, with 600 terabytes ingested daily, to engineer higher-quality, more reliable vehicles and reach production faster. This session shows the AWS architecture behind it and how it delivers real-time analytics with full retention at the scale agents have made standard. This presentation is brought to you by Edelbyte, an AWS Partner.

title: Building the Intelligent Health System, CXO blueprint for the agentic era (sponsored by PwC)
description: The health systems that will lead the next decade are not simply digitizing existing processes. They are reimagining what a health system looks like with AI native to every layer. On AWS that means a unified data foundation across electornic health records, claims, images, devices, and genomics; real-time AI at the point of decision; agentic workflows that absorb entire categories of administrative burden; and governance that holds up to audit at scale. Chief Information, Digital, and AI Officers building this now share what worked and what they would do differently. Attendees leave with a practical sequence, from data foundation to agentic deployment. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
description: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

title: Building Trust into Agentic AI on AWS in the Age of Autonomous Agents (sponsored by Check Point)
description: AI agents are evolving from assistants into autonomous systems that call APIs and take actions on behalf of users. Traditional perimeter controls aren't enough; threats now emerge from prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unmonitored tool use. In this session, we'll show how Check Point's AI security intelligence integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to enforce real-time guardrails at the agent runtime layer inspecting intent, validating actions, and preventing policy violations before they execute. Walk away with a practical framework for securing agentic AI on AWS with Check Point. This presentation is brought to you by Check Point, an AWS Partner.

title: Building Wealth Advisor Agents with Full Stack Architecture
description: In this SimuLearn session, you leverage the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore platform ito build production-grade wealth management advisor. You create Memory resources for client personalization, configure a Gateway with MCP tool targets for account and market data, deploy specialist agents and a supervisor to Runtime, and authenticate users through Cognito. The result is a multi-agent advisor that recognizes each client, remembers their goals, and produces auditable financial guidance through governed tools.

title: Building Your AI Practice: From Business Model to Partner Revenue
description: Enterprises expect agentic outcomes. That changes how solutions are built and deployed. Traditional delivery practices are evolving to agentic delivery, outcome-based models, and scalable IP transacted through AWS Marketplace. Partners moving first are delivering measurable business outcomes faster and building new revenue alongside their customers. In this session, learn the three-stage practice-building path. See how Forward Deployed Engineering gives partners a new engagement architecture and faster delivery: pod-based, and time-boxed. See where AWS co-investment programs and AI-specific enrollment paths de-risk each stage of practice growth. Walk away with example GTM models and a concrete action plan.

title: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
description: Learn how Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed - not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one - including Amazon - can access unencrypted data. We'll dive into NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs for auditability, mutual TLS with embedded attestation proofs, and key lifecycle management within encrypted VM memory. A practical blueprint for building zero-trust AI on Amazon EC2.

title: Build It, Govern It, Ship It: A Hands-On Multi-Agent System with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
description: Building an AI agent is easy. Building one you can trust, safe, affordable, and contained, is the hard part. In this session we build a working agent end to end on AWS using the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit: Nemotron reasoning models served as NIM microservices on AWS GPUs, NeMo Guardrails screening every prompt and response at the inference boundary, NeMo Switchyard routing easy requests to smaller models and hard ones to larger models to cut inference cost, and OpenShell sandboxing tool execution at the kernel with Landlock, seccomp, and eBPF. You will see each layer added live, then watch a side-by-side cost and latency comparison of routed versus un-routed traffic. Everything runs on open foundations, on Amazon Bedrock and NIM-on-AWS. Leave knowing how to assemble safe, cost-aware agents from open components you can adopt one piece at a time. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
description: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.

title: Build mission-ready software in regulated industries faster with Kiro
description: Federal dev teams struggle to ship fast while meeting compliance requirements. In this workshop, build a real app using Kiro's agentic IDE. Automate testing and docs with hooks, enforce AI behavior with steering rules, and extend capabilities through powers. Ideal for federal devs and architects.

title: Build multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence for automotive
description: Warranty and repair workflows span claim history, technical service bulletins, supplier quality records, and regulatory thresholds — a high-cost, fragmented data challenge for automotive OEMs. In this builders session, construct a multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence system using Strands SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build a triage agent that classifies incoming cases, a research agent that queries Bedrock Knowledge Bases across TSBs and repair records, and a resolution agent that synthesizes findings into a structured decision with cited evidence routed for technician approval via human-in-the-loop controls.

title: Build multi-agent workflows with Strands Agents SDK on AWS
description: In this hands-on workshop, build a multi-agent system using the Strands Agents open source SDK. You will create specialized agents with distinct roles, connect them via MCP for tool access, implement agent-to-agent delegation patterns, and add memory for stateful conversations. Deploy and test your multi-agent workflow end-to-end. Walk away with working code and reusable patterns for orchestrating collaborative AI agents using open source tooling.

title: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
description: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training from data preparation through distributed configuration to model test practices with interactive chat — showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. Walk away ready to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.

title: Build Once, Deploy Anywhere: Agentic AI from Data Center to Edge with Qualcomm & AWS (sponsored by Qualcomm)
description: AI is moving beyond the cloud, requiring developers to deploy intelligent workloads across data centers, edge infrastructure, vehicles, industrial systems, PCs, and mobile devices. The challenge is scaling AI efficiently across diverse hardware environments. In this session, learn how Qualcomm and AWS enable developers to build agentic AI applications across the compute continuum, from cloud training to real-time edge and on-device inference. Discover how open frameworks, portable AI runtimes, and streamlined workflows accelerate development and deployment. Through examples spanning automotive, IoT, industrial edge, mobile, datacenter, and cloud use cases, explore how a unified developer experience reduces complexity, increases flexibility, and helps deliver scalable AI applications anywhere. This presentation is brought to you by Qualcomm, an AWS Partner.

title: Build on top of large codebases without breaking your code
description: Your AI agent writes code fast, but when you unleash it on a large codebase, context can fill up quickly and the agent can make questionable implementation choices. Learn how Kiro uses neurosymbolic techniques to understand what you want to build, removing ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. Then, learn simple practices you can use to keep your agent implementation surgical, and detect drift before it spreads all over your codebase.

title: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
description: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end to end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands on workshop, use GenAI Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations, cutting model deployment time to days instead of weeks, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results. Then, configure capacity aware instance pools with priority based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI compatible APIs. You keep the working notebooks to reuse on your own endpoints.

description: Every product team wants an embedded AI assistant—but closed APIs erode margins and limit customization. In this Chalk Talk, we architect a production-ready solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. Walk away understanding how Native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium let you own your AI stack and scale.

title: Build Production Grade Agents with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
description: Learn how to ship agents for your applications with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents, powered by OpenAI, and accelerate development with Codex agents. Explore architecture patterns for reliable, governable workflows across enterprise systems, covering tool use, evaluations, observability, identity, and permissions. See how to keep agent behavior measurable, access secure, and actions aligned with organizational policies. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Build provable AI agents with Automated Reasoning checks
description: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.

description: Learn how to create applications that use real-time data to keep users engaged. In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build Reliable AI Agents on AWS with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
description: When your data changes frequently, RAG helps your agent access the latest information at query time. Fine-tuning an LLM with domain data brings precision in how the agent responds and executes. In this hands-on lab, build reliable AI agents by fine-tuning an LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, and connect it to Amazon Bedrock RAG to ground responses in your latest policies and customer data.

title: Build resilient apps on AWS: AI-driven resilience at any scale
description: Most teams discover resilience gaps during outages, not before. In this interactive chalk talk, you'll use the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub to map user journeys, define recovery objectives, discover dependencies, and run AI-powered failure mode assessments. You'll implement high availability improvements, deploy multi-region disaster recovery, and run the right automated disaster recovery tests that fit your architecture and use case. Walk away with a repeatable framework you can plug into your own environment next week.

title: Build, run, and improve: inside a production AI inference platform (sponsored by Baseten)
description: Getting a model to work is the easy part. Keeping it fast, cheap, and reliable in production is the hard part. Sai Maddali, Product Manager at Baseten, walks through the platform behind some of the highest-volume inference workloads running today: how GPU capacity is sourced and managed across clouds, how runtimes are tuned per workload, and how dedicated inference, model APIs, and training sit on one pool of compute. He shows why the teams pulling ahead treat build, run, and improve as a single loop, and what that changes about latency, cost, and model quality. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

title: Build Secure AI Agents on AWS: XAA, Bedrock AgentCore and the AI Blueprint (sponsored by Okta)
description: Building AI agents is easy, but securing enterprise data access without slowing development is hard. Teams often rely on static, over-privileged credentials, creating major security risks. But there’s a solution. This session explores how to secure agentic workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Okta. We’ll introduce the Blueprint Alliance, of which AWS and Okta are founding members, and cover how standards like Cross App Access (XAA) and SCIM for Agents transform AI identity. You'll learn how replacing static keys with dynamic, delegated permissions enables real-time policy evaluation at every tool call, empowering developers to build scalable, trusted AI agents that operate strictly within verified boundaries. This presentation is brought to you by Okta, an AWS Partner.

title: Build self-healing agents from diagnosis to disaster recovery
description: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

description: Production incidents at 2 a.m. don't wait for your team to wake up. In this builders' session, work with a deployed serverless application and use AWS DevOps Agent to resolve real-world failures autonomously. You'll inject common production issues—such as Lambda throttling, timeout cascades, DynamoDB throughput exceeded, and SQS dead-letter queue buildup—then configure the agent to perform root cause analysis, propose remediation, and apply fixes. You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.

title: Build, simulate, and validate physical AI-driven robotic systems
description: Commissioning industrial robots typically takes weeks of physical testing. Digital twins with real-time physics simulation and multi-agent AI optimization can compress that timeline from weeks to hours. In this builders session, construct a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell using virtual PLCs and controllers, real fieldbus connectivity, real-time physics simulation in NVIDIA Omniverse, and Amazon EC2 as the compute backbone. Leave with an AI-optimized robotic program validated against real-world conditions before ever touching real hardware. Generated in 60 minutes using open standards and open toolchains, the result is a reusable blueprint that scales across cells, lines, and sites.

Get hands-on experience building wallet infrastructure and executing USDC stablecoin operations end-to-end. Walk away with a working architecture that bridges traditional key management with the emerging agentic commerce paradigm.

title: Build the Agentic Workplace: What's New on the Slack Developer Platform (sponsored by Salesforce)
description: Slack is becoming a multiplayer work operating system, where humans and AI agents build together, not just chat. This session shows AWS developers how to ship on the modern Slack Platform: Code Channels, a new space where agents like Claude Code, Devin, and Cursor collaborate with teams in real time; the Slack Agent Kit for building first-class agents; deep bidirectional MCP support, including the Slackbot MCP Client; Real-Time Search (RTS) for grounding agents in live workspace context; and Block Kit for rich, interactive UI. Leave with a clear path to build your first agentic app on Slack. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
description: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

title: Build the Right Next Thing: A Forward Deployed Approach to AI ROI (sponsored by Slalom)
description: Two years ago, standing up generative AI technology was the hard part. Today, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore make the path to production more straightforward—but technology alone does not create value. AI initiatives often stall because ROI is undefined and business, user, and technical priorities are disconnected. Learn how Slalom’s Forward Deployed Expertise (FDX) model places a cross-functional team spanning product, business, industry, UX, and technology alongside customers. Using real data, these teams compare opportunities, prioritize the highest-value use cases, and co-build the right next thing through production, adoption, and measurable outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Slalom, an AWS Partner.

title: Build Trust in AI with Agent Observability (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
description: AI agents behave (and fail) in unpredictable and nuanced ways that erode customer trust before engineering teams know anything is wrong. Teams want to deploy agents into critical business workflows, but it's hard to know if agents are behaving as intended or returning wrong answers.In this talk, you’ll learn how to observe the entire AI stack, optimize tokenomics, and see a demo on how to evaluate and control agent behavior with guardrails to stop harmful or inaccurate outputs. All of this can be done in near real- time and at low cost. This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Build Your Agentic Transformation Roadmap with AWS Transform
description: You want to adopt agentic AI, but with hundreds of applications at different maturity levels, knowing where to start is the real challenge. In this chalk talk, we'll work through a practical framework for turning AWS Transform's automated agentic readiness and modernization analyses into a phased transformation plan. You'll see how to interpret portfolio-level scores, prioritize applications by business value and technical debt, sequence work into actionable phases, and connect readiness gaps to concrete next steps. Bring your portfolio challenges — you'll leave with a prioritization approach you can apply immediately

title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
description: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

title: Build Your Defense Factory for Continuous Defense with OpenAI (sponsored by OpenAI)
description: Put agents to work discovering vulnerabilities and driving fixes autonomously with OpenAI and AWS. Learn how to implement continuous defense with OpenAI tooling, Daybreak cyber models, and AWS infrastructure including Amazon Bedrock, drawing on lessons from OpenAI's internal Defense Factory. Explore routing findings to the right owners, reducing duplicate findings, and using development environments to validate vulnerabilities and test fixes. As broadly available cyber models help threat actors find decade-old vulnerabilities, this session focuses on how defenders can put continuous defense into practice. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Build your iOS CI/CD pipeline with AI agents on EC2 Mac
description: Build iOS CI/CD pipelines on Amazon EC2 Mac using AI-powered workflows with Kiro CLI and AWS MCP Server. Define infrastructure as declarative specs while AI agents guide deployment, explain concepts, and validate configurations. This hands-on workshop covers EC2 Mac architecture, dedicated hosts, Xcode automation, GitLab setup, and CloudWatch monitoring through interactive AI modules. Learn to collaborate with agents and balance automation with understanding. Gain practical experience in both EC2 Mac operations and modern spec-driven, AI-assisted development workflows for Apple platforms.

title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
description: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal)
description: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
description: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
description: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

title: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
description: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in routing to send requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, caching to reduce token counts, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.

title: Change. Wait. Debug. Let AI drive the infrastructure loop. (sponsored by HashiCorp)
description: Make a change. Deploy it. Wait. Dig through the logs. Try again. For years, that loop has cost infrastructure engineers countless hours—time that could be spent shipping what comes next. In this session, discover how to take engineers out of the routine operational loop without giving up oversight. Define the outcome, let AI work through the iterations, and step back in only when a real decision needs you. See the pattern in action with Terraform, Vault, Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and more. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.

title: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
description: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.

title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
description: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.

title: Choosing the right hybrid deployment for your AI workloads
description: Organizations are running AI workloads, including training, inference, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning, across an expanding set of environments, spanning AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. Explore how customers deploy GPU-accelerated AI across the full hybrid spectrum: NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances in Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time inference. Hear how customers navigate these decisions and learn which environment fits each AI workload, without compromising performance or compliance.

title: Claude Code: From first feature to optimized agentic workflows (sponsored by Anthropic)
description: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Point it at a codebase and choose your path, self-paced in the browser on Amazon Bedrock. In the Build with Claude track, give Claude project context, explore an unfamiliar repository, then plan, implement, and test a change you watch run - no experience required. In the Scale with Agents track, orchestrate parallel subagents across an agentic app, add review and verification gates, then apply Anthropic-authored skills to improve its performance and lower cost. Terminal experience assumed. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: Claude Keeps Building: How Coding Agents Change Software Development (sponsored by Anthropic)
description: Coding agents make sustained, autonomous progress on real software. The question is what happens to the rest of the software development lifecycle. Claude Code runs for hours unattended, works beyond the terminal, and takes on more of the work around the code. We'll show where it stands and how engineering changes when the whole lifecycle becomes automatable: what engineers do, how review and testing evolve, where quality comes from when code is cheap. Live demos on AWS and numbers from our engineering, where Claude writes most of our code. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: Cleared for Takeoff Hybrid Observability at the Busiest Airport (sponsored by SolarWinds)
description: Managing over a thousand network nodes across terminals, baggage systems, and cloud infrastructure requires more than reactive troubleshooting. Join Cedric Reed, Network Administrator at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and SolarWinds to discover how the world’s busiest airport replaced manual oversight with proactive observability. Learn how unified visibility across on-premises hardware and AWS Cloud eliminates noise, reduces downtime, and keeps critical systems online for millions of daily travelers. Discover how hop-by-hop visualization and real-time telemetry seamlessly monitor a vast network of surveillance systems covering the entire 7-mile campus to optimize operational resilience and passenger safety. This presentation is brought to you by SolarWinds, an AWS Partner.

title: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
description: Complex projects outgrow a single AI agent's context and capability. CLI Agent Orchestrator (CAO), an awslabs open source project, coordinates 8 CLIs including Amazon Kiro CLI, Claude Code, and Codex into a multi-agent powerhouse via the Model Context Protocol and tmux. It provides a centralised harness with shared skills, memory, and integration with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. In this builders' session you'll install CAO, launch a supervisor and specialist agents, and put the team to work on a real change in a sample repo. You'll walk away with a multi-agent workflow to drop into your projects.

title: Clinical Trials, Reimagined at the Speed of AI (sponsored by PwC)
description: Bringing a new drug to market takes over a decade, and much of that time is lost to paperwork rather than science. This session tells how pharma leaders are transforming clinical development with agentic AI on AWS. Attendees will hear how PwC’s Digital Trial Core turns clinical protocols into structured, machine-readable data, powering AI agents that draw on historical insights and reusable, modular content to streamline study startup activities such as vendor selection, budgeting, negotiations, and trial documentation. Industry leaders will share how these solutions move from proof of concept into live studies, bringing treatments to patients sooner. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Close the gap between code and production
description: Why is it so hard to connect a production alert to the code change that caused it? Metrics and traces reveal something is wrong but stop short of the function responsible. Developers guess which deployment introduced the regression, manually correlating dashboards with recent commits. Meanwhile, AI coding agents that could help write fixes are blind to runtime behavior. In this code talk, we'll explore how to close the gap between observability signals and the code your team owns, what new signals make that connection possible, how developers and AI agents can consume them, and what changes when observability reaches the code level.

title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
description: Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Closing the Loop: How Cognition’s AI Continuously Improves Itself (sponsored by Datadog)
description: As AI accelerates software development, production systems are changing faster than teams can understand manually. Cognition is closing that gap by giving Devin, its software engineering AI agent running on AWS, access to its own production telemetry through Datadog. Devin uses that context to reason about its production behavior and take action when needed. That feedback loop turns production insights into improvements to Devin’s reliability and future task performance. In this session, we’ll show how Devin investigates alerts, correlates metrics and logs, distinguishes real issues from noise, and uses those insights to improve its harness and workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

title: Cloud agent work needs infrastructure. We built it. (sponsored by Asana)
description: Organizations need an operating layer where humans and agents can run critical workflows together. That’s Asana. As software development shifts toward work performed by agents in the cloud, engineering teams need the same connected approach at enterprise scale. Command brings Asana’s operating layer to engineering, giving developers one surface for project management and coding work—connecting planning, assignment, and execution across the organization. Command works with coding agents teams already use, including Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. See the challenges Command solves for product and engineering teams and how it works against real engineering workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Asana, an AWS Partner.

title: Cocktails to Code Building AI Bartenders with Amazon Bedrock
description: Plain-language AI orders fail if models hallucinate items that are out of stock. I built a reliable AI bartender grounded strictly in live inventory data. This session covers how an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock uses Strands Agents, AgentCore, and MCP tools to fetch real-time menus. We will dive into the serverless architecture, see what breaks during live text streaming, and evaluate the cost versus performance tradeoffs of production grounding. You will leave with a reusable pattern and the repository to build reliable, data-driven agents.

title: Code real-time multi-agent AI systems with Amazon ElastiCache
description: Modern algorithmic trading platforms deploy fleets of specialized AI agents, including market analysts, risk assessors, order executors, and compliance monitors, that must coordinate in real time without conflict. In this session, follow along as a trading platform's multi-agent workflows are coded live using Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey. Valkey Streams organize agent task queues, pub/sub channels broadcast market signals to agent swarms with low latency, and vector similarity search gives agents memory of prior market scenarios. Discover how atomic Lua scripts prevent duplicate orders and enable exactly-once workflow transitions.

title: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
description: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.

title: Coding the tool layer for AI agents on Serverless
description: Agents don't need new infrastructure - they need access to what you've already built. In this code talk, you'll retrofit a Serverless API into a production-ready agent tool, live in code. Implement an MCP server with versioned tools, wire it to AgentCore Gateway for discovery and invocation, then expose an entire Step Functions workflow, human-in-the-loop gates and all, as a single callable tool. Add scoped agent identity, watch an unauthorized call get blocked, then an authorized one go through. Walk away with a repeatable playbook for turning existing APIs into agent-ready tools.

title: Compete to build an AI agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: Organizations are ready to move beyond rule-based workflows to agents that reason, adapt, and act. In this gamified workshop, you'll use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to assemble a realistic conversational banking agent end-to-end: orchestration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness; secure tool integration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway; and guardrails with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy. Prebuilt modules accelerate development so you can focus on agent logic. Compete in real time as your agent's accuracy and efficiency are scored on a live leaderboard. Leave with a working agent pattern you can adapt to your own use cases and bragging rights on the leaderboard.

title: Composable Agentic AI: Build Your Partner Offerings for Enterprises
description: Enterprises deploying agents in production are converging on a common pattern: distributed systems with stable layer contracts, bounded autonomy, and security and observability built in from day one. That raises a concrete question for AWS partners - does your product plug into the architecture your customers are already standardizing on? In this hands-on workshop for ISVs and consulting partners, you'll learn the composable Enterprise Agentic AI Reference Architecture, see exactly where your product fits at each layer, and build alongside AWS GenAI services, that compose into a single coherent production system. You'll leave with working reference code for an enterprise-ready agentic architecture and a playbook for co-building on the AWS agentic stack.

title: Connect agents across frameworks live using the A2A open protocol
description: Agents built on different frameworks need to talk to each other. In this session we will build two agents on Strands and LangGraph, then wire them together using the A2A protocol hosted at the Linux Foundation. You will see the full handshake: AgentCard publication for discovery, task negotiation, streaming artifact exchange, and multi-turn collaboration between agents that share nothing except the protocol. We will deploy both sides on AgentCore Runtime and demonstrate cross-framework interoperability working live. You will leave with the patterns to make any framework's agents collaborate over a standard wire.

title: Constrain AI agents with permissions boundaries and Cedar in AgentCore
description: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, and unconstrained permissions lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you build defense-in-depth governance for agentic workloads. You create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through IAM policy, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and add deterministic Cedar enforcement in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The result constrains what agents can do while still letting legitimate actions through.

title: Content at the Speed of Live: AI-Powered Media Ops at Live Nation
description: Live Nation's subsidiaries generate petabytes of live event content across siloed storage. When an artist creates a viral moment, teams need it in fans' hands in minutes not days. In this session, learn how Live Nation built a platform that unifies fragmented media silos so teams can search, create, and publish in near-real time. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.

title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
description: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using  Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications.
