title: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
description: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.

title: Context to Action: Turning Agent Memory into a Customer Retention Lever (sponsored by MongoDB)
description: When a customer calls, a support rep has seconds to understand what they need, what device they're on, and how to solve it fast. Get it right, and you earn trust. Get it wrong, and churn becomes a real risk. T-Mobile closes that gap with agent memory: session context pre-populated before the call starts, enriched turn by turn as it unfolds, with real-time graph traversal connecting customer, device, and issue so the rep sees the full picture. MongoDB Atlas runs it all, from vector search over T-Mobile's knowledge corpus to in-call graph traversal to the live session-memory documents. Afterward, AWS Neptune turns that history into a graph shaping future routing and retention. Walk away with an architecture pattern for building agent memory in real time, and a way to decide what belongs in short-term memory versus what should persist. Featuring T-Mobile, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Continuous Attack Chains Across Every Surface (sponsored by Terra)
description: Most security tools score vulnerabilities in isolation, but attackers do not think in isolation. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. Learn how continuous, cross surface attack chaining changes what a security team should actually prioritize first. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

title: Controlling the AI Software Factory (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
description: AI isn't just making software faster; it's changing how software is produced. Engineering teams now run agents that write code, review PRs, validate releases, and deploy around the clock. The promise is real, but so is a new problem: how do you stay in control of systems that never stop evolving? Edith Harbaugh, CEO of LaunchDarkly, argues the defining challenge of the AI era isn't generating code, it's controlling autonomous systems in production, where agents drift and the old detect-fix-redeploy playbook breaks down. She'll share what LaunchDarkly learned building its own AI software factory, and how engineers stay in charge. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

title: Co-Sell to Co-Marketing: An AI-powered, end-to-end partner motion.
description: AWS Partners manage account planning, lead management, and campaign execution across multiple workflows. Discover how to unify these activities and build a seamless co-sell-to-co-marketing motion.

title: Craft, Don’t Vibe, Your MVP
description: Many people today use LLMs only for code generation. The best teams embrace AI across all stages of the SDLC. The decisions made before building the first version of your product directly affect its viability and success. Rather than relying on vibe coding to make these decisions implicitly, agents can be used to evaluate architectural options, compare trade-offs and challenge assumptions before a single line of code is created. This session explores how high-performing teams are investing time capturing standards, patterns and expertise, making them available for agents to apply consistently. Learn from practical real world examples how AI is being used to accelerate the delivery of production-ready systems, rather than those that carry technical debt from day one.

title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect (sponsored by Deloitte)
description: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: Ctrl+Alt+Ship: Hands-On with Kiro, Amazon Quick, and Amazon Connect Customer
description: Ctrl+Alt+Ship is a choose-your-own-adventure experience with self-paced labs spanning Kiro, Amazon Quick, and Amazon Connect Customer. Start with the Kiro IDE for AI-native development, or level up to multi-agent workflows. Solve an escape-room-style corporate crisis using Quick, your AI work assistant, choosing between a guided investigation or an advanced multi-step operation to plan, execute, and automate your way to cracking the case. With Connect Customer, see how AI resolves customer issues, gives agents context, and helps supervisors improve service—or go hands-on with the agentic CX designer, a no-code visual canvas, to build conversational AI. AWS facilitators from each product team will be available to answer questions. Labs are 30-60 min. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed.

title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
description: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

title: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
description: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Run live cost benchmarks against x86 equivalents to see exactly where Graviton5 pays back, and instrument with CloudWatch Container Insights to confirm performance parity. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.

title: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
description: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. title: Cutting manual accounts payable work
description: Enterprise customers pay for cloud services across dozens of payer accounts and countries through procurement/accounts payable platforms like SAP Ariba and Coupa and track it all in spreadsheets and email threads. Purchase orders run out unnoticed. Payments land on the wrong invoices. Disputes take months. In this session, see how a new first-party application gives Accounts Payable teams one live view of purchase orders, invoices and payments matched against billing records no console login required.

title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
description: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
description: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. title: Danske Bank's AI City: Scaling AI agents across an enterprise
description: Getting AI agents into production across a regulated enterprise means solving governance and security first. Danske Bank started with a handful of generative AI experiments and now runs more than 40 use cases in production. In this session, learn how Danske Bank built "AI City"—a governed, reusable platform that cut time-to-production from months to days. See how they structured the platform so new teams can ship agents without rebuilding authorization, logging, or model access controls from scratch, with production examples from personal banking, compliance, and capital markets, and explore the Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore architecture underneath it all.

title: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO)
description: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

title: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS (sponsored by Veeam)
description: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.

title: Datacenter to Cloud: Safety, Security, & Trust for AI Agents & Models (sponsored by Red Hat)
description: Deploying enterprise AI requires a unified framework across four governance pillars: Safety, Security, Risk, and Trust. Demystify multi-layer vulnerabilities spanning base models, agentic harnesses, and tool usage, addressing threats like Mythos model risks. Learn defense-in-depth strategies for agents—including sandboxing, privilege control, reasoning tracing, and dynamic red-teaming—to mitigate prompt injection, data leakage, and excessive agency. We’ll map these practices to global frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act to ensure continuous production readiness. This presentation is brought to you by Red Hat, an AWS Partner.

title: Data Mesh to Agentic AI: Building an AI-Ready Enterprise on AWS
description: How do you build an AI-ready data foundation in a global investment organization without compromising trust, governance, or speed? CPP Investments—manager of one of the world’s largest pension funds—is evolving from fragmented data toward a governed enterprise data platform on AWS, using data mesh principles, federated ownership, and platform engineering to scale with guardrails. Join their CTO for a look inside the architecture, operating model, and critical trade-offs shaping this evolution, and how it brings trusted data closer to investment decisions while laying the foundation for conversational data experiences and agentic AI.

title: Decision patterns for AI Agents with Amazon Connect Customer
description: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation. In this chalk talk, we'll explore when to use first-party tools, when AWS Lambda gives you more flexibility, and when MCP integrations make sense—with latency, operational complexity, and compliance requirements as the deciding factors. We’ll discuss patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI agents and automated evaluation pipelines using Contact Lens and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. You'll leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center, including guidance for financial services and regulated industries.

title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora and its innovations
description: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. Aurora is a built-for-the-cloud, serverless relational database that delivers unparalleled performance and availability at global scale for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. Also, learn about Aurora DSQL, the fastest serverless distributed SQL database.

title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
description: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

title: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4)
description: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.

title: Defeat Player Evasion: AI Moderation at Scale on Amazon Bedrock.
description: Players evade moderation with leetspeak, homoglyphs, emoji sequences, and fast-evolving slang. Brute-force AI classification catches evasion but is cost-prohibitive at scale. In this workshop, build a tiered moderation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock that routes 80–90% of traffic through deterministic normalization and pre-filters before invoking a model. Ambiguous content gets classified by Amazon Nova at sub-500ms latency. Only the hardest cases escalate to multi-agent analysis on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for context-dependent decisions. Configure per-category thresholds, instrument cost-per-decision tracking, and stress-test against real gaming evasion patterns. Walk away with a deployable, cost-optimized pipeline. Laptop required

title: Defending the Three Lanes: Preventing Toxic Agentic Combinations with Cyera and AWS (sponsored by Cyera)
description: Agentic AI is entering production faster than enterprise authorization models can keep up, and most access decisions are made without regard to the sensitivity of the data agents can reach, turning over-permissioned agents into high-value targets. This session introduces the three lanes: the data agents touch, the identity they act as, and the actions they take, as the framework for defending agentic AI on AWS. See how Cyera's Agent Guardian extends Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with data-aware authorization to enforce least privilege, monitor agent-to-data activity, and prove it to auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
description: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.

title: Delivering Measurable Customer Business Outcomes
description: Proving business impact at the C-suite level is what separates a deployment partner from a strategic advisor. That's where the Value Realization Plan (VRP) comes in, the structured approach at the heart of the AWS Business Value Realization motion. We'll cover building a compelling case for change, defining KPIs that resonate with executives, and driving adoption through change management. Learn the pitfalls that stall outcome conversations, how to accelerate buy-in, and how to frame impact in terms executives act on. Leave with a repeatable approach for your next engagement and a foundation for a customer success practice that scales.

title: Deploy agents you can trust
description: You're ready to put AI agents into production, but you can't prove they will stay within bounds. When agents act autonomously, governance, safety, and security become one question: can you trust what they do next? In this session, explore what it takes to build a unified governance approach across identity, policy, observability, and compliance. Then see how automated reasoning delivers mathematical proof that agent policies hold under all conditions, including the ones you'd never think to test. Leave knowing how to govern what your agents do and verify they do only what you intend.

title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
description: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. This session explores how customers deploy agent sandboxes on EC2 across distinct patterns, each offering different trade-offs between isolation, latency, and performance across our instance families. We cover isolation trade-offs, cost per sandbox-second, and capacity planning at scale. Attendees leave with a decision model for selecting the right pattern based on their scale, security posture, and operational maturity.

title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
description: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
description: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

title: Deploy and optimize world models with agentic AI workflows
description: World models generate real-time video by learning environment dynamics, which powers interactive simulation for gaming, robotics, and autonomous driving, but deploying these latency-sensitive pipelines is complex. In this builders session, we deploy and optimize a real-time video world model on AWS Trainium using AWS Neuron Agentic Development skills that automate compilation, profiling, and kernel optimization through natural-language interaction. See the agent identify bottlenecks, then select optimized kernels from Hugging Face or write custom kernels from scratch. You will apply these agentic tools yourself to reach optimized, real-time inference on silicon built specifically for AI.

title: Deploying a Fitness App from Specs with Kiro and AgentCore
description: In a simulated scenario, Fitness trainers waste 30 minutes daily on manual data entry and cannot spot trends across clients. In this SimuLearn session, you build FitTrack AI using Kiro's spec-driven workflows and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You design flexible schemas, create agent tools for client management and natural language analytics, deploy the agent on ECS Fargate, configure Bedrock Guardrails for health safety, and implement anomaly detection using database change streams.

title: Deploying Frontier Voice Agents Privately on AWS (sponsored by ElevenLabs)
description: Frontier voice agents are already handling live customer calls inside health systems, banks and insurers, without audio ever leaving the customer's AWS account. This session covers the architecture that makes that possible, from in-VPC deployment and zero data retention to integration with their existing stack. Working from a production deployment taking real calls, we walk through the latency budget that keeps conversational voice feeling human, the trade-offs private deployment brings, and how to size it for your own environment. Leave with an understanding of where ElevenAgents fits in your current environment, a reference architecture and a deployment checklist. This presentation is brought to you by ElevenLabs, an AWS Partner.

title: Deploying the foundation for successful enterprise AI (sponsored by Glean)
description: Successful enterprise AI depends on more than just the latest models. It requires context that connects knowledge across systems, intelligence that turns information into useful action, and protection that preserves permissions, security, and trust. This session presents a practical foundation for deploying AI across the enterprise—using AWS and Bedrock to move from isolated pilots to governed workflows. Learn how leaders are designing for adoption, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement from the start. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.

title: Deploy, scale, and tune AI model serving with self-managed agents
description: Setting up AI infrastructure, tuning model performance, and benchmarking throughput could mean navigating brittle tooling, context rot in long sessions, irrelevant retrieval, missing guardrails for irreversible actions, bursty GPU and CPU demands, and observability gaps. In this chalk talk, explore how to set up, manage, and scale self-managed autonomous agents on AWS to address these challenges with built-in memory, safety boundaries, and audit trails. We will walk through how to quickly deploy a reference architecture on Amazon EKS, tune a 550B-parameter model for inference using disaggregated serving with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM, and scale with Elastic Fabric Adapter for cross-node KV cache transfer.

title: Deploy, scale, and tune AI model serving with self-managed agents
description: Setting up AI infrastructure, tuning model performance, and benchmarking throughput could mean navigating brittle tooling, context rot in long sessions, irrelevant retrieval, missing guardrails for irreversible actions, bursty GPU and CPU demands, and observability gaps. In this chalk talk, explore how to set up, manage, and scale self-managed autonomous agents on AWS to address these challenges with built-in memory, safety boundaries, and audit trails. We will walk through how to quickly deploy a reference architecture on Amazon EKS, tune a 550B-parameter model for inference using disaggregated serving with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM, and scale with Elastic Fabric Adapter for cross-node KV cache transfer.

title: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
description: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query. See how AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, where one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. The graph stays in your account.

title: Designing for Operability: Catching Performance Gaps Before Scale
description: A training workload had plenty of GPU capacity, yet utilization remained low and training time kept increasing. The GPUs were healthy. The real bottleneck was upstream: the data pipeline could not feed them fast enough, leaving expensive accelerators waiting for work. This talk walks through how we traced that utilization gap, found where throughput was being lost, and identified the signals that could have exposed the problem earlier. Through this production experience, we’ll look at what it means to design for operability before scale, when performance, utilization, and cost problems are still easier to fix.

title: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
description: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.

title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
description: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
description: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

title: Developing Apps from Specs with Kiro
description: Kiro, the Agentic IDE, transforms a single natural language prompt into structured requirements, a technical design, and an executable implementation plan. In this SimuLearn session, you build a city event management application by guiding Kiro through its spec-driven workflow: generating EARS-format user stories, reviewing architecture decisions, and executing a sequenced task list that produces a working MVP. You also configure a Kiro Hook that automatically validates data files on save.

title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
description: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall every active generation — and letting each phase scale on its own terms. It isn't free: KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still win. The difference is your traffic. In this hands-on builders session, you run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn the decision framework — input length, prefix reuse, latency SLO — and leave with runnable configurations.

title: Don't ban it, broker it: Govern AI coding agents with Amazon Bedrock
description: AI coding agents are becoming embedded in development workflows. In regulated environments (e.g.,financial services), that raises concerns around data residency, code exfiltration, auditability, and runaway costs. But banning the tools creates shadow AI. In this session, we'll whiteboard a better path by pointing AI coding agents at Amazon Bedrock through a gateway in your VPC. One control point for identity, data residency, prompt inspection, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, cost controls, and immutable audit. We'll walk through the request lifecycle, debate trade-offs around latency, budgets, and MCP tool calls, and show how the same broker pattern governs any agent touching sensitive data.

title: Don't build agents, build environments instead (sponsored by Modal)
description: The hard part of background agents is the background, not the agent. We'll talk about the common design that software factories have converged to and why building environments for agents is still hard. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

title: Don't rewrite your APIs: Make them agent-ready for agentic AI
description: Organizations want agentic AI, but valuable capabilities sit behind legacy APIs, AWS Lambda functions, and internal services. In this chalk talk, we explore practical, low-lift patterns for making existing endpoints agent-ready without replacing systems of record. Using a financial services scenario, we walk through how OpenAPI specs, AWS Lambda facades, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway expose existing endpoints as composable agent tools. We show how existing RBAC and OAuth scopes map into Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Cedar policies so you reuse your governance posture. Walk away with a 5-level maturity model you can apply to your own API estate.

title: Don't rewrite your APIs: Make them agent-ready for agentic AI

Using a financial services scenario, we walk through how OpenAPI specs, AWS Lambda facades, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway expose existing endpoints as composable agent tools. title: Drive AI at full speed: The enterprise blueprint (sponsored by HashiCorp)
description: AI gave teams a faster car. It did not fix the roads. As teams create more applications, infrastructure and complexity, the challenge shifts from moving faster to operating smarter. Enterprises need context to understand what is happening, agency to act across the tools they already use, and control to keep speed from becoming chaos. In this session, see how Terraform and Vault together with Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore and IBM Concert to standardize delivery, secure access and connect application context to action across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.

title: Drive multi-server migrations from discovery to cutover with AWS Transform
description: Migrating VMware or other on-premises environments to AWS involves dozens of coordinated steps, and most teams spend more time planning handoffs than actually moving workloads. In this workshop, you'll experience how AWS Transform's agentic AI orchestrates the full migration lifecycle: intelligent discovery, AI-driven wave planning, automated network translation, and server rehost execution. Specialized AI agents coordinate across each stage, making autonomous decisions while keeping you in control. You'll leave with hands-on experience using agentic AI to execute a real end-to-end multi-server migration. Laptop required.

In this workshop, you'll experience how AWS Transform's agentic AI orchestrates the full migration lifecycle: intelligent discovery, AI-driven wave planning, automated network translation, and server rehost execution. Specialized AI agents coordinate across each stage, making autonomous decisions while keeping you in control. You'll leave with hands-on experience using agentic AI to execute a real end-to-end multi-server migration. Laptop required.

title: DTCC: Rethinking mainframe modernization with spec-driven development
description: Services like Kiro, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Continuum, and AWS DevOps Agent have enabled DTCC to rethink its software delivery lifecycle. Now, the company is harnessing agents to modernize its legacy mainframe infrastructure. DTCC has adopted a spec-driven approach to COBOL refactoring, front-loading the process with a focus on principles, target architecture, and anti-pattern avoidance. In this session, you’ll see how a small team of engineers produced a fully functional microservice-based trade data ingestion platform in a few weeks, cutting the development timeline by 60% while laying the foundation to scale to peaks of 300+ million trades per day and beyond.

title: Duke Energy: Human-Led, Agent-Driven Enterprise App Innovation on AWS
description: Duke Energy is pioneering a new frontier in software creation by combining human leadership with agent-driven execution using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AppGen, its enterprise AI platform. Specialized agents enable both developers and business users to rapidly build production-ready, full-stack applications with speed and precision, driving millions in cost savings while accelerating innovation. This strategic, multi-year collaboration is transforming manual workflows into intelligent, automated processes across business units. The approach supports scalable adoption of agentic AI while ensuring strong governance, reliability, and operational excellence—empowering teams to innovate faster, reduce complexity, and modernize systems consistently across the enterprise.

title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
description: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

title: Earned autonomy: handing production over to agents (sponsored by incident.io)
description: What does it take to trust an AI agent with production? This talk explores how agents earn increasing responsibility, from investigating problems and recommending fixes to taking action themselves. We’ll look at where human judgment matters and what gives us the confidence to hand over more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by incident.io, an AWS Partner.

title: Edge-to-Action: Powering Agentic AI via Cloudera's Anywhere Cloud (sponsored by Cloudera)
description: Distributed edge assets, remote sensors, and transactional systems often leave operational data isolated from cloud AI platforms. This session demonstrates how to break down these boundaries using Cloudera Anywhere Cloud. Discover an event-driven architectural blueprint that standardizes real-time streaming on-premises, unifies hybrid pipelines, and lands telemetry directly into Cloudera’s Open Data Lakehouse on AWS. Learn how grounding autonomous AI agents on AWS with continuous edge context simplifies data sovereignty, eliminates bottlenecks, and enables real-time, closed-loop enterprise automation. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: EFA deep dive: Architecture, evolution, and scaling with OpenAI
description: We built EFA to deliver multi-tenant, elastic, high-performance networking with portability across every instance type and accelerator through Libfabric. The architecture that followed, such as multipath packet spraying, out-of-order delivery, and encryption of every byte in transit, has scaled from HPC workloads to the backbone of today's largest AI training clusters. Now it's evolving again to support disaggregated inference and expert parallelism. OpenAI joins to share how they adapted their production inference stack to EFA on EC2 UltraServers, covering Reliable Datagram semantics for GPU-to-GPU collectives, NCCL tuning, and topology-aware communication patterns that unlock new performance.

title: Elastic Fabric Adapter powering the largest AI workloads on AWS
description: AWS built Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to bring high-performance networking to the cloud - powered by the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol designed for elastic, reliable, cloud-scale performance. This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.

title: Elasticsearch - the Search database for Context Engineering and AI (sponsored by Elastic)
description: Your agentic applications have an accuracy and cost problem, and it's not your model choice. Sound familiar? If you're a developer trying to get LLMs to work effectively with your business context, this session is for you. Come learn how we rearchitected Elasticsearch as the database of choice for the different data types your enterprise knowledge is buried in — docs, logs, metrics, tickets, sales call transcripts, and more. From foundational innovations like Columnar and VectorDB mode with no ETL, to best-in-class retrieval that combines vector search, Jina embedding models, and native inference, Elastic is the context database for your production needs. Join this session to learn the best practices, from optimizing data preparation to retrieval patterns, to make your agents a production reality. This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

title: Emerging multi-agent patterns for complex financial workflows
description: Multi-agent systems are rapidly evolving beyond static orchestration patterns. In this chalk talk, we explore the newest collaboration paradigms gaining momentum, including ephemeral agent patterns and self-improving agents, alongside established approaches like hierarchical, sequential, and peer-to-peer coordination. Walk through how to apply these patterns to claims adjudication, underwriting, and financial portfolio advisory using Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness engineering best practices. We'll discuss when to select each pattern, how to combine them for complex workflows, and how AgentCore harness capabilities enable scalable, governed multi-agent architectures. Gain practical guidance for designing the next generation of agentic applications.

title: Enabling agentic development loops with a local cloud validation layer (sponsored by LocalStack)
description: Agentic coding loops let AI develop, test, and iterate on code autonomously. But agents often lack the permissions required to validate how code behaves in the cloud, stalling the cycle and holding back velocity. This session will show how simulating your AWS application environments locally can enable AI agents to identify and fix bugs faster, more securely, and more effectively than human engineers can when building in live cloud development environments. This presentation is brought to you by LocalStack, an AWS Partner.

title: End-to-end agentic modernization with United Airlines & Bank Hapoalim
description: Legacy applications across mainframe, midrange, and distributed platforms have long resisted modernization efforts. A new approach that combines deterministic methods with agentic AI is changing that by delivering speed and accuracy. Learn how United Airlines modernized crew operations while maintaining FAR compliance, and how Bank Hapoalim analyzed a 3.2-million-line mortgage application and delivered an insurance module to production under a board-mandated deadline while reducing operational risk. Follow the end-to-end journey, from automated discovery and business rule extraction with AWS Transform through microservices engineering with Kiro to production deployment. Leave with a playbook for modernizing the applications everyone said were untouchable.

title: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
description: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. Attendees track experiments with managed MLflow, orchestrate repeatable training workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and built-in lineage tracking, register and version models in Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, deploy through CI/CD promotion pipelines, and monitor for drift and quality with Model Monitor. Governance such as access control, validation, approvals, and Responsible AI guardrails is embedded into every step. Attendees leave with a repeatable, governed path from experiment to production they can stand up within a week

title: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
description: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. title: End-to-End Voice Agents with AWS and Deepgram (sponsored by Deepgram)
description: Voice agents are growing in popularity, but most fall apart the first time a caller interrupts or asks a hard question. In this session, Deepgram builds one live on AWS: the Deepgram Voice Agent API streams speech in and out within minutes, with Amazon Bedrock as the reasoning layer. You'll see natural, expressive voices, sub-second responses, and barge-in handling that actually works. Compliance requirements? The same models deploy via Amazon SageMaker inside your own VPC, so audio never leaves your AWS perimeter. Leave with running code and an architecture your security team can approve. This presentation is brought to you by Deepgram, an AWS Partner.

title: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
description: Your security team defines the controls, and your product teams build and deploy AI applications across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts. This chalk talk shows how to enforce AI guardrails centrally without making your security team the bottleneck. We walk through an architecture for applying Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through controls at the AWS Organizations, account, and AI infrastructure layers. You see how controls inherit across those layers, which limitations to plan for, and how tiered governance lets teams tailor controls to their applications while the organizational baseline stays enforced.

title: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
description: Your security team defines the controls, and your product teams build and deploy AI applications across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts. This chalk talk shows how to enforce AI guardrails centrally without making your security team the bottleneck. We walk through an architecture for applying Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through controls at the AWS Organizations, account, and AI infrastructure layers. You see how controls inherit across those layers, which limitations to plan for, and how tiered governance lets teams tailor controls to their applications while the organizational baseline stays enforced.

title: Engineering AI Agents You Can Trust in Production (sponsored by Workato)
description: Your agent nails the demo, then breaks in production. More often than not, the model isn't what failed, it's everything around it. We'll walk through a methodology for making agent actions reliable, recoverable, and observable in production. You'll leave with patterns you can build yourself, drawn from lessons learned over 100+ enterprise MCP deployments. This presentation is brought to you by Workato, an AWS Partner.

title: Engineering the Context that Makes Enterprise AI Work (sponsored by Impetus Technologies Inc)
description: Every enterprise has access to the same AI models. The real differentiator is context. Discover Impetus’ Context Engineering Delivery Lifecycle, a proven methodology than ensures no AI agent reaches production without a signed-off context bundle, evaluation record, and explainability trace. Learn how to engineer enterprise data, domain knowledge, industry ontologies, business rules, and governance into a robust context layer agents need to deliver accurate, trusted outcomes. Get practical insights on building AI systems on AWS that are grounded, explainable, reliable, and ready to scale. This presentation is brought to you by Impetus Technologies Inc, an AWS Partner.

title: Enhance Production Applications with AI-Assisted Development in Kiro
description: Enhancing production apps requires balancing delivery velocity with code safety. Kiro gives you both. In this hands-on lab, add features to enhance a live application using AI-assisted development on Kiro. Define coding standards with steering files and specs, generate UI components from natural language prompts, automate quality checks with agent hooks, install powers for domain expertise, and delegate backend analysis to custom subagents. Deploy your changes confidently to production environments.

title: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j)
description: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. This presentation is brought to you by Neo4j, an AWS Partner.

title: Enterprise-Ready: How NetEase Governs AI at Scale
description: Learn how NetEase, one of the world's largest gaming companies, is building enterprise AI governance as AI adoption scales across the organization. Discover how Amazon Bedrock enables multi-model routing, cost controls, and team-level budget management to optimize AI usage. See how NetEase enforces governance with company-wide AI policies, Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestrating agentic AI workflows with centralized governance and observability. Learn why a platform-first approach to cost, access, and safety is critical for enabling AI innovation at enterprise scale.

title: Escaping IIoT Pilot Purgatory: Why Your Database Breaks at Scale (sponsored by Tiger Data)
description: Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen. See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. This presentation is brought to you by Tiger Data, an AWS Partner.

title: Eval-Driven LLM Routing: Cut Costs Without Losing Accuracy
description: This session shows how to build an eval-driven LLM routing system: harvest a production eval dataset, define accuracy KPIs using LLM-as-judge, set a non-negotiable accuracy floor as the practitioner's decision, benchmark candidate models, and generate a routing policy optimized for cost within that floor. Result: approximately 80% cost reduction at maintained accuracy. A reference architecture you can start implementing immediately.

title: Evaluate and ship AI agents confidently
description: Amazon CloudWatch Omni converges application and AI agent observability into one AI-powered experience built on open standards. In this session, instrument an agent with a popular framework and trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step in the Trace Explorer. Run built-in evaluators to score responses for correctness, coherence, and faithfulness, then test prompt variations in the Playground and compare configurations against golden datasets with Experiments. Explore auto-discovered topology, correlate agent behavior with downstream services, and investigate issues with AWS DevOps Agent using natural language. Leave with a working observability pipeline from IDE to production and the skills to evaluate, debug, and operate agents from one pane.

title: Evaluate Enterprise AI Agents with an Eval-First Approach
description: A successful agent demo does not guarantee production readiness because agents can behave inconsistently across question types and multi-turn sessions. In this spotlight lab, you build two custom evaluators for an agent: THELMA, which scores single-turn RAG quality across seven dimensions including hallucination detection via groundedness scoring, and Mind the Goal, which computes Goal Success Rate across entire conversations and attributes failures to root causes. You register both as native AgentCore evaluators, run batch evaluations, and use diagnostic outputs to pinpoint exactly what to optimize first.

title: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services
description: Financial institutions building AI agents face a core challenge: how do you prove an agent is reliable enough for production when regulators demand explainability and consistency? How do you reliably detect when a production agent's behavior drifts? In this chalk talk, we explore patterns for rigorous agent evaluation in regulated environments. We discuss defining ground truth, measuring agent quality with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, and automating re-evaluation as prompts, tools, and parameters evolve. Leave with practical blueprints for constructing datasets, choosing metrics, and building continuous agent evaluation workflows for production.

title: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services
description: Financial institutions building AI agents face a core challenge: how do you prove an agent is reliable enough for production when regulators demand explainability and consistency? How do you reliably detect when a production agent's behavior drifts? In this chalk talk, we explore patterns for rigorous agent evaluation in regulated environments. We discuss defining ground truth, measuring agent quality with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, and automating re-evaluation as prompts, tools, and parameters evolve. Leave with practical blueprints for constructing datasets, choosing metrics, and building continuous agent evaluation workflows for production.

title: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
description: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.

title: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
description: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.

title: Event-driven AI agents for security triage with AWS Continuum
description: Security teams need to detect, correlate, and respond to threats faster than manual processes allow. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Continuum orchestrates event-driven AI agents that triage, investigate, and escalate security incidents in real time. We walk through how alerts from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub flow through Amazon EventBridge, triggering AWS Lambda functions that invoke agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with human-in-the-loop controls for high-severity events. Discover best practices for reducing alert fatigue, accelerating MTTR, and scaling security operations for financial services and other regulated industries where every response must be explainable and audit ready.

title: Every Candidate, Every Time: AI-Led Structured Interviews at Scale
description: Who you hire is the most important decision you make, and the hardest to get right at scale. What if AI agents could run structured interviews grounded in Amazon’s hiring science and evaluate every candidate the same way? In this chalk talk, we show how role requirements become evaluation criteria and questions, how AI agents hold a natural conversation while covering each competency and gathering evidence, and how responses are scored against a rubric tied to specific evidence. See a single job posting become a scored, evidence-backed evaluation. Leave knowing how to tell hiring science from gut feel, and why that shows up in better hires and a fairer experience for every candidate.

title: Everyone is a Coder. Govern what they build. (sponsored by Coder)
description: Suddenly, everyone is a coder. People who never wrote code now build apps, dashboards, and prototypes with AI, faster than most teams can govern them. The result is shadow AI, ungoverned data, and IP risk. See how a leading global private investment firm gave citizen developers a governed place to build on its existing AWS infrastructure, replacing scattered, unmanaged tools. Learn how approved models, scoped templates, centralized container management, and a complete audit trail let hundreds of builders move fast inside guardrails. Attendees leave with a practical model for governing AI adoption on their own AWS environment. This presentation is brought to you by Coder, an AWS Partner.

title: Everyone Says They Have an Ontology. Almost Nobody Does (sponsored by TextQL)
description: Ontology has become one of the defining ideas in enterprise AI. Every cloud and data platform now claims to have one. They rarely converge on the same structure, conventions, or architecture. Those differences determine whether an ontology can support agentic AI. That test comes down to three things: how it's structured, how it's generated from the systems and context already in place, and how it stays current as the business changes. This talk lays out the practical requirements for an ontology built for agentic AI, drawing on the architecture TextQL runs across the messiest data estates at Fortune 50 companies. This presentation is brought to you by TextQL, an AWS Partner.

title: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
description: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver compelling price-performance for inference and select training use cases. This session breaks down where G7e/G7 fits: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS/$) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. We'll cover the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), walk through a TCO comparison, and close with a decision framework for when G7e/G7 is the right call vs. P-family instances.

title: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm)
description: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.

title: Faster tech debt remediation without the setup overhead
description: In this Code Talk, learn how continuous modernization enables faster tech debt analysis and remediation by starting directly from your cloud accounts. Instead of manually connecting code repositories upfront, you can begin identifying tech debt immediately using lifecycle-event signals from your cloud environment. The platform then provides an easy path to resolution with automatic generation of pull requests. We will walk through the account-first workflow and how it gets you from discovery to remediation faster with less setup.

title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
description: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
description: Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Find the waste hiding in your accelerator fleetÂ
description: GPU and AI accelerators are the most expensive resources your teams run â€” and the hardest to observe when shared across teams. Most platform owners can't tell which workload is using which device, whether it's working or idle, or what a stalled run is costing per hour. When something degrades, teams find out after a crash or a surprise bill.Â This lightning talk explores how to spot what's sitting idle, pinpoint a failing device without sacrificing the healthy ones around it, and prioritize fixes by how much spend you can recover.

title: Fine-tune and evaluate NVIDIA Open models on Amazon SageMaker
description: Learn how to customize NVIDIA Open models using Amazon SageMaker without managing training infrastructure. This session walks through preparing a dataset, fine-tuning the model, and evaluating the customized model against the base model to measure improvements in quality. Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for adapting NVIDIA's open models to domain-specific use cases on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
description: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
description: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. title: FinOps for AI: Scale Investments That Work. Stop Ones That Don't. (sponsored by Kion)
description: Most organizations can tell you what they spend on AI. Fewer can tell you what they're getting for it. FinOps for AI closes that gap, but it takes three things: visibility into spend by use case; controls that act on what the data tells you instead of just surfacing it; and value tracking that connects spend to outcomes your stakeholders can evaluate. This session includes real examples of token attribution, guardrail patterns that respond to data, and a model for turning ROI signals into corrective action. This presentation is brought to you by Kion, an AWS Partner.

title: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
description: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Using Bedrock's multi-model routing, each agent selects the optimal foundation model for its task. Along the way we solve hard coordination problems: message routing, shared state, deadlock avoidance, and cost control. One presenter codes; the other narrates architecture decisions. Whether you synthesize research literature, member feedback, grant requirements, or compliance updates — leave with replicable patterns for your domain.

title: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
description: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. Leave with a production-ready cost optimization blueprint.

title: Free your .NET app from Windows licensing with AI-powered portability
description: This workshop walks you through modernizing a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to cross-platform .NET 10. You will learn how to transform a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor using AWS Transform Interactive Mode. Throughout the session, you will interact with the AI agent in real-time asking questions, reviewing assessment and transformation plans, and examining transformation results, including code diffs and build verification. Finally, use Kiro to identify and fix post-transformation runtime issues, such as layout problems, and containerize and deploy the transformed application to Amazon ECS Fargate using the Kiro IDE.

title: Fresh Threats, Stale Defenses: The Race for Real‑Time Security (sponsored by Booz Allen)
description: Cyber conflict has entered a new phase, accelerated by AI that increases the volume, velocity, and sophistication of attacks. The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.

title: From AI-Assisted Engineering to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by Dynatrace)
description: As enterprise AI matures, the opportunity extends far beyond software development. Join United Airlines, AWS, and Dynatrace to discover how insights powered by AI, full stack cloud observability, and runtime intelligence are helping engineering and operations teams improve reliability, accelerate delivery, and reduce operational complexity. Learn how leading organizations are using real-time data to automate investigations, predict issues before customer impact, and move toward autonomous operations. The session will cover real-world adoption lessons, AI governance considerations, and practical steps to balance automation with accountability while unlocking greater value from AI across the software lifecycle at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

title: From AI to Action: Powering Agentic Enterprises with AWS and Infosys (sponsored by Infosys)
description: As AI evolves from generating insights to driving action, leading organizations are adopting intelligent agents to transform how work gets done. Hear from enterprise leaders as they share their journeys to building agentic businesses with AWS and Infosys, accelerating decision making, improving productivity, and unlocking measurable business value at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Infosys, an AWS Partner.

title: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
description: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.

title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
description: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.
