title: From commit to secure: catch vulnerabilities at machine speed with AWS Continuum
description: Organizations struggle to detect vulnerabilities before code reaches production. This session demonstrates how to use AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent) directly into your CI/CD pipeline. Learn how to shift security left, catch vulnerabilities at commit and build stages, surface actionable remediation guidance that prevents vulnerable code from reaching production, and accelerate secure software delivery without slowing developer velocity.

title: From Databases to Agentic AI: Powering Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS (sponsored by AMD)
description: Today's organizations need infrastructure that can efficiently support everything from mission-critical databases to next-generation AI applications. Join AMD and AWS to explore how customers are leveraging Amazon EC2 instances powered by AMD EPYC processors across Amazon RDS, analytics, Agentic AI, HPC, and cloud-native applications. Learn how AMD-powered AWS infrastructure delivers compelling price-performance, scalability, and operational efficiency while helping organizations accelerate innovation, optimize costs, and meet growing compute demands. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

title: From dataset to a deployed fine-tuned LLM in hours on SageMaker AI
description: Go from dataset to a custom foundation model in just a few hours, without the need to set up any infrastructure. In this hands-on workshop, you will fine-tune LLMs using Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization, requiring no infrastructure setup or GPU management. You will walk through the entire workflow — preparing datasets, launching training jobs, registering assets in the SageMaker AI Registry, evaluating using the "LLM-as-a-Judge" technique, and deploying to a real-time endpoint — leveraging Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with LoRA as a memory-efficient optimization method. By the end of the workshop, you will be ready to customize models at scale immediately.

title: From Demo to Production: The Craft Behind AI Agents at Scale
description: Your agent reasons, calls tools, and demos beautifully. Then production happens. This session is about the craft that lives after the demo: the unglamorous engineering that separates agents that ship from agents that stay in notebooks. Using real AWS accounts and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, I'll walk through deterministic guardrails that make destructive actions impossible (not just discouraged), spend limits an agent can't prompt-inject its way past, evaluation you can trust, and the IAM that silently breaks first. You'll leave with a production-readiness framework for agentic systems—and honest stories about everything that failed on the way there.

title: From discoverable to buyable: Commerce stacks for agent-driven shoppers (sponsored by Stripe)
description: Join Stripe on how AI is changing how shoppers find and buy products—and what it means for your commerce stack. With 20% of holiday ecommerce traffic projected from AI agents, this session is designed for retail leaders moving from "exploring" to "ready." Converting this traffic requires a different approach to catalog readiness, checkout, fraud, and fulfillment. Attendees will leave with clear priorities to act on today and carry into 2027. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

title: From documents to decisions: Agentic AI for federal operations
description: Accelerate mission-critical federal operations with agentic AI—from public-information analysis to sensitive document workflows. This expert chalk talk explores patterns for document review, supply chain optimization and classified medical health records backed by real-world implementations. Whiteboard multi-agent orchestration with Amazon Bedrock, including least-privilege tool access, human approval, auditability, and failure recovery. Compare Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for eligible workloads such as regulatory review, grants, and benefits processing with FEDRAMP (Class C and D). Further explore container-based agent architectures for IL4/IL5 environments using authorized AWS services and models.

title: From First Prompt to Production: Running AWS's AI-DLC at Trillion-Token Scale (sponsored by Anaconda)
description: Bring AWS's AI-DLC methodology together with open source agents, Amazon Bedrock inference, and a governed Python foundation. Watch a full bolt run live — business intent to deployed AWS workload — with model choice, dependency provenance, and cost attribution intact. AI-native development the enterprise can actually put into production. This presentation is brought to you by Anaconda, an AWS Partner.

title: From First Workload to the Autonomous Enterprise: Transform and Scale with SAP on AWS (sponsored by SAP)
description: Agentic AI is making ERP modernization more urgent than ever. To coordinate decisions across the organization enterprise, AI must be grounded in a modern cloud ERP foundation—one that connects data, processes, business rules, and controls. ERP is no longer just where work is recorded. It has become the operational foundation that enables enterprise agentic AI and ultimately the Autonomous Enterprise.SAP and AWS are partnering to help clients accelerate their AI vision Autonomous Enterprise where people set direction, AI executes operational tasks, and organizations respond faster to change leveraging a single intelligent system with full business context. Join us to explore how SAP on AWS helps moves organizations of all sizes to move beyond isolated AI pilots to enterprise-wide outcomes delivered with reliability and confidence. This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.

title: From Gen AI to Agentic AI: Transforming Finance Operations on AWS with Barclays (sponsored by Capgemini)
description: Barclays is transforming finance operations through an AWS-powered AI platform that combines Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector knowledge bases, and Agentic AI. The platform unifies structured and unstructured finance data to automate SOX controls, enhance management reporting, enable finance data enrichment, and support intelligent decision-making across strategic finance initiatives. Built with enterprise-grade governance, explainability, and auditability, the solution helps strengthen control effectiveness, improve regulatory compliance, and accelerate reporting outcomes. Learn how AI-powered agents, explainable workflows, and governed human-in-the-loop processes are driving operational efficiency, enhancing regulatory confidence, improving audit readiness, and laying the foundation for autonomous finance operations. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: From Generic to Industry Expert: The Next Era of AI
description: AI assistants handle calendars and inboxes but fall short on domain-specific workflows. What if AI could understand your industry's systems, standards, and compliance requirements? In this session, we explore how pre-configured agents, skills, knowledge bases, and ISV connectors can address industry-specific use cases while giving customers the flexibility to extend and customize their enterprise workflows. Learn how AI assistants can go beyond a general-purpose productivity tool into a domain expert for your industry.

title: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
description: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

title: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
description: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

title: From Hours to Minutes: Fast Android Builds and Virtual Testing on AWS
description: Automotive software teams lose hours to a slow development cycle: Android builds run for hours, and testing means waiting on scarce physical target hardware. This chalk talk shows how to compress that cycle on AWS. SourceFS cuts Android build times from ~3 hours to under 5 minutes, and the Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) lets engineers test against virtual targets in the cloud instead of queuing for physical boards. We'll build up the reference architecture live, show where each piece fits, and walk through the adoption path customers are on today.

title: From Hours to Minutes: Fast Android Builds and Virtual Testing on AWS
description: Automotive software teams lose hours to a slow development cycle: Android builds run for hours, and testing means waiting on scarce physical target hardware. title: From Intention to Production: Loop Engineering with the FDE Kit
description: The AWS FDE Delivery Kit replaces linear agent pipelines with delivery loops: each program's output enriches shared state and feeds the next. Live-coding: from plain-English intention to production CDK infrastructure, Bedrock agents with guardrails, and AgentCore via re-resolve cycles.

title: From Intention to Production: Loop Engineering with the FDE Kit
description: The AWS FDE Delivery Kit replaces linear agent pipelines with delivery loops: each program's output enriches shared state and feeds the next. Live-coding: from plain-English intention to production CDK infrastructure, Bedrock agents with guardrails, and AgentCore via re-resolve cycles.

title: From Intent to Interconnection: Building Multicloud Networks in Minutes (sponsored by Equinix)
description: Modern enterprises span clouds, AI providers, private infrastructure, partners, and sovereign environments, yet networking is still built one connection at a time. Equinix Fabric One introduces a new approach: declare the business outcome you need and let the platform automatically compose the secure, resilient, any-to-any network required to deliver it. In this live demo, see how Fabric One transforms multicloud networking into an intent-driven experience. Watch a simple declaration trigger automated routing, cloud peering, encryption, resiliency, and failover across multiple providers and destinations. See how Equinix enables organizations to move from “choose, design, configure, operate” to “declare, compose, deliver.” This presentation is brought to you by Equinix, an AWS Partner.

title: From Legacy to Agentic: Modernization Beyond the Code (sponsored by SoftServe)
description: What if modernization started beyond the code? SoftServe is reimagining application modernization by working backwards from business needs and desired outcomes to determine what should change and why. In this session, see how SoftServe Agentic Application Modernization combines this outcome-driven approach with CAST Software, AWS Transform, Kiro, AI-DLC and specialized AI agents to accelerate discovery, assessment, transformation, and validation. Learn how SoftServe provides the AI foundation to orchestrate and govern these agents, turning modernization into an intelligent, repeatable journey that enables AI for organizations, connects business intent with technology decisions and execution on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by SoftServe, an AWS Partner.

title: From Manual to Autonomous: Agentic AWS Partner Growth via Quick & MCP
description: Expertise locked in SMEs doesn't scale, and manual partner operations are expensive. The answer is architectural. Amazon Quick, Partner Central MCP Server, and Marketplace AI experiences cut three costs. Cost of sales: AI Listing Experiences, prospecting and co-sell PC agents, demand generation, Funding Agents, and Express Private Offers. Cost of customer operations: Tools to manage customers at scale, auto-renewals, adoption-nudging and reporting agents. Cost of partnerships: automated AWS Specializations, onboarding and journey agents, and Partner revenue telemetry. We cover real-time SME guidance, MCP integration, and orchestration across Partner Central and Marketplace. Leave ready to build your own workflows at scale.

title: From MCP poisoning to defense: securing the agent tool supply chain
description: MCP is becoming the standard for connecting AI agents to tools, but MCP servers are packages that present supply chain risk. In this builders session, you will observe a live MCP tool poisoning attack, then build three defense layers hands-on: gateway validation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy to restrict tool actions, a pre-deployment integrity scanner that detects silent tool definition changes, and runtime monitoring that flags anomalous tool behavior. Leave with a working understanding of how MCP supply chain attacks work and how to defend against them.

title: From migration to continuous modernization: reduce tech debt at scale
description: Learn how agentic AI is transforming enterprise modernization from one-off projects into an always-on practice. In this session, we explore how organizations are accelerating cloud migration, modernizing mainframe, Windows, and custom applications, and continuously reducing tech debt across their entire portfolio, evolving their pipelines from CI/CD to CI/CD/CM (continuous modernization). See how teams are compressing modernization timelines from years to months while keeping codebases current and AI-ready. Hear from product leader Neha Goswami on the latest innovations and what's ahead.

title: From Millions of Gamers to AI at Scale: Roblox's Hybrid AWS Architecture Unleashed
description: "Auto-scaling was only the beginning. At Roblox, scaling means continuously adapting to changing capacity, hardware availability, GPU constraints, and unpredictable global demand. Join Roblox to learn how they combine AWS with on-premises infrastructure to dynamically place workloads across regions, architectures, and AI providers. Using EC2 Capacity Health Visualizer, hybrid scheduling, multi-region load balancing, self-hosted AI inference alongside Amazon Bedrock, and heterogeneous compute (x86, Graviton, Inferentia, Trainium, GPUs), you will learn how Roblox keeps gaming and AI services responsive under record-breaking load."

title: From On-Premises to Agentic AI: Bayer's Amazon Connect Transformation Journey (sponsored by Capgemini)
description: Capgemini transformed 414 contact center hotlines across more than 68 countries by replacing Cisco UCCE with Amazon Connect and introducing AgentX, an AWS-native agentic AI platform deployed across the Bayer enterprise. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, AWS Lambda, and other AWS services, AgentX delivers real-time agent assistance, automated call summarization, governance controls, predictive analytics, and autonomous workflow execution. Learn how Bayer established a "build once, deploy globally" operating model that enables consistent AI innovation across business units while reducing operational complexity, improving agent productivity, and delivering significant cost savings. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
description: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

title: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
description: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

title: From proofs to production: Neurosymbolic AI and provable security
description: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.

title: From reactive operations to autonomous resilience: How Agentic AI is redefining SRE
description: Traditional SRE was built to restore systems quickly, but today’s complex, distributed environments demand more than reactive operations. This lightning session explores how agentic AI is redefining SRE by enabling autonomous detection, decision-making, remediation, and continuous learning. It examines how observability can extend beyond infrastructure metrics to connect system health with customer experience and business outcomes. Attendees will learn how AI, observability, and operations are converging to create resilient, self-optimizing environments, why autonomous resilience is becoming a competitive advantage, and the practical steps organizations can take to progress toward Level 5 autonomous operations while retaining appropriate human oversight and governance

title: From rules to reasoning: Build an intelligent tagging compliance agent with AgentCore
description: AWS Config rules detect missing tags, but what about resources where the correct tag value isn't obvious? In this builder session, you'll create an AI agent using AgentCore that goes beyond detection to intelligent remediation. Your agent analyzes resource context, account ownership, VPC placement, creator identity, naming patterns to infer correct tag values, and handles ambiguous cases by requesting human input. Start where Config rules end: not just "is it tagged?" but "what should the tag be?"

title: From SAP to Agentic AI: Building a unified data strategy on AWS
description: This chalk talk presents a unified architecture spanning SAP Business Data Cloud, Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services. Learn how AWS enables progressive modernization from zero-copy federation via BDC Connect, to Iceberg-based lakehouse architectures, to AI-powered analytics with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and QuickSight. We introduce the AWS for SAP MCP Server, accessing OData services as AI-ready tools via Model Context Protocol. Live demos showcase AI agents resolving supply chain exceptions, generating Customer 360 insights, and accelerating BW modernization.

title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
description: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers. AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Discover battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.

title: From Signals to Action for Sempra: AI-Powered Cybersecurity on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
description: AI is reshaping cybersecurity, but security teams must act faster without adding complexity. Sempra Energy, AWS, and Accenture deployed Accenture Cyber.AI on AWS to create a unified view of cyber risk and identify the highest-priority actions across the enterprise. Learn how the team integrated existing security investments, addressed governance and architecture requirements, and operationalized AI-driven risk management. Speakers will share key design decisions, implementation lessons, and practical guidance for using AI to improve cyber resilience, strengthen security operations, and maintain control of data and infrastructure in cloud environments. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
description: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.

title: From static to self-improving agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: AI agents that learn from every production cycle deliver better outcomes without retraining or manual prompt tuning. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores live agent behavior across multiple quality dimensions and how the optimization capability discovers better system prompts and tool configurations from production traces. Learn how the agent improves continuously from production results, expert corrections, and revised context your team contributes. We'll demonstrate the full observe-evaluate-improve cycle with an underwriting agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents Framework, then discuss how the pattern applies to claims, fraud, and customer service agents.

title: From static to self-improving agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: AI agents that learn from every production cycle deliver better outcomes without retraining or manual prompt tuning. title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
description: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.

title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering At Scale
description: Most developers use AI coding assistants as interactive tools and see modest gains. A small cohort works differently: they treat agents as autonomous workers they direct and validate, and the results are a step function in productivity improvements, not an increment. In this session, we break down what these power users do differently, share success stories, where experts still find friction, and the bottlenecks coming next. We'll share demos so you leave with concrete, repeatable practices for getting orders-of-magnitude more out of Kiro agents.

title: From vulnerability to exploit to fix: closing the loop with AWS Security Services
description: You start with a deployed e-commerce web application containing OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities like SQL injection and SSRF, hardcoded credentials, and a dependency CVE. Using Amazon Inspector and AWS Continuum (formerly AWS Security Agent), you discover and validate existing flaws, reproduce the exploit chain, and push Continuum-generated fixes through CI/CD. When Amazon GuardDuty detects the active exploitation, including credential theft and prompt injection against an AI assistant, you isolate the compromised instance and harden it. Walk away with a repeatable closed-loop workflow: Inspector finds it, GuardDuty catches it, Continuum fixes it.

title: From Workloads to Agents: Rethinking Cloud Resilience (sponsored by Cohesity)
description: Under the shared responsibility model, you own the security and recoverability of your entire cloud estate - and that estate now includes AI agents. These agents are becoming core infrastructure, executing actions across interconnected systems at machine speed. Yet most organizations can't recover agent memory, credentials, or configurations any better than they could recover a corrupted server a decade ago. Join us to see how Cohesity's resilience platform extends AWS-native protections to agents and infrastructure alike, so risk doesn't outrun your ability to recover. This presentation is brought to you by Cohesity, an AWS Partner.

title: From zero to HPC: Build production clusters with AWS PCS
description: Master AWS Parallel Computing Service at re:Invent. Build fully managed compute environments with zero setup. This hands-on session covers job submission, resource optimization, and intuitive interfaces to accelerate workflows for researchers and engineers. Scale faster without the complexity.

title: Fuel Intelligent AI Agents with Trusted Enterprise Data (Sponsored by Informatica)
description: To unlock transformative business outcomes, AI agents require a foundation of trusted data with rich enterprise context. Delivering success means bridging the knowledge, trust, and action gaps across a highly complex data landscape. In this session, learn how Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) provides the comprehensive AI-ready data needed to power reliable agentic workflows. Explore how headless IDMC architecture via integrations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Agent Registry and Amazon Quick fuels agents with trusted enterprise context and end-to-end governance, driving impactful results and long-term project success.

title: Full stack development on AWS: bring your questions
description: Building modern web and mobile front ends means juggling a lot of moving parts, and everyone's stack looks a little different. This chalk talk is an open Q&A, so bring your real questions and challenges. We'll talk through how AWS Amplify helps you define backends in code and ship full-stack apps fast, how AWS AppSync powers real-time and offline data with managed GraphQL and WebSocket APIs, and how AWS Device Farm lets you test across real browsers and mobile devices before your users do. Whether you're starting a greenfield app or scaling an existing one, come ready to steer the conversation.

title: Future-Proof Your Customer Service with Salesforce, Slack and AWS (sponsored by Salesforce)
description: Modern service demands always-on, personalized experiences. See how Agentforce Service and Slack partner with Amazon Connect Customer, so you can cut handle times, costs & boost CSAT. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

title: Gatekeepers & guardrails: Secure AI agents across your nonprofit stack
description: AI agents that reach across your tools via MCP are a force multiplier — but letting an agent call OAuth-protected APIs means handling credentials, identity, and blast radius. Get it wrong and you expose sensitive data. In this code talk, deploy an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and walk through three-legged OAuth live: secure token storage via AgentCore Identity, identity propagation across agent chains, confused-deputy prevention, and guardrails on tool results. Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.

title: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
description: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves traders with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs adjacent to the matching engine with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency to the matching engine through Amazon VPC peering: bringing compute into New York Local Zone cuts round-trip latency by roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the AWS Region offers a fully managed API that also serves agentic trading systems via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever for your location-sensitive workloads.

title: GenAI chip selection: From training to inference
description: Every GenAI workload hits the same question: GPU, Trainium, Graviton, or Inferentia—and when do you use each? In this chalk talk, we walk through a practical decision tree covering model training, real-time inference, and agentic AI workloads. We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. Expect opinionated guidance, real customer math from teams that cut inference costs without sacrificing latency, and a whiteboard framework you can take back to your team on Monday.

We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. title: Give AI Agents Business Context with Genie One and Genie Ontology (sponsored by Databricks)
description: Connecting an AI agent to enterprise data is easy. Getting it to understand which tables, metrics, definitions and sources to trust is much harder. In this session, learn how Genie Ontology on Databricks combines governed semantics with context automatically learned from queries, dashboards, notebooks and connected systems, then ranks that knowledge by relevance and authority while enforcing user permissions. See how Genie One uses this shared context to reason over live structured and unstructured data, call tools through MCP, take action and deliver more accurate results with less costly agentic exploration on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

title: Give Your Best Engineers Back to the Roadmap, Not the Pager (sponsored by NeuBird AI)
description: Forty percent of engineering time goes to firefighting instead of the roadmap you funded. The problem isn’t a lack of dashboards or headcount, it’s that these engineers are forced to act as the glue across these fragmented tools. Between incidents, an autonomous Production Ops Agent keeps working. It deepens its model of your environment, right sizes observability spend, and turns every incident into a captured fix nobody has to relearn. This session shows how NeuBird AI has helped teams recover 200 plus engineering hours a month and cut incident costs 60 percent or more, not by hiring more people or buying more dashboards, but by giving one agent the job of running production so your senior engineers can go back to building it. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird AI, an AWS Partner.

title: Giving Your AI Agent a Wallet: The Architecture of Spend Control
description: AI agents can now hold a wallet and pay for APIs, data, and even other agents. The demo takes a few hours; making it safe to ship takes much longer. At the whiteboard, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, x402 micropayments, and Cedar policy, we design an agent that spends under a hard budget, then break it together. We work through where guardrails belong, why session limits aren't enough, custodial versus non-custodial tradeoffs, and human-in-the-loop without human-in-the-way. Bring your edge cases. You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.

You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.

title: Go from Code to Deployed Agent with AgentCore CLI
description: Go from zero to a deployed, observable AI agent in under an hour. Use the AgentCore CLI to scaffold a Strands agent with a custom tool, test it locally against the Runtime contract, then deploy to AgentCore Runtime via CDK. Invoke the agent to demonstrate session isolation, inspect automatic CloudWatch logs and X-Ray traces, and confirm the framework-agnostic contract by replacing the agent with a plain Python function.

title: Go Hack Yourself. With AI. (sponsored by Horizon3.ai)
description: Defenders often drown in noise while attackers move at machine speed. To truly secure your environment, you must adopt an attacker’s perspective. Horizon3 CEO Snehal Antani shares insights from 250,000+ autonomous pentests across 6,000+ environments, demonstrating how AI hackers find exploitable paths that scanners miss, such as credential theft and domain compromise without CVEs. You’ll learn why vulnerable doesn’t mean exploitable, how to validate controls through a Hack-Fix-Verify loop, and where AI belongs in offense and defense: tool for scale and proof, not a black box. This presentation is brought to you by Horizon3.ai, an AWS Partner.

title: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
description: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you own the loop or let AWS handle it? We build one on-call responder three ways: an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a managed loop with built-in memory and tool routing, AgentCore Runtime for full control, and AWS DevOps Agent as a batteries-included DevOps harness. Then we build the shape most teams land in: your own orchestrator, DevOps Agent composed in headless over remote MCP and A2A. Bring your challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.

title: Golden Opportunities: Unlocking Business Value with Agentic AI (sponsored by Atos)
description: Companies have shifted from talking about agents to putting them to work, but moving from an AWS Bedrock AgentCore demo to a governed, production multi-agent system inside a regulated enterprise isn't a straight line. Atos will show what that path looks like, where it breaks, and how to fix it. What you'll learn ⮚Enterprise patterns that separate successful AWS agentic AI deployments from stalled pilots ⮚Building a governance layer on Amazon Bedrock that regulated industries will approve ⮚How GSI partners turn ideas into completed, production-ready deployments ⮚Where AWS tooling is mature, where it's still evolving, and how to architect around the gaps This presentation is brought to you by Atos, an AWS Partner.

title: Go-Live to ROI: How Partners Turn Customer Outcomes into Revenue
description: The partners thriving in the AI era aren't the ones who just deploy, they're the ones who prove impact. The Business Value Realization (BVR) motion is how consulting and managed services partners are building their next growth engine: documenting outcomes, unlocking milestone-based funding, and turning deployments into expansion revenue. Explore how BVR helps partners quantify ROI, earn a new Competency, build customer success practices that drive revenue beyond go-live, and where the motion is heading next. As AI moves from pilot to production, the partners who own the value conversation won't just retain customers, they'll shape what is built next.

title: Gotta detect 'em all: finding rogue devices with Amazon Bedrock
description: Participants build and command autonomous drone fleets to identify rogue devices using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS IoT Greengrass, and Strands Agents. This gamified scenario showcases a Human-Machine Teaming architecture in which AI operates autonomously within defined trust boundaries, with human-in-the-loop escalation at configurable confidence thresholds.

title: Governance foundations for AI workloads that grow into autonomous agents
description: Agentic workloads are reaching production, and governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. This session shows how to build a governance foundation for AI with AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to autonomous agents. You apply preventive and detective controls to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence, and map controls to frameworks such as ISO 42001. The same controls hold whether the workload is a single model call or a fleet of agents acting on their own.

title: Govern and optimize AI agents for desktop work on WorkSpaces
description: Your most valuable business processes often run inside desktop applications and mainframes that expose no APIs for AI agents to call. In this session, learn how to use Amazon WorkSpaces to give agents a governed desktop where they operate these applications directly, just as an employee would. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into scoping what agents are permitted to do, auditing agent actions, and configuring agent identity. We'll walk through strategies for agent optimization:  how to choose the right agent tools, select the right model for your workflow, and build reusable agent skills. Applied together, these techniques cut task time, lower cost, and increase the accuracy of your agent workflows.

title: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
description: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.

title: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
description: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.

title: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
description: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.

title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
description: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
description: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

title: Governing hundreds of accounts in seconds: agentic AI meets Landing Zone operations
description: When you manage hundreds of AWS accounts, governance can fall behind. Drift accumulates, controls take days to propagate, and problems go undetected until something breaks. We demonstrate Landing Zone Accelerator 2.0 with built-in AI that lets operators use natural language to apply organizational changes in minutes, if not seconds. We deploy org-wide security controls, provision accounts, and enforce encryption through a Bedrock-powered interface supporting CloudFormation and Terraform. An AI agent generates each change plan, and before anything is applied, an org-wide preview catches conflicts and policy violations. Issues are surfaced up front instead of discovered after a break. Attendees learn how we built LZA 2.0 with Kiro spec-driven development and Rust, and how to design pre-deployment previews that keep multi-account operations safe.

title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
description: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways single-node debugging never taught you: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass every health check yet corrupt your results. In this hands-on builders session, you diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults before your jobs do. You leave with a failure-signature runbook and a triage method distilled from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

title: Graviton5: Migrate your workloads, cut costs, get better performance
description: AWS Graviton5 delivers up to 25% better compute performance than the previous generation, features caches up to five times larger, and offers some of the fastest memory performance available in the cloud. But what do those improvements actually mean for your workloads? In this session, we go beyond the spec sheet into real-world benchmarks across databases, web applications, and ML inference. Hear from a customer who migrated production workloads across multiple Graviton generations and the compounding performance and cost gains they achieved. Walk away with concrete performance data and a practical framework to evaluate Graviton5 for your own migration.

title: Grounding LLMs in Truth: Build a Live Fact-Checking Pipeline
description: Walk through the reference architecture of a real-time fact-checking pipeline built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how a live audio stream is turned into fact-by-fact verdicts (true, misleading, or false), with source citing at broadcast-compatible latency. Learn how to build it yourself using a chain of specialized agents on AgentCore, hybrid search on Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and custom tool-use hooks. Leave with a mapped path to create a reference architecture, plus answers to the concrete design questions blocking you such as: agent sharding, tabular corpus indexing, guardrails, and streaming reasoning to the UI.

title: Grow Adoption Where Customers Work with AWS Bedrock and Quick
description: Your customers increasingly live inside an AI work surface, and your product needs to be there too. In this hands-on session, you'll take a SaaS product—its API and a simple agentic capability—and bring it into Amazon Quick using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll adapt it for AgentCore, wire up secure identity, then build Chat Agents, Research, Flows, and Apps that put your product's intelligence in front of users. Customers get your whole product in Quick, as-is. Walk out with a working reference pattern and the ability to spin up POCs for product leadership.

title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
description: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
description: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

title: Guardrails for AI-generated Serverless infrastructure
description: Coding agents generate full serverless architectures in seconds, but without guardrails they produce over-permissioned IAM policies, skip encryption at rest, and deploy resources that violate your organization's tagging and cost policies. In this chalk talk, discuss operational controls for AI-generated infrastructure: automated security reviews that catch policy violations before deployment, cost estimation gates that flag unexpected spend, compliance checks against organizational standards, and MCP server configurations that enforce service boundaries and naming conventions. We whiteboard which guardrails to automate versus which require human review, and where teams are getting the balance wrong.

title: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
description: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Transform's agentic AI compresses that timeline, from migration inventory to fully deployed, validated landing zones and modernized networks. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

title: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
description: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
description: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium—covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization—all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. Leave with the skills to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
description: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium—covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization—all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. Leave with the skills to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

title: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
description: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open weight models, and Amazon Bedrock.

title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
description: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and the AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration — apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. In this hands-on session, fine-tune a transformer-based world model, implement parameter-efficient training strategies, and deploy trained agents for real-time inference. Leave with practical skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents at scale.

title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
description: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and the AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration — apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization.
