title: Hands-On Workshop: Build & Deploy AI Agents with Cloudera Agent Studio (sponsored by Cloudera)
description: Join this exclusive hands-on workshop to master building and deploying high-impact AI agents with Cloudera Agent Studio. Move from experimentation to production using trusted data, scalable workflows, and governed infrastructure. Led by Cloudera solution architects, you will build multi-agent workflows without code, develop agentic chatbots for data access, learn Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration with AWS tools including Amazon Bedrock and PuppyGraph, and explore the latest Cloudera AI and Workbench enhancements. Designed for data scientists, developers, engineers, and analysts ready to enable secure, scalable, open AI across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
description: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI, but they struggle to move from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent, progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll create a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.

title: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
description: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI, but they struggle to move from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent, progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll create a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.

title: How AI-native startups run untrusted agent code on Lambda MicroVMs
description: AI agents increasingly generate and execute untrusted code that needs a safe, isolated place to run. A growing set of AI-native startups and ISVs are converging on one pattern: one MicroVM per agent session, spun up on demand, torn down when the work is done. In this session, see how [Customer] built production agent sandboxes on Lambda MicroVMs, walking through the full lifecycle that delivers hardware-level isolation per session. See how they scale to thousands of concurrent sandboxes and the operational tradeoffs they navigated to get there.

title: How AI-Powered DevSecOps Fueled Intuitive Machines' Race to the Moon (sponsored by GitLab)
description: In 2019, Intuitive Machines won a NASA contract to land a spacecraft near the Moon's south pole — with five years to build every system from scratch and a team of just 50 developers. Join James Blakeslee, Vice President of Engineering at Intuitive Machines, as he shares how the team used AI-powered DevSecOps to ship mission-critical software fast enough to become the first U.S. venture in 50 years — and the first commercial company ever — to land intact on the Moon. You'll learn how they're now using GitLab Duo Agent Platform and Amazon Bedrock to accelerate development toward their next lunar lander. This presentation is brought to you by GitLab, an AWS Partner.

title: How a state agency transformed constituent services with Connect Customer
description: When the Georgia Department of Community Supervision needed to modernize their contact center, they turned to Amazon Connect Customer and AI. In this session, hear firsthand how AI-powered call analysis, real-time transcription, and automated case notes are changing the way officers and staff handle daily interaction. We share lessons learned from discovery through implementation, including how to prioritize high-impact AI use cases and build stakeholder buy-in across a state agency. You’ll leave with actionable strategies to bring AI-powered constituent services to your own agency.

title: How AWS Continuum validates security findings across the SDLC
description: AWS Continuum embeds security expertise at every stage of the software development lifecycle: AWS Continuum reviews architecture documents, AWS Continuum scans pull requests and full repositories, and AWS Continuum can pentest deployed applications. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into how AWS Continuum coordinates multiple analysis passes with built-in safety guardrails and multi-step validation to deliver high-confidence findings. Bring your questions about integrating security into CI/CD pipelines and scaling AppSec across multiple teams.

title: How Bayer Designed 50K Proteins on Amazon Bio Discovery
description: This chalk talk explores how to architect agentic AI workflows for generative protein design at enterprise scale. Using Bayer's oncology nanobody campaign as the reference implementation, we walk through the technical and scientific decisions behind a pipeline that generated 50,000 candidates and 3,000 prioritized candidates in weeks using Amazon Bio Discovery. Topics include: model orchestration patterns for generative and predictive models, designing scoring functions that encode biological mechanism (not just binding affinity), iterative feedback loops between computation and wet-lab validation, and scaling considerations for enterprise drug discovery programs. Attendees will leave this session with a reusable architectural blueprint for building agentic biomolecule design workflows on AWS.

title: How Bayer modernized R&D analytics into an agentic decision engine
description: Bayer's R&D analytics relied on manual pipelines, fragmented tooling, and engineering-heavy workflows that bottlenecked scientists. In this session, hear how Bayer modernized that stack into an agentic decision engine on AWS, cutting token costs by roughly 600% and saving scientists 70% of their engineering time. We'll trace the modernization journey from legacy analytics architecture through the migration to cloud-native services and show how that foundation enabled autonomous multi-agent workflows that now orchestrate R&D decisions at enterprise scale. Leave with a framework for modernizing analytics into agentic AI capabilities.

title: How Blue Origin built a centralized enterprise knowledge graph on AWS
description: Building enterprise AI applications shouldn't require every team to reinvent the wheel — standing up data pipelines, managing security, and keeping knowledge bases current. Blue Origin faced this at scale: dozens of teams, hundreds of data sources, and growing demand for AI apps that could reason across all of it. The answer was RAGNet — a centralized enterprise knowledge graph platform built on Amazon Neptune and Amazon Bedrock that aggregates structured and unstructured data into a secure, always-current graph any developer or AI agent can query in plain natural language.

title: How Bridgewater Associates uses agentic SDLC to accelerate change
description: Learn how Bridgewater Associates, a leading macroeconomic investment manager, built an agentic SDLC platform that transformed the way technology and investment teams work by leveraging AI agents to automate the software development lifecycle. Built as an AI teammate in Slack and powered by an orchestration service running these agents in secure sandboxes, the platform automates every stage of the SDLC—from idea inception through merge requests in GitLab to deploying code that generates investment signals. Amazon Bedrock powers their coding agents, orchestration stages, and custom agents built using agent SDKs. This session will also discuss integration with AWS frontier agents like AWS DevOps Agent.

title: How Citizens Bank reimagined CX with Amazon Connect Customer & GenAI
description: Citizens Financial Group is transforming its customer service ecosystem using Amazon Connect Customer, Amazon Lex, and generative AI. In this session, learn how Citizens migrated legacy IVR and contact center infrastructure to Amazon Connect Customer, deployed conversational AI across voice and digital channels, and integrated generative AI-powered agent assist and real-time conversation intelligence. We cover the solution architecture spanning Amazon Connect Customer, Amazon Lex, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge, along with measurable outcomes in containment rates, handle time, and routing accuracy. Attendees will gain a practical blueprint for enterprise-scale customer experience transformation in financial services.

title: How Context Graphs Cut AI Token Usage by Up to 70% (sponsored by Sphinx AI)
description: Context graphs can reduce token usage by up to 70% while maintaining accuracy. This session explores how context graphs help AI agents understand relationships, definitions, and business meaning across enterprise data. We will look at how context graphs capture knowledge that traditional data models miss, and how organizations are applying them. You will see real examples of the architecture and results involved in giving AI the context it needs to reason effectively. This presentation is brought to you by Sphinx AI, an AWS Partner.

title: How Cox Achieved 7x ROI with Agentic AI on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
description: Cox Communications partnered with Accenture and Anthropic's Claude on AWS to transform B2B marketing and sales, generating a 7x return on its first-year AI investment. By deploying AI-powered marketing and sales agents across 120 micro-industries and eight customer segments, Cox replaced one-size-fits-all campaigns with personalized engagement at scale. The initiative delivered 55% faster speed to market, a 2-point increase in B2B conversion, 40% higher campaign efficiency, and an 86% reduction in lead management costs while improving data accuracy from 18% to 97%. Today, Cox is operating an end-to-end agentic go-to-market system with human oversight. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: How Delta Air Lines achieved always-on code modernization
description: Every enterprise carries the same growing list: outdated dependencies, end-of-life runtimes, and security vulnerabilities that nobody has time to fix. In this session, learn how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to find these issues across your entire portfolio and fix them without waiting for a human to intervene. We'll cover how to maintain a living inventory of what needs upgrading, prioritize by risk, and automate remediation at scale. Hear how Delta Air Lines drove autonomous remediation across 100+ development teams, turning tech debt from a never-ending backlog into an always-on process.

title: How Deutsche Bahn made 10 years of cloud modernization pay off in AI
description: You've invested in cloud. Maybe migrated. Maybe modernized. Your board wants AI yesterday, but 88% of companies use AI and only 1% believe they're at maturity. The gap isn't infrastructure. It's whether your organization can move fast enough. In this fireside chat, an AWS executive-in-residence sits down with Deutsche Bahn leadership to unpack how they built that speed: 550+ autonomous teams, AWS migration completed 18 months early, and enterprise-scale agentic AI now in production. You'll leave with: (1) what "AI-ready" requires beyond cloud, (2) a governance model for agents at scale, and (3) a framework for pilot to all-in.

title: How Elevance Health Built a Trusted Data Foundation for AI-Native Member Experiences
description: Members shouldn't have to navigate fragmented systems to understand their benefits and find the right care. Serving 46 million members, Elevance Health designed for the holistic experience by building a governed semantic and data foundation that unifies clinical, claims, pharmacy, and member-services data so AI agents can reason accurately across domains. Attendees will hear why Elevance set out on this work, how it built the foundation on AWS, and how agentic workflows now deliver more coordinated, personalized guidance for members, providers, and associates across the care journey. The session closes with lessons learned and practical guidance for other payers under a governed deployment model for regulated healthcare.

title: How Emirates built Multicloud Agents with open-source Agentic AI Gateway
description: Enterprises running AI agents across multiple clouds face fragmented model access, inconsistent pricing, and vendor lock-in. Open-source Gateways provide a unified interface to orchestrate Models across Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI based on use-case requirements and token economics. This session demonstrates how Emirates built a multi-cloud agent architecture using an open-source Agentic AI Gateway as the routing layer and Bedrock as the primary backbone. Learn patterns for cost-based routing, fallback strategies, model selection by capability, and unified observability across model and cloud providers.

title: How Fidelity built a cloud-agnostic AI Gateway
description: Fidelity Asset Management runs 40+ LLM models across AWS, Azure, and GCP, serving 100K+ daily requests to 20 business units. Rather than building separate integrations per provider, they built a cloud-agnostic AI gateway that provides a single abstraction layer for model access, governance, and observability. Learn how Fidelity Asset Management implemented three-tier rate limiting, centralized audit logging, fine-grained access controls, and real-time cost tracking across all providers without sacrificing developer velocity. Attendees will leave with a reusable pattern for building governed, multi-cloud AI platforms in regulated industries.

title: How FINRA automated dependency lifecycle management with AI agents
description: With 2,300 components and over 700,000 dependencies, FINRA uses Kiro and AWS Transform custom to deploy GenAI upgrade agents across Python, Java, and Angular. Learn how governed automation and monthly "Transform-a-thons" reclaimed 1,800 engineering hours across 25 teams in three months, and how to shift from reactive patching to predictable dependency lifecycle management. Discover how FINRA's move to continuous modernization reduces the effort of maintaining technical debt.

title: How FINRA Brings Governed Agentic AI to Its Member Firms on AWS
description: FINRA protects investors and enforces regulation for 3,400+ broker-dealer firms and 1.2 million financial professionals, so regulation must evolve as fast as the markets it oversees. FINRA is exploring the role agentic AI services like Amazon Quick can play on FINRA’s Gateway, its primary external platform serving firms. This session covers the how: the design patterns and guardrails for responsible AI in a regulated environment, including draft-and-attest human accountability, data grounding with hallucination detection, tenant isolation, and a pragmatic governance model. Behind that experience, FINRA keeps models and frameworks interchangeable, so capabilities evolve without rebuilding. Leave with a practical framework for governing agentic AI at scale.

title: How Hertz Made Karpenter Smarter with autonomous AI-Driven Optimization (sponsored by Cast AI)
description: Hertz used Cast AI agents to make Karpenter much smarter: the agents autonomously analyze every workload, rightsize it, then continuously instruct Karpenter how to rearrange nodes to cut waste. Hertz's platform engineering team deployed this across their multi-cluster EKS fleet entirely through Terraform. Sonal will show the real numbers: where the extra savings hid, how infrastructure-as-code took onboarding from pre-dev to production, and what it takes to automate cost optimization at fleet scale without babysitting it. This presentation is brought to you by Cast AI, an AWS Partner.

title: How Iberdrola Increased Marketing Capacity 4x with Agentic AI (sponsored by Accenture)
description: Iberdrola, a Spanish multinational electric utility company, is transforming marketing with CreatIA, an agentic AI platform co-developed with Accenture and AWS. Facing rising demand for content, faster decisions and accelerated campaign delivery, Iberdrola adopted a new operating model powered by specialized AI agents across the marketing lifecycle. CreatIA unifies market intelligence, insights generation, content creation, validation and campaign activation in a single enterprise platform. The solution has reduced time spent analyzing and processing information by 80%, accelerated strategic decision making by 40%, increased creative production capacity by up to four times, and reduced content production costs by 60%. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: How IT leaders actually pulled off their cloud migrations
description: How did other organizations get their on-premises environments to AWS? In this panel, migration leaders from global organizations share exactly how they did it, including those moving off VMware and other aging infrastructure. You'll hear the real planning decisions, execution strategies, and lessons learned that made their transitions successful. They'll also share where they're headed next with modernization and innovation. Whether you're just getting started or pushing past roadblocks, you'll leave with proven strategies and practical insights to accelerate your own cloud migration.

title: How Jack in the Box delivers personalized store reporting at scale
description: Franchise operators run restaurants, not BI tools. In this session, learn how Jack in the Box delivered store-specific performance reports and actionable insights straight to every operator's inbox across 2,100+ locations. We'll cover throttle-aware parallel orchestration, failure isolation patterns, and how this approach turns business intelligence into a scalable, zero-friction communication channel that drives operator engagement and revenue. Walk away with a reusable blueprint for high-volume, per-location reporting in any multi-unit retail or restaurant business

title: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
description: Learn how Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent’s memory lifecycle. See how Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes, such as successful build commands or rejected pull requests. Explore how it consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, and retrieves only relevant context for tasks. You’ll also learn how provenance keeps memories auditable and correctable, how memory stays consistent across IDE, CLI, and web, how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, and how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes.

title: How leading AI builders push the frontier with AWS Trainium
description: Hear from four AI leaders building experiences that didn't exist a year ago: real-time video generation, world models, physical AI, and LLMs for drug discovery. These breakthroughs demand both high performance and low cost to work at all. AWS Trainium helped turn that future into production reality. Each panelist walks through their use case: the specific technical barrier they hit, how they used Trainium to get past it, and what shipping it to customers unlocked.

title: How LG U+ cut migration time 50% with AI-powered app refactoring
description: Moving servers to the cloud without modernizing the applications on them just moves your technical debt to a new address. LG U+ needed to modernize applications before they could migrate them, and doing both sequentially would have taken too long. In this session, LG U+ shares how they ran AI-powered modernization and migration in parallel across 87 systems spanning 1,579 virtual servers and 107 physical servers. The result: roughly 20% migration velocity improvement and a 50% reduction in Java migration time through AI-assisted refactoring. You'll learn how to modernize at scale without slowing down the move.

title: How LSEG Built a Multicloud Internal Developer Platform with Kubernetes and AI
description: At London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), deploying enterprise workloads traditionally took weeks or months of onboarding, governance, networking, and operational setup. In this session, we’ll share how a small AI-augmented engineering team built RouteOne: LSEG’s fully managed multicloud application platform, enabling developers to deploy compliant workloads across multiple cloud providers in minutes by committing their code and a single YAML definition. We’ll explore the Kubernetes-based control plane, enterprise guardrails, and AI-native developer experience powered by APIs, MCP and agent skills. We’ll also share lessons learned from using AI-assisted engineering practices to rapidly deliver a lean, enterprise-grade platform in a regulated environment.

title: How Mercedes-Benz accelerates engineering and production with AI
description: Mercedes-Benz is using agentic AI on AWS to transform how vehicles are brought to life, from engineering to production. Hear how Mercedes-Benz is using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to accelerate engineering for 14,000 engineers—building specialized AI agents that reason over millions of interconnected artifacts, compressing specification generation by 90%, from 35 weeks to 3.5. On the factory floor, discover how Mercedes used AWS to build a fully cloud-native manufacturing execution system orchestrating 1M+ vehicles annually, with AI-powered quality intelligence providing rapid root-cause analysis and digital twins helping optimize throughput. Walk away with real-world lessons for deploying industrial AI at scale.

title: How Moeve turned natural language into enforced governance controls
description: Translating compliance requirements such as GDPR or NIS2 into enforceable controls usually means writing policy by hand. Moeve built a Governance Control AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock to change that. You see how engineers ask questions in natural language and the system turns their intent into SCPs, hooks, and AWS Config rules assigned at OU and account scope, validated through CI/CD and GitOps. Moeve shares the architecture and what it learned running the assistant in production.

title: How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic
description: Organizations want to automate enforcement of critical rules—financial, legal, regulatory—yet those rules live in ambiguous natural-language documents. Bridging this gap is error-prone and expensive. In this session, we show how neurosymbolic AI enables subject-matter experts to formalize natural-language rules into mathematical logic—capturing the original intent in an unambiguous, executable, and verifiable form. We cover the mathematical foundations and demonstrate through practical examples how formalized rules can serve as agent guardrails, compliance checks, and trusted knowledge sources. Attendees will leave with a deep understanding of how neurosymbolic techniques can help them formalize and operationalize their own domain rules.

title: How Nordstrom, Coca-Cola Andina & Mondelez use agentic supply chains
description: Supply chain leaders are moving from dashboards that report problems to agents that resolve them, sensing disruption, optimizing routing, and acting in real time. Hear how three retail and CPG leaders deployed agentic AI on AWS at scale. Nordstrom built a multi-agent framework on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, starting with an agent that cut audit investigations from five weeks to thirty seconds. Coca-Cola Andina developed Miruta, a multi-agent routing solution optimizing supply chain operations across its bottling network. And Mondelez is modernizing production and distribution across 150+ countries. Each shares their architecture, what changed for their teams, and measurable results.

title: How Novartis is Reimaging an AI-Native Drug Development with AWS
description: Developing a new medicine takes 10 to 15 years and $2.6 billion, and timelines are getting longer. Novartis decided not to optimize the old model but to replace it, building an AI-native ecosystem spanning information, decision, and physical AI across the drug development lifecycle. In this session, hear how AI now writes over 80% of their RWE protocols in production, then go deep on intelligent decision systems that optimize clinical trial planning, and formulation optimisations that improve the medicines Novartis creates. Learn how Novartis and AWS are compressing the path from AI prototype to production, turning ambition into patient impact.

title: How Observability Evolved From Dashboards to Agents Writing Code (sponsored by Honeycomb)
description: Observability's real job has always been closing the feedback loop between what you ship and what happens next. We'll trace how that loop evolved at Honeycomb: from dashboards you stared at, to SLOs that quantified what mattered, to Canvas, agents that investigate with you, and now MCP tools feeding production reality straight back into software written by agents This presentation is brought to you by Honeycomb, an AWS Partner.

title: How Paytm powers millions of customer journeys with AI agents on AWS
description: Every Paytm customer and merchant leaves a trail—payments, transfers, loans, logins, chats, and voice conversations. Together, these events form a story. Pi Agents, Paytm's multimodal agentic platform on AWS, turns that story into action across acquisition, retention, monetization, and support for 50M+ merchants and 80M+ monthly users. A Paytm-built foundation model learns from 100B+ activity sequences, while specialized SLMs and voice models enable sub-second interactions across 10+ languages. Beyond the customer lifecycle, Pi Agents powers sales, marketing, support, and operations. This session explores how Paytm combines these models with agents to understand, decide, and act.

title: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
description: Premium animated series traditionally take 3.5 years to produce. Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months, with plans to extend support to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, and feature films. The suite is powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, and evaluate outputs. Learn how Prime Video trains and serves their first-party diffusion model fleet on Amazon SageMaker and EKS, running on Amazon EC2 P6 GPU clusters for production-grade throughput and latency.

title: How Rail Operators Are Using Agentic AI to Improve Service Reliability (sponsored by PwC)
description: Many organizations successfully pilot generative AI but struggle to scale adoption. Rail operators worldwide are now exploring how agentic AI can transform mission-critical operations and improve service reliability. Deutsche Bahn (DB) and Norfolk Southern are among the organizations leading this journey. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, they are transforming rail operations through AI agents embedded into the systems that support daily operations across their transportation networks. The solution combines AI agents and human oversight to automate incident resolution, support operations teams, and improve service reliability. This session explores the journey from proof of concept to production, the governance and safety guardrails required for adoption, and how lighthouse programs are becoming blueprints for enterprise-wide agentic process transformation. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: How Ramp tracks and governs AI spend down to the team, model, and API key
description: When AI token spend spans multiple providers and dozens of teams, knowing who spent what, on which model, and whether it's COGS or OpEx requires its own pipeline. We'll cover ingesting usage data from third-party AI APIs, processing with Temporal workers, persisting on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, running on Amazon ECS Fargate, and surfacing anomalies before they hit your invoice. See how Ramp attributes spend by provider, model, team, and API key, and attributes cost down to the request-level when teams connect their router, gateway, or internal data. Learn how Ramp separates COGS from OpEx for accurate unit economics, then closes the loop with governance.

title: How Santander governs hundreds of AI agents in production on Amazon Bedrock
description: Financial institutions need a consistent way for independent teams to build, deploy, and govern AI agents without creating silos or losing visibility. In this session, learn how Banco Santander built Santander Cortex—a self-service platform where business teams configure, deploy, and monitor their own AI agents with tools, knowledge bases, memory, guardrails, and authorization using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We'll cover identity integration, agent-to-agent (A2A) interoperability across independently owned teams, and the governance model that made self-service possible without losing control. The platform runs hundreds of agents, including customer-facing chatbots serving millions of users across more than 10 countries.

title: How Securian Uses Agentic AI to Prioritize CIO Investments (sponsored by PwC)
description: CIOs face a question: where should they invest next to strengthen technology capabilities? Securian Financial Group and PwC built an agentic AI Capability Maturity Measurement Instrument (CMMI) engine using Amazon Quick that turns evidence into a repeatable view of capability gaps, investment priorities, and recommendations across 20 IT domains and 2,000+ capability criteria. The solution ingests documents and surveys, applies consistent scoring, and translates results into prioritized actions spanning skills, resources, processes, and tools. Learn how Securian moved from periodic, manual assessments to an on-demand decision engine that helps technology leaders' direct investment where it matters most. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: How startups ship faster with Kiro
description: Startups live and die by velocity. Small teams, big ambitions, and no time to waste. In this session, hear how fast-moving startups are using Kiro to punch above their weight: turning ideas into working software with spec-driven and agentic development, keeping a lean team focused on product instead of boilerplate, and shipping features that would normally demand far more engineers. We'll describe real patterns startups use to move from concept to production quickly, and share practical takeaways any team can apply. Whether you're a founder, an early engineer, or scaling quickly, learn how agentic development helps small teams build big.

title: How Stripe built an enterprise agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: Operating global payments infrastructure requires AI that is secure, reliable, and scalable across internal and customer-facing experiences. Learn how Stripe built a shared agent platform for Kai, its company-wide AI coworker, and hundreds of other AI workflows. Stripe will share how it integrated Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter with its existing infrastructure, data-access controls, and security model. Discover the architectural decisions that helped Stripe move rapidly from prototype to company-wide adoption, supporting more than 10,000 employees and nearly 500,000 Kai sessions each week.

title: How TeleTracking runs AWS at a 30:1 ratio with Grafana Cloud AI (sponsored by Grafana Labs)
description: TeleTracking's platform is air traffic control for hospitals: 200K+ beds and 100+ command centers depend on it. Re-platforming onto an AI-native foundation has taken its service-to-engineer ratio from 6:1 to 30:1. The lever isn't headcount: It’s relying on one agent to pair gcx and the Grafana Cloud MCP server with AWS MCP tooling. Oren Lion replays an MSK incident where Grafana Assistant identified a cluster-wide broker disruption in minutes, pairing Frontend Observability with Amazon CloudFront to line up what hurt with what changed. He closes with Assistant Investigations, read-only guardrails, and a recipe you can run yourself.. This presentation is brought to you by Grafana Labs, an AWS Partner.

title: How the Air Force defends DoD workloads with Amazon Bedrock Agents
description: AWS built STORMS with the Air Force SOC to defend DoD workloads across AWS accounts in multiple Organizations - pairing centralized security telemetry and one-click containment with a multi-agent Amazon Bedrock system that analyzes logs, answers analyst questions, and executes containment actions.

title: How the most advanced teams manage the full SDLC on an agentic stack (sponsored by Cursor)
description: This 201 technical deep dive covers the AI Software Development Lifecycle featuring the Grok product family. SpaceXAI experts and customers in production will demo proven patterns, covering which parts of the SDLC to delegate to agents first, how to structure review and testing when agents write most of the code, and where the Grok API and Grok Voice fit a production workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

title: How to assess your environment to migrate & modernize with confidence
description: Without a clear picture of what's running in your environment, teams carry forward outdated assumptions, inherit unplanned tech debt, and miss the fastest path to value. Assessment is the foundational step that sets everything else up for success. Learn how to go hands-on with AWS Transform, an agentic assessment experience that delivers results fast, or work with AWS specialists and partners who leverage this technology alongside decades of migration experience. Use assessment data to make informed decisions, optimize environments, and eliminate redundant licensing.

title: How to build an autonomous compliance environment auditors trust
description: Auditors require evidence of compliance on demand. Learn how to keep your AWS environment audit-ready at all times, continuously producing the proof auditors need, without manual intervention. Across services such as AWS Config, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Security Hub and more, we walk through an architecture that automatically collects evidence, maps it to your control frameworks, checks whether the collected evidence meets control requirements, identifies gaps and delivers prescriptive guidance to close each gap. We finish with how AI agents now investigate findings, draft remediations, and defend evidence to auditors, moving compliance from continuous monitoring to continuous resolution.

title: How to Build Autonomous Enterprise Agents with SOPs using Kiro and Bedrock AgentCore
description: Enterprise operations hit a limitation when humans can't keep up with the volume of exceptions in ERP systems like SAP which is solved by autonomous AI agents. In this session, learn how to build production agents by writing SOPs in natural language. We'll cover how to write SOPs that let agents exercise judgment while embedding guardrails. A single SOP becomes a deployable agent, and this pattern scales across different business processes. Using Kiro's spec-driven development and Strands agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, partners own the full agent lifecycle and differentiate by layering domain expertise and industry-specific IP into SOPs. Walk away with hands-on experience building the agentic architecture that enables autonomous enterprise operations for your customers.

description: Enterprise operations hit a limitation when humans can't keep up with the volume of exceptions in ERP systems like SAP which is solved by autonomous AI agents. Walk away with hands-on experience building the agentic architecture that enables autonomous enterprise operations for your customers.

title: How to Build Omni-Channel AI Agents with Twilio + AWS (sponsored by Twilio)
description: Orchestrating AI conversations across channels requires more than just connecting APIs. Learn how to build agents that understand context, respond instantly, and adapt to channel constraints. Explore Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock integration patterns, plus the operational playbook for deploying engagement AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Twilio, an AWS Partner.

title: How to decompose Oracle and SQL Server into purpose-built databases
description: A monolithic traditional RDBMS databases serves transactions, reporting, and search, but serves none of them well. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard how to decompose a proprietary database into purpose-built layers on AWS, including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for transactional workloads, Aurora pgvector for semantic search and GenAI (RAG), and Amazon Redshift via zero-ETL for real-time analytics, for a smarter modernization approach. We'll walk through how this pattern eliminates licensing costs, removes ETL pipelines, and turns your operational data into an AI-ready platform. Come ready to whiteboard your decomposition use case.

title: How to Deploy Purpose-Built Clinical AI Agents to Production with Speed and Scale
description: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

title: How to Govern an agent fleet: auto-approve the routine, escalate the ambiguous
description: Your teams are building agents faster than anyone can review them by hand, and that creates operational and security risk along with the visibility problem. In this workshop, you build a layered controls stack for an agent fleet. You enforce content and business-logic boundaries with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, apply an evaluator pattern for policy validation, and track compliance posture with AWS Config conformance packs. Then you connect these into an operating model that approves routine actions automatically and sends only the ambiguous ones to a person, so you can deploy more agents than your team could review individually.

title: How to improve your security and governance maturity and prove it to your auditor
description: With so many security best practices available, knowing what to do first is a challenge. In this session, you learn how to use the AWS Security Maturity Model to systematically identify and prioritize security improvements for your AWS workloads through a phased approach. You discover how to extend your governance capabilities to manage security consistently across multi-cloud environments. Finally, you see how automatic evidence collection helps you continuously demonstrate compliance to auditors, turning security posture into provable assurance.

title: How to run parallel coding agents without sitting in the loop (sponsored by Cursor)
description: Running multiple coding agents in parallel can increase throughput, but only if technical leads and engineers avoid being pulled into every agent’s execution loop. Join this session to learn how Grok Bot is an orchestration layer for technical knowledge work, coordinating workflows while saving time and mitigating costs. Through live demos, see Grok Bot operate from its own VM and browser, maintain authenticated tool access, monitor usage, and provision cloud agents on demand. We’ll be joined by a customer in production as well as SpaceXAI engineers as they share the workflows they run today. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

title: How to use AI to develop and deploy controls from your internal policies
description: You maintain internal security policies but turning them into implemented, risk-prioritized controls could be manual and slow. This lightning talk demonstrates how to use Kiro to develop and deploy controls at scale across three layers. Preventive controls that block non-compliant actions, detective controls that identify violations and trigger remediation, and proactive controls that validate configurations before deployment. You leave with a practical approach to using AI to accelerate the entire control lifecycle from policy to enforcement.

title: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier, from silicon to application
description: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack: chips, servers, software, and the models built on top, each layer making the next one faster and cheaper to run. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. You will see how each layer of innovation compounds and learn where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.

title: How Vanguard Scales AI Oversight Without Scaling Human Review (sponsored by Capgemini)
description: Human review can't scale linearly with generative-AI volume. Vanguard's AI Center of Excellence built a closed-loop oversight system where every AI response is scored by an LLM-as-judge, confirmed or overturned by a subject-matter expert, and routed through a confusion matrix: confirmed catches sharpen the agent, disagreements calibrate the judge. Each SME label grows a benchmark that resets how much oversight the next cycle needs, proving mathematically that coverage can fall while risk holds flat. Built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda-hosted detector SLMs, SQS, DynamoDB, and SageMaker, the loop moves toward real-time interruption of harmful responses before customers see them. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: How WBD Became the First Media Company to Go Agentic Across AdTech
description: Buying and selling media has historically been manual, constrained by legacy systems and fragmented tools. Warner Bros. Discovery is changing that. As the first media company to integrate agentic AI workflows into every system across the media lifecycle, WBD is leapfrogging the competition by embedding autonomous agents at every step: planning, forecasting, optimization, and measurement. This converged platform makes linear TV as addressable and measurable as digital. Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self-improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.

title: How Workday built multicloud data interoperability foundation for Agentic AI
description: As enterprises scale agentic AI, the hardest problem is often giving agents secure, governed access to data spread across multiple clouds. Physically copying the data between clouds introduces cost, latency, and governance risk. In this session, you will learn how Workday leverages Apache Iceberg catalog federation to build bidirectional, zero-copy integration that enables cross-cloud data access without duplicating or moving data. You will see how this open standard based approach lets AI agents reason over trusted enterprise data in place, with governance and business context preserved.

title: Hugging Face on AWS: AI Model Deployment at Scale
description: AWS and Hugging Face collaborate on open source Deep Learning Containers, optimized inference frameworks, and Neuron integrations that make deploying community models production-ready. This session covers the open source stack - from Transformers library optimizations for Graviton and Trainium to TGI container contributions - that enables customers to serve Hugging Face models at 50% lower cost. Learn deployment patterns used by enterprises running open weight LLMs at millions of requests per day.

title: Hybrid Kubernetes made simple: EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway for on-prem and edge AI
description: Enterprises are migrating from legacy hypervisors to Kubernetes-native stacks but need hybrid connectivity without complex network changes. In this builder session, attendees set up the newly launched Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway to seamlessly connect on-premises worker nodes to a cloud EKS control plane without modifying existing network infrastructure. They deploy an AI inference workload spanning cloud and edge, configure pod-to-pod communication across environments, implement data residency controls, and validate failover scenarios.

title: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!
description: AI agents are non-deterministic - they can burn tokens, stall, or drift into wrong behaviour with no warning, and teams often have no visibility until something breaks. In this hands-on builders session, you will use Amazon CloudWatch to observe live agents from both the console and your IDE: trace what an agent actually did, spot failures, and surface anomalous behaviour. Working with real agents - a production agent and a custom chatbot - you build the detection and alerting yourself and leave able to apply it to the agents you run in production.

title: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

title: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. title: Implementing agentic AI solutions on-premises and at the edge
description: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-premises data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.

title: Implementing agentic AI solutions on-premises and at the edge
description: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-premises data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.

title: Implement semantic caching for AI agents using ElastiCache for Valkey
description: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Innovations in Elastic Load Balancing and application networking
description: Discover the latest innovations in application networking. This session covers new capabilities in Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) and simplified application delivery across all compute environments. Learn how new approaches to application networking help you save time and money. Whether you're building microservices, modern application architectures, or AI agent workloads, see what's next for application networking on AWS.

title: Inside AWS Trainium3: Hardware innovations for better AI economics
description: What does it take to build a chip purpose-made for AI? In this deep dive, we explore Trainium3 architecture innovations: NeuronCore innovations that delivers higher TFLOPs, hardware-accelerated quantization, softmax acceleration, near-memory compute and Mixture-of-Experts optimizations. We'll share micro-benchmark data showing how these choices translate to real performance for Mixture-of-Experts and other demanding workloads. At the system level, we examine the Trn3 UltraServer family, scaling from 32 to 144 chips via NeuronLink fabric to enables up to 4.4x more performance. Leave with a deep understanding of how to evaluate and leverage purpose-built AI Chips for your AI workloads.

title: Inside Bayer’s AI agent: Interpretability as governance (sponsored by Thoughtworks)
description: Enterprise AI governance has focused on controls around agents—identity, permissions, sandboxing, and audit trails. But what happens inside the model? This session explores a live production system: Bayer’s PRINCE research assistant, built with Thoughtworks on AWS to give researchers access to 18,000+ preclinical study reports. We’ll share how Thoughtworks’ AI Research Labs applies mechanistic interpretability research, published at ICML, NeurIPS, and AAAI, to understand why the assistant answers, cites, or refuses queries. See how sparse autoencoders identify internal circuits behind refusal, how targeted steering changes behavior without retraining, and why this matters in regulated environments. Leave with a practical framework for making interpretability a core component of AI governance. This presentation is brought to you by Thoughtworks, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
description: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose built AI chips to deliver better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference, and leave equipped to write custom, hardware-optimized kernels.

title: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
description: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders, partners, and teams putting agents into production go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join us for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Agentic Engineering Org of the Future (sponsored by Harness)
description: What does it actually take to become an AI-native engineering organization? A senior technology executive from a Fortune 500 enterprise sits down with Harness Field CTO Nick Durkin to talk through what it's really taken to go all in on agentic software delivery, orchestrating agents across the entire SDLC instead of one-off automations. They'll get into what that transformation actually looks like end to end, how they decide when an agent runs on its own versus when a human stays in the loop, how agentic engineering has affected cloud migration and consumption, and what it takes to do this at the scale of a Fortune 500 engineering org. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Architecture: Building Secure AI Applications on AWS (sponsored by TrendAI™)
description: AI is rapidly moving from experimentation to production, creating new challenges for developers, architects, and security teams. In this technical session, explore the real-world architectures enterprises use to build and secure AI applications on AWS. Learn how organizations leverage Amazon Bedrock, EKS, ECS, Security Lake, CloudTrail, and cloud-native automation to protect AI workloads, monitor risk across multi-account environments, and streamline security operations. Through practical deployment patterns and lessons learned from large-scale AWS environments, discover how to build AI applications that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. The session draws on deployment patterns described for TrendAI Vision One on AWS, including AI workload protection, cloud telemetry integration, and AWS-native architecture approaches. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees)
description: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true. This presentation is brought to you by CloudBees, an AWS Partner.

title: Integrate Agents with MCP Servers and Tools using AgentCore Gateway
description: Your agent may handle basic conversations well, but to take real-world actions it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this hands-on lab, use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to expose Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tools with JWT authorization. Register tool targets, connect to a pre-deployed nutrition coach agent, and validate how it dynamically discovers and invokes new capabilities at runtime without redeployment.

title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
description: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
description: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

title: Intelligent Co-Sell: Removing Friction and Empowering Customer Conversations
description: AWS Partners are moving faster than ever—into new regions, new AI-native solution categories, and more complex deal structures—while manual selling processes haven't kept pace. This session reveals how a new generation of AI agents handles the work that used to slow deals down: surfacing co-sell intelligence and funding eligibility in the tools Partners already use. See how intelligent co-sell gives Partners more time selling, bigger and more repeatable deals, and proof of impact that compounds.

title: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS)
description: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.

title: Investigate Incidents Across Teams with AWS DevOps Agent
description: Production incidents typically involve multiple teams, but tooling and investigations are often siloed. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS DevOps Agent meets teams where incident response already happens. See how engineers can interact with the agent directly from tools like Slack, consolidating investigation activity, findings, and recommended actions alongside team communication. Bring your multi-team incident patterns and discuss approaches to faster, more connected incident response across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments.

title: Investigating Threats to AI: Incident Response to Compromised AI Workloads
description: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

title: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
description: There are now three ways to migrate Java from x86 to Graviton. AWS Transform Custom runs at scale across hundreds of repos with managed CI/CD and validation. The open-source Java skill runs locally in any agentic IDE, no AWS credentials needed. The Arm MCP server (in Kiro) goes broader, covering non-Java languages and general x86-to-Arm patterns. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and migration timeline. We demo all three on the same codebase, show where each succeeds and where it hands off, and give you a decision framework so you pick the right tool before you start.

title: Keep sleeping at 3am: Elastic watches your Prometheus metrics so you don't have to (sponsored by Elastic)
description: When your kubernetes cluster fires at 3am, who's investigating? In this session we'll show Elastic Nightshift — our autonomous AI SRE — detecting a real Kubernetes incident and working it end to end: from alert to root cause to remediation, with its reasoning made transparent at every step. Nightshift draws on native Prometheus and PromQL metrics in Elastic. Kubernetes logs, out-of-the-box EKS dashboards and workflows, and ES|QL subqueries that correlate metrics with logs and traces in a single investigation. We'll also show how the 30x faster columnar metrics engine and full telemetry retention give Nightshift the complete context it needs to work like your best engineer This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
description: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
description: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

title: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu)
description: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.

title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
description: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. Discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences industries—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.

title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
description: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
description: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.

title: Koa: NVIDIA Nemotron-Powered CRM Reasoning Inside Salesforce’s AWS Trust Boundary
description: Salesforce Koa is a family of CRM reasoning models post-trained from NVIDIA Nemotron open models. Koa is in production on AWS, inside Salesforce's trust boundary. This session covers technical insights on how Koa was built and how Salesforce serves the model on AWS. Additionally, attendees will learn how Salesforce enforces trust and safety controls in the serving layer outside the model. This session is relevant to any team building and deploying custom open models for the enterprise.

title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
description: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
description: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. title: KYC in 90 Seconds: Real-Time Onboarding with AgentCore
description: Opening a bank account should take seconds, not days. This session shows how AI agents can speed up KYC while keeping the final decision under control, specialized agents that run on Agentcore Harness investigate identity, documents, fraud signals, and screening results, with checks running in parallel. AgentCore Gateway routes tool requests through Cedar policies before tools run, while deterministic rules decide whether a case moves forward or needs human review. The session follows a clean case, an ambiguous case, and a new risk event after onboarding. Attendees leave with a pattern for regulated agentic systems.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
description: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
description: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. title: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
description: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.

title: Land migrated workloads with controls already in place
description: Most migrations add governance controls after workloads land on AWS, and that creates rework. This chalk talk shows how to build guardrails into your AWS Transform migration workflow with AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub so workloads arrive with controls in place. Bring your migration challenges, and we design a secure-by-default landing together that carries governance through each phase of the migration.

title: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
description: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.

title: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
description: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.

title: Learn new AI development skills with Kiro
description: Discover Kiro, the IDE for structured agentic development. In this builder’s session, explore how to use Kiro as your intelligent partner - helping to understand complex codebases, crystalize detailed requirements, and deliver quality solutions at unprecedented speed. You will iterate with Kiro to finalize your detailed design, before using Kiro to orchestrate AI agents and implement a fully working solution – all while maintaining complete control throughout the development process. You must bring a laptop to participate in this session.

title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
description: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

title: Live AI and the Infrastructure Behind It (sponsored by Decart)
description: AI is entering a new era: from static generation to live experiences. From shopping to entertainment, digital experiences are becoming live, visual, and personalized. In this session, Decart will explore the infrastructure powering this shift, what it takes to deliver AI-generated video in real time, and how to bring these experiences to scale. Join us for a look at the technology behind Live AI, and where it’s going next. This presentation is brought to you by Decart, an AWS Partner.

title: LOTA: Detecting and preventing advanced lateral movement
description: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

title: LSEG: Scaling multi-agent AI with assurance on Amazon Bedrock
description: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) manages one of the world's largest risk intelligence datasets, processing millions of records that demand continuous curation and validation. In this session, learn how LSEG built a durable agentic AI framework on Amazon Bedrock—orchestrating multi-agent workflows that combines deterministic rules, AI enrichment, and human review to reduce false positives in financial crime screening. LSEG will share their approach to continuous AI assurance with golden dataset evaluations and staged rollout gates with real-time observability and automated rollback to safely scale automation while maintaining the accuracy global financial institutions require.

title: Machines on Call for Humans: Agents to run and fix your prod (sponsored by Resolve AI)
description: We're entering a new era of software operations where the question is no longer whether intelligent agents have a role in production, but whether humans should still be the first responder. As production environments continue to grow more complex, agents are becoming part of the operations team, handling the repetitive work of operating production while engineers focus on the decisions that require judgment, creativity, and experience. This session explores how leading enterprises are rethinking on-call, improving reliability, and reshaping the way production is operated by putting machines on call for humans. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

title: Make AMD Your Default on AWS: Efficient EC2 for the Agentic AI Era with EPYC (sponsored by AMD)
description: What if you could run agentic AI for over 30% less on Amazon EC2—within the contracts you already have? As autonomous agents call inference models and tools, compute demand explodes and the CPU-to-GPU ratio inverts from 1:8 to 8:1, making processor choice the defining ROI decision. This session proves how 5th-Gen AMD EPYC "Turin" on EC2 runs general-purpose workloads faster and smaller, delivering >30% OpEx savings you can redirect from IT overhead into AI budgets. Partners see how MAP-aligned migration funding, POC support, and co-sell turn efficient, variety-ready AMD infrastructure on AWS into bigger, faster customer wins. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
description: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.

title: Make the agent code while you sleep
description: Anyone can prompt an agent. The hard part is getting it to work the way you want—for hours, unattended, without going off the rails. This advanced workshop digs into orchestration. You'll build a custom agent, then set a goal so strong the agent can't redefine it or declare victory early. You'll decompose work across subagents, use directives like /goal to keep execution on track, and design guardrails that let an agent run long and autonomously while landing where you intended. We'll use Kiro, but these patterns transfer to any agentic system. You must bring your laptop to participate.
