title: Make your multi-agent orchestration more deterministic
description: As agents work on longer, more complex tasks, the context window fills up and the agent can lose track of its plan and execution steps. The manual setup required to get multi-agent orchestration to reliably complete these kinds of tasks can be complex and brittle. In this session, you'll learn best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale your multi-agent workloads and take on hours-long tasks with confidence.

title: Making Enterprise Data AI-Ready Without the Data Engineering Overhead (sponsored by Eon)
description: Enterprise data is spread across databases, object stores, and compute, but making it usable by AI often requires months of data engineering and a growing web of pipelines to build and maintain. In this session, we’ll show how Eon continuously discovers, connects to, classifies, and transforms data across Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EC2, S3, and more into a unified, AI-ready data layer. We’ll walk through the architecture and semantic layer on AWS, then share how agents can use Amazon Bedrock to query that governed context in natural language through MCP, with Claude, Amazon Quick, and other AI clients. This presentation is brought to you by Eon, an AWS Partner.

title: Making Kiro Crew work for your team
description: Kiro Crew is the persistent, open source development workspace that remembers your context, learns how you work, and coordinates across your unique tools and workflows, so you come back to progress instead of another workflow to restart. In this session, you'll learn how to make Kiro Crew work for your team: wire in the tools your team already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape shared memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold and maintain team standards and best practices.

title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
description: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.

title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
description: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.

title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
description: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.

title: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
description: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.

title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
description: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

title: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
description: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

title: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
description: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

title: MCP is Just An MVP. Knowledge Lakes Are The Sequel. (sponsored by Atolio)
description: MCP lets agents connect to systems. It's a minimum viable product, not a complete way to run that connection at scale. Raw database access hit the same wall decades ago, before warehouses and data lakes brought structure and governance at scale. Point-to-point agent connections hit it again: costs climb with every added tool call, latency stacks with every cross-system hop, and permissions rarely travel with retrieved data, making synthesized knowledge a sharper security risk than raw SQL ever posed. This session traces that history, breaks down each failure mode, and maps what a knowledge lake built for agents solves. This presentation is brought to you by Atolio, an AWS Partner.

title: MCP Meets GraphQL: A Typed Foundation for Enterprise AI Agents (sponsored by Apollo GraphQL)
description: Enterprises connecting AI agents to systems of record face three unsolved problems: can an agent discover what data exists and what it means, get that context without runaway token cost, and touch only what it's authorized to touch. GraphQL, the proven Linux Foundation-backed standard beneath many of the world's largest customer experiences at brands like Netflix, AirBnB, Shopify, Walmart, and countless others, already solves all three through self-describing schemas and field-level queries. This talk lays out the architecture for combining GraphQL with MCP, including Apollo's approach to graph-based orchestration for cost and reliability. This presentation is brought to you by Apollo GraphQL, an AWS Partner.

title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
description: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

title: Meet Your AI Teammate for WorkSpaces Administration
description: Whether you run WorkSpaces today or are evaluating cloud desktops for the first time, operational overhead follows every virtual desktop deployment: ongoing monitoring, systemic issues that surface as tickets, and end-user requests that consume administrator time. Most teams operate reactively, triaging problems after they surface and manually guiding users through resolution. This session explores how Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor is using AI to reduce resolution time for both IT administrators and end users. We'll walk through the operational challenges we're hearing from customers, share our approach to solving them, and demonstrate early results from production environments. Bring your deployment architecture questions.

title: Migrate on-premises storage to AWS with agentic AI
description: Migrating on-premises storage to AWS typically means weeks of manual assessment, business case building, and wave planning before a single byte moves. AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities handle the full lifecycle, from automated assessment and business case generation to wave planning and execution, reducing that timeline to hours. In this lightning talk, see how to migrate storage from VMware estates, enterprise databases, and associated data with AI handling the complexity. Leave knowing how to start your first Transform project and accelerate time to results.

title: Migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with AI-powered conversion
description: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. In this workshop, you'll walk through the end-to-end workflow using AWS Transform's agentic AI: assess your SQL Server database, automate schema conversion, resolve dependencies, then hand off to your local IDE where you review, refine, and deploy converted database objects directly. You'll leave knowing how to reduce weeks of manual effort to hours while improving conversion accuracy and confidence.

description: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
description: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
description: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
description: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.

title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
description: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.

title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
description: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

title: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
description: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
description: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

title: Modernize legacy batch into event-driven with AWS Transform & Kiro
description: Batch processing has powered critical enterprise workloads for decades, from mainframes running COBOL and PL/I to distributed systems on legacy Java. The trade-off? Overnight batch cycles that business processes can no longer afford. In this session, reimagine batch as event-driven microservices using Domain-Driven Design. AWS Transform reverse-engineers business rules from legacy code across platforms with full traceability, and Kiro translates that understanding into microservices specifications, generates production code, and creates Infrastructure as Code for AWS deployment. Leave with a repeatable pattern for reimagining batch workloads as real-time, event-driven microservices built on business rules that took decades to refine. Laptop required.

title: Modernize .NET Applications with AWS Transform and Kiro
description: Legacy .NET Framework applications tied to Windows limit your deployment options and increase operational costs. In this lab, you use AWS Transform for .NET in Interactive Mode to automatically port a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor application. You review the AWS Transform generated assessment report and migration plan, accept the automated transformation, then use Kiro to identify and fix the residual runtime issue that remains after the port.

title: Modernize SAP business processes with agentic AI on AWS
description: Enterprise processes span SAP for ERP, Salesforce for CRM, and ServiceNow for ITSM, connected by aging, brittle integrations that are slow to change. Agentic AI offers a better path: replacing point-to-point integrations with agents that reason across applications. In this workshop, you modernize an SAP-centric business process by orchestrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents over Model Context Protocol, including the AWS for SAP MCP Server. You implement cross-application use cases spanning finance, supply chain, and operations then leave with a deployable reference architecture for moving from custom integrations to agent-orchestrated workflows.

title: Modernize Windows to Linux and SQL to PostgreSQL with agentic AI
description: Moving workloads from Windows to Linux and SQL Server to PostgreSQL has always been a complex, multi-step project. Agentic AI changes the game by orchestrating the entire journey for you. In this expert-level workshop, you'll start with on-premises Windows Server workloads in a simulated data center and migrate to Amazon EC2 covering agent installation, continuous replication, and cutover. Then you'll modernize by upgrading SQL Server to PostgreSQL and migrating PHP to Amazon EKS, applying replatforming patterns in practice. You'll leave with end-to-end experience executing OS and database modernization, accelerated by agentic AI. Laptop required.

title: Modernize your full .NET and SQL Server stack with AWS Transform
description: Modernizing Microsoft workloads means tackling .NET and SQL Server together, not as separate projects. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to compress this effort into a single sprint and reduce operating costs by up to 70% by moving off costly licenses. Working from a legacy app, you'll port .NET Framework code to modern, cross-platform .NET, migrate SQL Server to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, then containerize and deploy to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Come ready with your personal GitHub account. Laptop required.

title: Modernizing Care for the Underserved: Montefiore's Cloud Journey
description: Montefiore Einstein is one of New York's leading academic health systems, serving 1.3 million Bronx residents across 11 hospitals and 300+ ambulatory locations. To best care for patients, most of whom rely on Medicare or Medicaid, Montefiore needed to modernize its enterprise technology. Montefiore selected AWS as its strategic cloud provider to build a secure, scalable, and resilient foundation that strengthens security and optimizes costs. This session explores how the transformation—including an Epic migration—enables AI-powered clinical decision support, improves the reliability of critical medical records, and expands patient access through Amazon One Medical. Learn the strategies, lessons, and cloud-first approach driving better outcomes for the patients and communities Montefiore serves.

title: Modernizing HPC on AWS: Migration at scale with PCS
description: AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) is helping teams modernize their HPC infrastructure by making it easier to migrate off legacy schedulers without disrupting engineering velocity. In this session, hear how organizations have moved to PCS at scale, including how Amazon Leo migrated 400 engineers and achieved 20% cost savings and 50% faster jobs. Walk away with practical migration patterns, performance tuning strategies, and architecture decisions that apply whether you're running simulations, modeling, or other compute-intensive workloads.

title: Molecule to Market: Bayer & Capgemini Accelerate Drug Discovery with NVIDIA BioNeMo (sponsored by NVIDIA)
description: Join us to learn how Bayer Crop Science needed to accelerate target identification and lead optimization within its drug/crop-science discovery pipeline, and was able to accelerate their process with NVIDIA GPUs and BioNeMo. Building on AWS, they created a drug discovery workflow accelerating target identification and lead optimization through GPU-accelerated inference, molecular generation, and protein modeling, running on NVIDIA hardware. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Monetizing your applications with AWS
description: In this session, learn how to transform your finished application into a revenue-generating SaaS product. Learn about analyzing your cloud infrastructure, choose pricing models, and instrumenting code for usage metering. You'll see how to manage the complete billing lifecycle, from subscription management and invoicing to tax calculation and payment processing. Walk away with a clear path to accelerate your time-to-market and start charging customers.

title: Monitor Agent Performance and Telemetry using AgentCore Observability
description: A personal finance assistant agent deployed on AgentCore Runtime starts showing intermittent failures and slow responses. In this lab, you will use AgentCore Observability with CloudWatch GenAI dashboards and Transaction Search to diagnose production issues. Trace errors through spans, correlate telemetry with application logs, and identify root causes including a tool timeout and conversation history bloat. Apply fixes, redeploy to AgentCore Runtime, and set up CloudWatch Alarms to catch issues before users do.

title: Monitor AI workloads and agents end to end
description: Get hands-on with Amazon CloudWatch Omni, the next evolution of CloudWatch that converges application and agent observability into one AI-powered solution. Instrument an agent, trace its execution, run evaluations, and experiment with prompts and models in your IDE. Explore auto-discovered topology, golden metrics, and AI-powered investigation with AWS DevOps Agent.

title: Monitor and optimize costs for Amazon Bedrock
description: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how that spend maps to business outcomes. In this lightning talk, see how to tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

title: Move AI agents from prototype to production with 1Password (sponsored by 1Password)
description: An AI agent can be easy to prototype but hard to take to production once it needs access to real systems. For developers, platform engineers, and security teams building with AWS AgentCore, this session shows how 1Password uses the same governed credential workflow from a local sandbox to the cloud without code changes. Attendees will see how this approach helps engineering teams move faster, limits the blast radius of a compromised agent, and gives security teams a clear audit trail. The session covers short-lived credential delivery through the AgentCore gateway and policies that apply consistently from development through production. This presentation is brought to you by 1Password, an AWS Partner.

title: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
description: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale. We'll dig into what continuous mode looks like in practice, what early enterprise customers are seeing, and how this changes the way your teams think about maintaining code health over time. Bring your questions.

Bring your questions.

title: Move Fast With AI Agents Without Betting the Business (sponsored by MontyCloud)
description: You are under pressure to put AI agents to work fast, without betting the business. Everyone is racing to build agents, but no one is governing them. MontyCloud is an AI-native, autonomous CloudOps platform built on one conviction. As agents become easy to create, value moves to trusted execution. Walk away with a blueprint for turning insights into governed workflows, and governed workflows into trusted outcomes. See a live demo where any agent, model, or tool acts only with the right context, identity, policy, approvals, and cost controls. Learn why the unit of value is the governed workflow. This presentation is brought to you by MontyCloud, an AWS Partner.

title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
description: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.

title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
description: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.

title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
description: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Multi-Agent Operations for Broadcast & Streaming
description: When live or streaming video breaks, every second costs revenue and audience trust. This session shows how to build coordinated AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands SDK that ingest observability data from AWS Media Services and partners, reason across signal domains, and accelerate root cause identification. Walk away with an architecture for agentic operations that turns reactive troubleshooting into proactive resolution.

title: Multi-Agent Operations for Broadcast & Streaming
description: When live or streaming video breaks, every second costs revenue and audience trust. This session shows how to build coordinated AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands SDK that ingest observability data from AWS Media Services and partners, reason across signal domains, and accelerate root cause identification. Walk away with an architecture for agentic operations that turns reactive troubleshooting into proactive resolution.

title: Multicloud Operating Models for ISVs
description: ISVs adopting multiple clouds face the same trade-offs. This breakout distills cloud-agnostic operating-model patterns from production multi-cloud estates -- workload placement, abstraction layers, resiliency, and FinOps (optimization, tokenization), and unified observability -- illustrated by SAP running at 25,000+ accounts across AWS, Azure, and GCP. SAP's team walks through what stayed cloud-specific, what they unified, and what they had to invent. Leave with operating-model patterns you can apply across clouds.

title: Multi-tenant agentic AI with Aurora and DynamoDB
description: AI agents are autonomous, stateful, and capable of invoking external tools. In a multi-tenant SaaS system, every one of those capabilities is a potential data isolation failure. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tenant agentic AI solution enforcing tenant isolation across Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level security, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3 Vectors. Implement tenant-scoped vector stores for RAG, agent memory backed by multiple database engines, MCP-based tool authorization gated by subscription tier, and usage metering. Leave with a working reference architecture that prevents cross-tenant data leakage. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Multi-Tenant Agentic Platforms: A Scalable Reference Architecture
description: SaaS is going AI-native. ISVs must orchestrate third-party agents at scale. This session presents a multi-tenant architecture covering MCP, A2A, and AgentCore for orchestration, entitlement-based monetization, secure token exchange, agent lifecycle via Agent Registry, and cross-tenant observability.

title: Multi-tenant compute modernization with Amazon EMR on EKS
description: What does it take to run millions of diverse jobs a day across many tenants without costs spiraling or one bad workload taking down the fleet? In this chalk talk, we explore how organizations modernize a multi-tenant compute layer on EMR on EKS to serve batch analytics, streaming, ML, and agentic AI from one platform. We whiteboard the choices that make it possible: custom bin packing to mix heterogeneous tenant workloads efficiently, EKS provisioned control planes to sustain high job throughput per cluster, and Graviton to drive down cost per job. Bring your scaling challenges and we'll design solutions together.

title: Multi-tenant SaaS and agentic apps on Amazon EKS
description: Amazon EKS has become the runtime of choice for ISVs building agentic SaaS, offering the control, workload isolation, and networking flexibility that managed runtimes cannot. The challenge is multi-tenancy: how do you run agent workloads for hundreds of tenants on shared infrastructure without blast radius, cost leakage, or isolation drift? In this workshop, build a multi-tenant agent deployment on EKS with tenant isolation across namespaces and network policies, IRSA-backed credentials per agent workload, and per-tenant observability via OpenTelemetry. Each lab ends with an isolation proof. Leave with a reference architecture you can apply directly to your cluster.

title: Navigating the inter-workings of an agentic SOC & threat hunting analyst
description: Security analysts face an expanding attack surface with finite time and attention. In this session, we show how analysts can leverage AI-powered agents to accelerate their core workflows — from automated triage and log correlation to proactive threat hunting across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and threat intelligence feeds. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. You will see how to configure trust boundaries so agents act within your approved scope, how source attribution ensures every AI-surfaced claim traces back to a specific log, and how to evaluate whether the AI is actually making your team faster.

title: Network security innovations for agentic workloads
description: AI agents plan and execute actions autonomously, at machine speed, with real-world consequences. Unlike traditional automation that follows pre-defined network paths, agent traffic is non-deterministic, calling different APIs and chaining different services each time it runs. In this session, we cover the network security capabilities AWS has built for this shift. You'll see how to inspect and control autonomous traffic at every layer, from DNS resolution to application-layer filtering, enforce least-privilege connectivity for agents, and detect anomalous behavior in machine-to-machine communication.

title: Nine Seconds to Zero: Protecting AWS from AI Agent Disasters
description: In April 2026, an AI coding agent deleted a company's entire production database in nine seconds, without being asked. The agent was confidently wrong and had the permissions to act on it. In this session, we recreate that incident live using Amazon Bedrock, walk through every failure in the chain, then rebuild the architecture with six hardening layers: Bedrock Guardrails, human approval gates, least-privilege IAM, deletion protection, isolated backups, and real-time monitoring. Walk away with a concrete checklist for designing AI-assisted systems that plan for when the AI is wrong, not just when it performs perfectly.

title: No Data Left Behind: The AI-Ready Path Through AWS (sponsored by Qlik)
description: Your enterprise data is scattered across SAP, mainframes, databases, and cloud platforms that were never designed to talk to each other — and every AI initiative depends on enabling that communication. This session shows how Qlik and AWS modernize that data without downtime, rewrites, or re-platforming risk: zero-footprint CDC, Qlik Open Lakehouse with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Athena, Spark Structured Streaming on Amazon EMR, and governed data products built for AI. You'll also get a bonus preview of Qlik's Studio AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock and what's next for agentic workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

title: No room for error: deploying trusted AI when the stakes are high (sponsored by Monte Carlo)
description: Deploying agents at scale is a major endeavor for any organization; in healthcare, the stakes are especially high. Unpredictable behaviors & unreliable outputs pose a risk to patients, invite scrutiny from regulators, & erode hard-won institutional trust. Regulated industries must balance accuracy alongside their drive to innovate. Barr Moses, co-founder & CEO of Monte Carlo, will delve into this challenging topic with leaders from GE Healthcare. They’ll dissect some of the most difficult failure modes for agents & discuss how reliability practices have to evolve as teams scale agentic workflows in high-stakes environments. Discussed: how AI itself can be turned back on the problem of observing, resolving, and optimizing agents as well as building the guardrails, ownership models, & trust infrastructure that let a highly regulated organization move quickly without compromising on trust. This presentation is brought to you by Monte Carlo, an AWS Partner.

title: Northwestern Mutual: Reinventing policy servicing with agentic AI
description: Financial representatives at Northwestern Mutual traditionally logged service requests and waited for back-office resolution. In this session, we'll walk through the production architecture behind this transformation: Amazon Bedrock Agents connected to core insurance systems through the Model Context Protocol, with orchestration and governance controls designed for a regulated environment. We'll cover authorization patterns, auditability, human oversight, and lessons learned moving from proof of concept to production. Representatives now resolve significantly more requests directly—reducing resolution times, improving good-order processing, and driving higher satisfaction, with participants reporting better outcomes for their clients.

title: Not all bots are bad: building a secure perimeter with AWS WAF
description: Your edge traffic is a mix of customers, AI agents, scrapers, and attackers. Treat them the same and you lose either security or revenue. In this workshop, you turn AWS WAF into a decision layer that classifies traffic in real time and routes it. Legitimate users get a fast lane, suspicious traffic goes to deception environments that waste attackers' time and reveal their intent, and AI agents get their own treatment that opens the door to new ways of charging for access. None of it requires changes to your origin logic.

title: OAuth delegation patterns for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
description: AI agents act on behalf of users and systems, and delegating the right access without over-permissioning is hard. In this chalk talk, we use code examples to work through authorization delegation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity. We cover the OAuth grant flows that matter for agents, including authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine calls, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. For each flow, you see which agent scenario it fits and when to choose it over the others.

title: Observability and operations in the AI era
description: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.

title: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
description: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.

title: Observability patterns for agentic AI in production
description: AI agents are non-deterministic, multi-step, and make autonomous decisions and traditional APM isn't enough. Explore observability patterns for agentic workloads: reasoning chain tracing, token cost attribution, guardrail monitoring, and multi-agent coordination. We'll whiteboard architectures in real time. Bring your toughest production agent monitoring questions and leave with actionable patterns.

title: Observable Agents with Lambda Durable Functions and OpenTelemetry
description: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.

title: Observe AI agents beyond your perimeter
description: Your developers are burning tokens on AI coding agents with zero visibility. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex run on laptops, outside your perimeter, with no telemetry reaching your observability backend. In this session, we fix that. Using native OpenTelemetry export and Amazon CloudWatch's OTLP endpoint with a single bearer token, with no collectors, no sidecars, no credential wiring, we ship metrics (token usage, cost, productivity), logs (tool decisions, errors), and traces (agent reasoning chains) directly from developer machines. Then we build a live dashboard with per-team cost attribution and anomaly alerting, all queryable with PromQL. Walk out ready to deploy in minutes.

title: Observe your applications and agents in one place
description: Traditional monitoring tools weren't built for the complexity of modern agentic and distributed applications. Teams juggle siloed dashboards, fragmented logs, and disconnected signals with no unified way to troubleshoot across agents, applications, and infrastructure. Amazon CloudWatch Omni is an AI-powered observability experience organized around your teams and the applications they run, combining OpenTelemetry interoperability with CloudWatch scale. See how you can troubleshoot applications faster and manage agents with confidence using automatic service discovery, dependency mapping, built-in evaluations, and natural-language investigation — all from the Omni UI, your IDE, or your favorite tools.

title: One agent to thousands: Building for scale with Newforma
description: When every team builds agents independently, you get the same ungovernable sprawl that drove the shift from artisanal EC2 to container platforms. Agents are non-deterministic workloads that require deterministic governance, and this tension drives every platform decision, from dual orchestration for known vs. emergent topologies, to policy-based boundaries around soft reasoning, to defense layers that compose without coupling. We walk through how Newforma operationalized this architecture on AWS, and attendees leave understanding how to layer orchestration, policy, and defense into an enterprise agent platform that scales safely.

title: One Control Plane for Every Agent: Architecture Patterns for Cost, Risk, and ROI (sponsored by Boomi)
description: Every agent call carries cost, permission, and blast radius, and as agents multiply across tools, frameworks, and SaaS, the gaps compound: uncapped spend, unapproved permissions, no shared record. This session breaks down an AI infrastructure layer, running on AWS, that governs every model, agent, and system. A design-time layer publishes an approved catalog of agents, tools, and MCP servers; a runtime layer routes, meters, and enforces policy on every call before it executes. See how spend caps, in-tenant SLMs, and governed APIs turn cost into a controlled input, while one trace gives finance, security, and engineering a shared, audit-ready record. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

title: One Control to Rule Them All: Guardrail Automation for Every Identity (sponsored by Sonrai Security)
description: Separate guardrails for humans, machine identities, and AI agents get messy, and rewriting every IAM policy takes forever. SCPs deployed at scope are easy to write. What follows is not. Nobody can say what a policy will break, so it never deploys. Someone gets blocked and the fix becomes a two hour hunt. The tenth control behaves nothing like the first. New accounts inherit none of it. This lightning talk answers all four using only AWS Organizations, SCPs, and RCPs. See how usage data makes a default deny safe, how access returns in seconds, and how least privilege holds. This presentation is brought to you by Sonrai Security, an AWS Partner.

title: One Data Foundation for Agentic AI and Real-Time Analytics on AWS (sponsored by Databricks)
description: Your team is under pressure to deliver real-time applications, AI agents, operational experiences, and analytics faster—but separate databases, serving layers, and pipelines create stale data, duplicated copies, governance gaps, and scaling challenges. In this session, we’ll explore how Databricks on AWS brings these workloads together with Lakehouse//RT, Lakebase, and the Lakehouse Transactional Application Platform (LTAP). See how teams serve low-latency, high-concurrency analytics, power operational applications and AI agents with live transactional data, and analyze data where it is created—all from one platform and one governed copy of data. You’ll leave with practical architecture guidance for building reliable real-time and AI applications on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

title: Ontology-Powered AI Agents: Verifiable Decisions Across Manufacturing
description: Manufacturing stakeholders make dozens of high-velocity decisions daily. Each must be traceable, defensible, and grounded in enterprise knowledge and lifecycle data. Yet the systems informing these decisions remain siloed, and AI agents reasoning over this fragmented data cannot produce verifiable results. Ontologies solve this by structuring manufacturing knowledge so agents can trace decisions back to their source data. In this chalk talk, we show how ontology-grounded agents, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, make verifiable decisions across the lifecycle with a live demo. Attendees leave with a reference architecture, best practices, and a clear path to building verifiable AI agents for manufacturing.

title: Open source agent observability and evals with AgentCore and Langfuse (sponsored by ClickHouse)
description: Production agents need more than infrastructure. They need an open source foundation for understanding behavior, evaluating quality, and improving continuously without sacrificing control of their data. In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Langfuse combine secure agent infrastructure with open source observability and evaluation, powered by ClickHouse. See how teams capture OpenTelemetry traces, debug trajectories and tool calls, evaluate production quality, turn failures into datasets, and prevent regressions before deployment. We will share a practical architecture for unifying policy and telemetry across AgentCore, EKS, and other runtimes so teams can ship trustworthy agents faster. This presentation is brought to you by ClickHouse, an AWS Partner.

title: Operational resilience in regulated environments with AWS DevOps Agent
description: As software delivery accelerates, financial services organizations struggle to manage incidents across fragmented toolchains. In this chalk talk, learn how AWS DevOps Agent acts as an always-on operations teammate for regulated environments—resolving incidents autonomously, strengthening systems proactively, and validating releases before they reach production. We'll whiteboard four patterns: how the agent investigates and resolves incidents in minutes; how the agent learns from past incidents to recommend improvements; how on-demand SRE tasks give your team instant operational intelligence; and how release readiness reviews catch compliance and dependency risks before code ships. Bring your operational challenges and leave with best practices.

title: Optimize agentic AI costs with EC2 Capacity Blocks and Spot Instances
description: Agentic AI turns ML infrastructure into a dynamic scheduling problem, where the goal is cost per accepted outcome. In this lightning talk, watch a self-managed agentic workflow run financial services portfolio stress testing on Amazon EC2, with telecom and media content generation as bonus patterns. EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML reserve capacity for deadline-critical stages, while EC2 Spot Instances add elastic, checkpointable capacity for parallel work. A bounded agentic planner proposes placement across NVIDIA GPUs and AWS silicon while deterministic controls enforce budget and deadline limits, keeping cost per accepted outcome low as workloads shift.

title: Optimize AI apps on Amazon Bedrock for cost, latency, and control
description: As AI workloads scale, engineers face complex trade-offs between cost, latency, and response quality. This code talk explores advanced optimisation techniques for production AI applications on Amazon Bedrock: prompt engineering, model selection, caching, and context window management. Through live coding, attendees examine the reasoning behind each design decision, observe cost impact via AWS Billing and Cost Management, and learn to instrument apps to detect performance regressions. Understanding the tokenomics of your AI stack is essential to operating efficiently at scale.

title: Optimize AI inference costs: Compare token economics on AWS silicon
description: Most enterprises run their entire AI pipeline on GPU and can overpay. AWS's silicon portfolio (Trainium & Graviton) along with NVIDIA GPU, Intel, and AMD all offer radically different cost-per-token economics for different workloads. This session delivers a decision framework for matching silicon to workload: training and inference on Trainium, RAG pipelines on Graviton, real-time agents on GPU, batch on Intel/AMD. Includes Bedrock vs. self-host crossover analysis, volume thresholds, and the architecture patterns to put the savings into practice.

title: Optimize AI workloads with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless
description: Building highly scalable, high-performance AI and data-driven applications requires intelligent caching strategies. In this session, learn how to build with Amazon ElastiCache to scale workloads across caching patterns such as session caching, KV-caching, and more. Dive deep into microsecond latency networking optimizations that enable sub-millisecond response times, and explore common performance pitfalls with practical solutions to keep applications running smoothly.

title: Optimize HPC with storage for throughput and IOPS
description: High-performance computing workloads demand storage that keeps pace with thousands of compute nodes processing data in parallel. Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers sub-millisecond latencies and high throughput without the operational burden of managing a parallel file system. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS adds high IOPS with consistent low-latency response for latency-sensitive workloads. Explore how to select the right deployment type based on your workload profile, leverage native S3 integration for data pipelines, and right-size performance independently from capacity. Bring your questions about CFD (computational fluid dynamics), genomics, semiconductor design, weather modeling, and other compute-intensive workloads.

title: Optimizing agentic AI: Vanguard's production deployment journey
description: Deploying AI agents in production is just the beginning. Optimizing them at scale is the real challenge. In this session, Vanguard shares how they transformed their investor-facing AI agent from functional to fast, safe, and personal. Learn the techniques—from prompt caching to adaptive thinking to guardrail tuning—that delivered 70%+ latency reduction without sacrificing safety, and how long-term memory now powers personalized conversations across sessions. Walk away with battle-tested patterns for balancing response quality, cost, and speed in agentic AI at enterprise scale.

title: Optimizing model performance with agentic loops on AWS Trainium
description: Extracting peak performance from AI accelerators requires optimization at multiple levels — from framework configuration to individual kernels — and the complexity grows with every new workload. Agentic loops replace this manual work with autonomous profiling, diagnosis, and code generation, iterating toward performance targets without human intervention. In this session, we demonstrate this workflow on AWS Trainium, purpose-built to deliver better price-performance for AI workloads. Explore how these loops identify bottlenecks, how persistent memory prevents repeated failures, and how long-running campaigns uncover optimizations for different inference shapes. Walk away with practical patterns for agentic optimization on purpose-built silicon.

title: Orchestrating agentic applications with Lambda durable functions
description: AI agents are powerful, but production workloads need more than an LLM and a prompt. They require deterministic routing, audit trails, compensation logic, and human oversight. In this workshop, build agentic orchestration using AWS Lambda durable functions and MCP tools. Learn to design workflows that checkpoint progress, recover from failures automatically, and pause for human-in-the-loop approval—all without managing additional infrastructure. You'll implement tool-calling patterns, handle multi-step reasoning with retries, and deploy agents that are observable, testable, and production-ready. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Orchestrating agentic workflows: Step Functions & durable functions
description: AI agents need orchestration that handles long-running tasks, human approvals, and recovery from partial failures. In this chalk talk, compare AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for agentic workloads, and learn when to choose code-first, replay-based recovery versus visual state-machine semantics. We’ll whiteboard how durable functions checkpoint progress and resume after failures, how Step Functions handle branching and parallel tool calls, and where Lambda MicroVMs fit for sandboxing agent-generated code execution. Bring your architecture questions—we’ll design hybrid patterns that combine both orchestrators based on your workload shape.

title: Orchestrating AI agents for continuous code security hardening
description: Agentic AI is increasing the rate at which organizations discover and fix security vulnerabilities — and the rate at which findings arrive faster than anyone can act on them. In this workshop, you'll build an agentic security hardening pipeline using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore: deterministic scanners fan out across code, dependencies, secrets, and infrastructure; reviewer and triage agents correlate and rank what comes back; and policy-as-code gates decide on demonstrated evidence rather than on agents agreeing. You'll learn how to decompose a security audit into parallelizable agent tasks, and how to keep a human holding every consequential decision before changes reach production.

title: Orchestrating AI Agents with AgentCore Runtime
description: You need more than one agent to reason across inventory, shipments, forecasts, and suppliers at the same time. In this lab, you deploy a multi-agent supply chain system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. You load data into DynamoDB, build container images with CodeBuild, and deploy specialist agents plus a supervisor orchestrator powered by Amazon Nova models. The orchestrator classifies questions, routes them to the right specialists in parallel, and synthesizes their responses into one coherent answer.

title: Orchestrating AI agents with AWS serverless services
description: Production AI agents need orchestration that handles non-deterministic behavior, multi-hour workflows, human approvals, and multi-agent coordination. Learn how AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda durable functions provide the reliability layer that agents demand. We cover patterns for durable execution, human-in-the-loop controls, event-driven agent communication, and the scale-to-zero economics that make serverless the natural home for agentic workloads.

title: Organizing Enterprise Knowledge and Securing Data with Amazon Quick
description: Amazon Quick transforms how teams access insights and automate decisions. In this SimuLearn session, you design Spaces in Quick to organize enterprise knowledge, configure custom Chat Agents with specialized instructions and curated knowledge bases, and integrate Quick with enterprise systems using Actions and connectors backed by Amazon S3 or Amazon DynamoDB. You then apply row-level and column-level security controls to protect sensitive data and explore Quick Research for comprehensive multi-source analysis and reporting.

title: Outpace AI attacks: Auto-recover AWS apps at machine speed with Rubrik. (sponsored by Rubrik)
description: Abstract: AI-driven attacks move at machine speed, and your AWS application is an interconnected system of code, infrastructure and data. Rebuilding by hand is a nightmare, if it’s even possible. Join us to see how an AI attack unfolds, and how Rubrik brings your business back by recovering the whole application in one automated motion. Rubrik discovers your application's dependencies, flags structural drift before it becomes an incident, and recovers it all together. Hear how Just Eat is moving from manual to validated, isolated recovery on AWS. Outpace AI-speed attacks with machine-speed recovery: less downtime, no manual rebuilds. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

title: Outrun technical debt in the age of autonomous development
description: The legacy estate has not gone away. Aging applications with undocumented business logic, outdated frameworks, and platforms nobody wants to touch remain a priority. Agentic tools have increased development velocity, but speed does not eliminate technical debt — it changes its shape. This compounding debt erodes productivity, weakens security posture, and inflates operational cost. Learn how AWS Transform custom and continuous modernization help organizations assess and remediate technical debt at scale — from framework migrations like Angular to React to language translations like C to Rust.

title: Own Your Harness: Control Cost & Risk in Enterprise-Wide AI Adoption (sponsored by Presidio)
description: The fastest way to lose control of AI is to let agents multiply without a harness. This talk walks through Presidio's journey from scattered pilots to enterprise-wide adoption, built on a custom orchestration layer that treats cost, identity, and policy as first-class concerns. Attendees will get an inside look at the architectural decisions, guardrails, and economic models that let us scale AI use predictably across the business. If you're weighing governance (cost and risk) against velocity, this is the playbook you want from day one. This presentation is brought to you by Presidio, an AWS Partner.

title: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
description: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. This session introduces the S3 stack purpose-built for agentic workloads. S3 Files provides a shared file system for multi-agent artifact handoff. S3 Vectors stores embeddings as long-term semantic memory that persists across sessions and restarts. S3 Metadata makes every object discoverable by tag, time, or custom attribute without scanning. Learn reference architectures for coordination, checkpointing, least-privilege access patterns, and framework integration.

title: Philips' Agentic AI Leap: 45 Days to Minutes on Sales Quotes (sponsored by EPAM)
description: Philips faced a 45-day sales quoting bottleneck in digital pathology, chasing systems and spreadsheets on every deal. With EPAM and AWS, Philips built Sensei, a conversational AI sales agent, using an AI-native SDLC powered by AWS Kiro and running on Amazon Bedrock with Strands Agents. In under six months, specialized agents for pricing, quoting and CRM cut quote turnaround by 90 percent, generating customer briefings in under two minutes, with governance and compliance built in for a regulated industry. This session shares a practical blueprint for applying agentic AI to complex enterprise workflows at speed, without sacrificing enterprise-grade trust. This presentation is brought to you by EPAM, an AWS Partner.

title: Physical AI for MedTech: From Intelligent Devices to Business Impact
description: Physical AI — AI that senses, reasons, and acts in the physical world — is reshaping medical devices. From surgical robots to connected infusion pumps, imaging to wearables, every next-gen device needs training, simulation, edge deployment, and fleet management at scale. In this chalk talk, we’ll architect the full Physical AI stack on AWS for medical devices — SageMaker for model training, IoT Greengrass for edge inference, regulated OTA at fleet scale, and NVIDIA solutions integrated into the AWS backbone. We’ll whiteboard the hard tradeoffs — edge vs. cloud, regulatory constraints, and scaling from prototype to 100K devices. Leave with a reference architecture and a clear path to pilot

title: Pit Crew AI: Building Multi-Agent Cloud Operations on AWS
description: AI can generate code at racing speed, but production workloads still require continuous attention to security, reliability, cost, and operational risks. In this Code Talk, we build a multi-agent architecture on AWS inspired by a Formula 1 pit crew. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, MCP, GitHub, Jira, and Infrastructure as Code, we evolve from a single agent to a team of specialized agents for security, cost optimization, reliability, and observability. Through a live demonstration, you’ll see how agents turn cloud findings into engineering tasks. Attendees will leave with reusable architectures, orchestration patterns, and examples for cloud operations on AWS.

title: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
description: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.

title: Powering America's AI and HPC leadership for mission-critical outcomes
description: AI and HPC deliver real mission breakthroughs across defense, national security, and science. In this session, hear how AWS's $50B infrastructure investment and leadership-class hyperscale elasticity compress timelines from years to months. Ideal for mission owners, architects, and tech leaders.

title: Powering Interactive Agents with Live Context (sponsored by Materialize)
description: How do you keep an agent's understanding of the world fresh enough for it to act on? Interactive agents need current context about the customers, orders, inventory, accounts, and other entities they reason about. But assembling that context from constantly changing operational systems is complex, forcing teams to choose between stale data, expensive recomputation, or complex pipelines. This talk will show how to build continuously updated context in SQL that is trustworthy enough for agents to rely upon. You'll learn how to transform operational data into agent-ready representations, keep attributes and relationships up to date as the underlying data changes, and propagate those changes to search indexes and embeddings when needed. Attend if you're deploying AI agents to production and want to give them fresher, more complete context and tighten their read-act-react loop. This presentation is brought to you by Materialize, an AWS Partner.

title: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
description: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.

title: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
description: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

title: Prime Video Financial Systems on the Road to 10x Velocity with Kiro
description: This chalk talk will deep-dive into Prime Video Financial Systems' journey toward 10x engineering velocity with Kiro. Starting at 3x through AI-assisted sprints, the team evolved to autonomous agent-driven delivery, where agents pick up tasks, implement code, raise code requests, address feedback, and merge 24/7 without human intervention. Each step compounds, enabling parallel execution, zero idle time, and freeing engineers to focus on design and review. This is an honest, in-progress story that demonstrates the concrete methodology, structured specs, persistent Kiro sessions, and architectural decisions required to move from acceleration toward order-of-magnitude transformation.

title: Production Agentic Trading: Build the pipeline Moeve runs on AgentCore
description: This session details the implementation of an agentic workforce managing the trade lifecycle in production energy trading operations. In this workshop, you'll build the pipeline Moeve runs in production: a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that extracts deal data from unstructured emails, resolves ambiguity deterministically against master data, and carries evidence per field. You'll harden it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on input and output, then score it for accuracy and run-to-run consistency, including the fields that measured badly, and why. You'll leave with a reusable pattern for production deployment of mission-critical trading workflows with strict latency and reliability requirements.

title: Productionize, secure, and scale agentic applications on Amazon ECS
description: AI agents are easy to prototype but hard to run in production. They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builders session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builder's session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including hardware-level task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Provision Desktops for Builders Faster with WorkSpaces
description: Builders lose days configuring environments. IT teams struggle to govern the growing sprawl of AI tools and extensions across their organization. In this session, we explore these challenges and share how Amazon WorkSpaces is approaching the builder desktop experience. We'll discuss what enterprises need to provision environments faster, maintain governance across multiple surfaces, and keep pace as AI-assisted development becomes the norm. Bring your questions.

title: Pushing AI Boundaries: Transform Marketing with Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker and AWS (sponsored by Adobe)
description: As generative AI matures into autonomous ecosystems, enterprise marketing demands a new era of collaboration. In this session, discover how Adobe and Amazon co-innovate to deliver next-generation AI capabilities for marketers, business practitioners, and developers. At the center of this revolution is Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, an advanced AI teammate powered by Adobe Harness. We will showcase how Coworker and its flexible, headless capabilities seamlessly unite Adobe’s deep customer experience expertise with the power of AWS. Attendees will discover how this combined innovation enables teams to transition from manual execution to goal-based, automated workflows with built-in governance. Join us to learn how this partnership helps enterprise organizations take a massive leap forward in operational effectiveness and unlock entirely new business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Adobe, an AWS Partner.

title: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
description: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Architecting AI Governance & Security at Scale
description: Everyone wants AI. Nobody wants to be the team that shipped it without security and governance. In this Rodeo, you'll join a team and face three demanding stakeholders: a security hawk, a data visibility champion, and a platform lead, racing to get Agentic AI live. Your team's mission: build a governance architecture that keeps all three happy. Together, you'll whiteboard, debate, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Best architecture rides away with the win.

title: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform
description: Enterprise data teams maintain ETL pipelines built on legacy tools like stored procedures, custom bash scripts, IBM DataStage and others, that resist migration due to undocumented dependencies. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. Each attendee picks one legacy source module (stored procedures, bash/SQL scripts, or DataStage jobs etc) and works hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized pipeline.

title: Rebuild CI for AI coding agents with content based caching (sponsored by RWX)
description: Continuous integration was designed around human pace. A developer pushes a branch, a webhook fires, and a ten minute wait feels acceptable. AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. Learn which parts of a pipeline are structurally slow and which are simply misconfigured. This presentation is brought to you by RWX, an AWS Partner.

title: Red team CTF: when auth and guardrails aren't enough
description: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.

title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
description: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
description: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. title: Reduce token costs by caching inference results on ElastiCache
description: Multi-agent AI systems now orchestrate complex workflows requiring frequent foundation model calls. In this session, learn how you can reduce latencies to single-digit milliseconds from single-digit seconds with for Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in agentic AI applications using semantic and KV caching, while also reducing the cost incurred from your foundation models for production workloads. By implementing these caching strategies in agentic architectures like RAG-powered assistants and autonomous agents, customers can create performant and cost-effective production-scale agentic AI systems.

title: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
description: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. We'll explore how data partitioning decisions shift when agents are also a target, when Amazon EKS becomes the substrate for both migrations, and which patterns create more debt than they solve when combined wrong. Leave with a framework for the one refactor window you can afford. Bring your questions.

title: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass

title: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
description: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. Tightly coupled dependencies across mainframe and interconnected systems make it nearly impossible to add intelligent capabilities without rearchitecting. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.
