title: Reimagining the Operating Room: Gen AI's Impact on Surgery (sponsored by Deloitte)
description: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
description: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.

title: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
description: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. We built a different path: Ingesting policy, using Large Language Models, and building a formal logic representation, followed by using neurosymbolic techniques to produce a verified rule set, enabling deterministic eligibility decisions with full audit trails. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

title: Reshaping Agentic AI and Business Analytics with Databricks on Intel (sponsored by Intel)
description: Intel and Databricks are collaborating to optimize price-performance for workloads running on AWS. This session covers optimizations for ISVs running Photon/Spark on Databricks leveraging custom Amazon EC2 instances powered by Intel Xeon processors, delivering advanced AI capabilities and high core density. This presentation is brought to you by Intel, an AWS Partner.

title: Resilience for Data Foundations: The Lessons Iceberg Forced Us to Learn (sponsored by Commvault)
description: When customers needed to recover Iceberg environments in production, we discovered that restoring data was often the easy part. Preserving metadata, table state, consistency, and downstream dependencies proved far more challenging than we expected. In this session, Clumio's product and engineering leaders share the assumptions that didn't survive production, the recovery scenarios that surprised us most, and the architectural lessons that emerged along the way. Leave with practical guidance for designing more resilient data foundations on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Commvault, an AWS Partner.

title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
description: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

title: Resolve Amazon ECS incidents faster with AWS DevOps Agent
description: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Resolving and Preventing Production Incidents with AWS DevOps Agent
description: AWS DevOps Agent investigates production incidents end-to-end: tracing failures to the responsible change, guiding the fix, and verifying recovery. Once the service is stable, the agent converts root cause findings into automated prevention rules that enforce mandatory review gates on the same class of risk in future deployments. In this SimuLearn session, experience the full investigate, resolve, and prevent lifecycle as one continuous workflow in a single session.

title: Responsible AI Enablement: Balancing Innovation, Governance and Control (sponsored by Island)
description: Most organizations are currently stuck between two worlds: the urgent need to adopt AI to remain competitive, & the critical mandate to protect corporate data & reputation. AI is evolving faster than any tool in IT history, and faster than any organization can keep up with. The temptation to simply block access to AI is strong, but just saying "No" means ceding the advantage to those able to say "Yes!". The 3 Pillars of a "Secure Yes": Visibility: Knowing what AI is being used across the org. Accountability: Defining who owns the data & the output. Resilience: Building frameworks that adapt as regulations change. In this session, we will outline the framework for secure AI adoption. We will move past the hype to discuss how leaders can build visibility, maintain accountability, and foster a culture of responsible innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Island, an AWS Partner.

title: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera)
description: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
description: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. With the new AWS SDK for Python, async is native, concurrent calls no longer require thread-pool workarounds, and bidirectional streaming enables use cases like live transcription and speech-to-speech that go beyond what's available in boto3 today. Follow along as we put those capabilities to work with clean concurrent calls, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Transcribe streaming, and a practical path to migrating your own code to the new SDK.

title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
description: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
description: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

title: Right tool, right layer: Combining ML models and autonomous agents
description: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.

title: Ring's Security Evolution: From Doorbell to Enterprise Platform (sponsored by Ring LLC)
description: Ring started with a simple mission: make neighborhoods safer with a video doorbell. That mission has scaled — from 100M+ residential cameras to SMB storefronts and jobsites with mobile security towers, to an AI-powered Appstore unlocking entirely new use cases across elder care, workforce analytics, and beyond. Now, Ring is making its boldest leap yet: a cloud-native enterprise platform built on AWS, combining video management, intelligent alerting, third-party camera ingestion, and access control. Join this lightning round to trace Ring's evolution and see what's next for enterprise security. This presentation is brought to you by Ring LLC, an AWS Partner.

title: Rise of Autonomous Clinical Data Management: AI Agents Accelerating Drug Development
description: Explore how autonomous AI agents are transforming clinical data management from a collection of manual processes into an intelligent, continuously learning system that improves quality, accelerates study execution, and shortens the path from protocol to patient impact. Clinical trials generate unprecedented volumes of complex data, yet many Clinical Data Management (CDM) processes remain highly manual, resource-intensive, and constrained by siloed workflows. Critical activities such as protocol interpretation, clinical trial data systems build and configuration, edit check generation, data review, data quality management, reconciliation, and database lock often reside on the critical path to study completion.

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
description: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture behind AWS Specialist Agent: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
description: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture behind AWS Specialist Agent: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. title: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
description: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.

title: Running larger, higher-fidelity quantum experiments on Amazon Braket
description: Amazon Braket offers access to the latest trapped-ion quantum hardware alongside advanced error mitigation techniques, unlocking the largest, highest-fidelity quantum workloads on the platform. In this chalk talk, we demonstrate how error mitigation combines noise-aware transpilation and error suppression to expand usable circuit volume, and how trapped-ion connectivity enables deeper, more complex circuits. We will whiteboard a real workload to estimate cost, runtime, and expected fidelity gains.

title: Running untrusted code in sandboxes with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
description: AI coding assistants generate code. Customers upload plugins. Third parties submit extensions. All of it needs to run somewhere and that somewhere can't be your production environment. In this builders' session, use AWS Lambda MicroVMs to build secure sandboxes that execute untrusted code at scale with hardware-level tenant isolation. You'll configure sandbox lifecycle management, implement resource limits and permissions boundaries, and test failure modes when code misbehaves. Walk away with a working isolation architecture you can adapt for your own multi-tenant workloads. Bring your laptop.

title: Running Vercel in Your Own AWS Account (sponsored by Vercel)
description: This session explores how Vercel Enterprise customers can run workloads in their own AWS account while continuing to use the Vercel developer experience. You’ll learn about the separation between the Vercel control plane and customer runtime, and why this model can help organizations meet data privacy, security, and compliance requirements. You’ll see how the setup works through a live walkthrough and demo, and how this architecture can support broader access to tools like v0, Amazon Q, and other coding agents. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
description: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

title: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
description: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.

title: SAST Is Dead: Program Analysis for AI Agents (sponsored by Semgrep)
description: LLMs didn't kill security testing, they exposed tools that guess at context they don't have. This talk explains what we learned by reinventing program analysis for new end users: builders and agents. We had to develop benchmarks and add determinism with program slicing to better control costs and deliver the optimal price per true vulnerability detected. This presentation is brought to you by Semgrep, an AWS Partner.

title: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
description: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.

title: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
description: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.

title: Scale reinforcement learning globally with sparse weight updates (sponsored by Modal)
description: Reinforcement learning post training usually keeps trainers and rollout workers in one tightly coupled GPU cluster. This talk shows how to keep backpropagation on fast local fabric while moving independent rollout workers to elastic GPU capacity across regions and clouds. The key is to diff weights in the precision actually served, then publish lossless sparse version transitions instead of full checkpoints. Attendees will learn why Adam/Muon updates often disappear under BF16 rounding, how version aware sidecars commit exact weight versions, and how this architecture turns globally available inference capacity into practical reinforcement learning capacity. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

title: Scale Through Partners: The Partner-Led SMB Growth Engine
description: SMB is a $1T opportunity—98% of global businesses are small/mid-size, 81% are increasing AI spend, yet fewer than 300 AWS partners hold the SMB Competency. This session unpacks AWS's Indirect Selling engine: new incentives aligned to growth, AI-powered lead generation, SMB solution selling, and a Partnership Maturity Framework turning opportunistic engagement into repeatable business practice. You'll leave with unit economics proving indirect selling reaches SMBs globally, a clear activation timeline from Opportunity through full Business Practice, and specific first moves to build a scalable, profitable SMB practice on AWS—your 20-minute roadmap to outsized growth.

title: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
description: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
description: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
description: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. title: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
description: Today, organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU instance families. But scaling Spot successfully requires understanding how capacity actually behaves. In this session, the EC2 Spot product leader shares what the data reveals: which diversification strategies consistently deliver high fill rates, how allocation strategies differ for CPU vs. GPU workloads, and when tools like Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager make the difference. You'll leave with a modern playbook covering instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ deployment, checkpointing for long-running jobs, and capacity rebalancing patterns the largest Spot customers use today.

title: Scaling Frontier AI model inference on AWS Trainium
description: Every team moving AI to production hits the same wall: scaling frontier model inference against growing token demand, tighter latency budgets, and spiraling compute costs. This workshop tackles that problem head-on. Experience how purpose-built chips changes the inference economics equation as you deploy Frontier AI models on AWS Trainium, apply optimization techniques, and learn how the Neuron software stack integrates with familiar open-source frameworks - no rewrites required - to achieve superior tokenomics. Leave with actionable skills to run performant, cost-effective model inference at production scale on AWS Trainium.

title: Scaling inference compute across clusters (sponsored by Baseten)
description: Your traffic outgrows a single cluster long before you expect it to. Colin McGrath explains how Baseten runs inference across more than 80 GPU clusters and roughly 15 cloud providers as one system: how capacity gets found and claimed, how requests get routed to the right region under real load, how large models get delivered to new clusters quickly, and how autoscaling behaves when traffic is bursty and cold starts are expensive. He covers what happens when a whole region goes down, and the patterns that matter most for teams scaling past one cluster. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

title: Scaling interactive generative AI at Netflix with AWS Local Zones
description: Generative AI VFX and Animation teams at Netflix require the latest GPU hardware for creative workflows, including real-time rendering, VFX editorial, and color correction. These workloads demand low-latency access to high-performance compute close to creative teams. AWS Local Zones make this possible by placing Amazon EC2 G7e instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in the Los Angeles metro. Netflix's Studio GenAI Infrastructure, including GenAI Sessions and Universal Compute Service, uses Local Zones to serve just-in-time combinations of software and hardware in secure, isolated sandbox environments. Tools like ComfyUI and AI Toolkit with complex dependencies run on task-oriented, elastic GPU assignments, so Netflix scales creative AI workloads efficiently without managing physical infrastructure.

title: Scaling legacy app modernization with autonomous agents
description: Legacy application modernization is a coordination and code generation problem. A large application must be understood, verified, and integrated without losing fidelity. AWS Transform for mainframe reads legacy code and extracts its business rules into traceable specifications that describe what the application does. Learn how AWS Transform overcomes this modernization challenge, and discover the latest capabilities for scaling modernization that compress delivery from days to hours.

title: Scaling Pharma Transformation Through Data-Driven Agentic AI (sponsored by Tech Mahindra)
description: Hear from a leading U.S. pharmaceutical company on its journey to transforming enterprise AI from isolated experiments into a scalable business capability. Discover how Tech Mahindra helped establish trusted data foundations, harness Agentic AI to enrich product and customer master data, unlock semantic intelligence, and create governed data products that power enterprise-wide insights, including drug demand forecasting. This session will explore the architectural principles, governance strategies, and leadership decisions required to scale compliant, trusted, and value-driven AI. Join Tech Mahindra and a pharma industry leader to learn how data-driven Agentic AI is reshaping the future of the intelligent pharma enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by Tech Mahindra, an AWS Partner.

title: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
description: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this chalk-talk, work through how to build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets using AWS temporary credentials and leverage AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.

title: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
description: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.

title: Secure AI Agent Access with AgentCore Identity
description: Not every caller should have access to your AI agents, and you should verify who is calling them before responding. In this hands-on lab, you deploy an IT help desk agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and configure AgentCore Identity to enforce inbound authentication. You set up an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, obtain and decode a JSON Web Token (JWT), and test that the agent rejects unauthenticated callers while allowing verified employees through.

title: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
description: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Continuum for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.

title: Secure by design: the AWS foundation for your AI applications
description: As organizations put AI and agents into production, leaders need confidence that their cloud provider is secure by design. This session explains how AWS foundational security extends into AI services and which AI security capabilities build on that foundation. You see the controls customers use to protect their most critical AI workloads.

title: Secure Coding Agents for Regulated Environments with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Act Security)
description: Learn how HUB International, a top-five global insurance broker, partnered with AWS and Act Security to securely bring autonomous coding agents into a regulated enterprise environment, without giving the agents standing credentials or expanding the attack surface. The team transformed the local Claude Code experience into a secure, per-user cloud sandbox on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preserving the familiar IDE and terminal workflow while moving execution to the cloud. See how OIDC authentication through the corporate IdP, per-call token minting through AgentCore Identity, and Cedar-based authorization for tools exposed through AgentCore Gateway enforce per-user, per-action access. Finally, discover how Act Security sustains least privilege over time and enforces narrower policies - whether you are deploying AgentCore for the first time or hardening an existing environment. This presentation is brought to you by Act Security, an AWS Partner.

title: Secure your CI to operate at machine speed (sponsored by Chainguard)
description: AI agents are changing how software is built, introducing new security challenges across the software supply chain. CI environments are particularly vulnerable, with access to sensitive credentials and elevated permissions. We’ll explore how Chainguard's trusted artifacts, isolated build environments, and integrations with AWS can reduce risk from development through deployment and what securing software delivery looks like when AI agents are doing more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by Chainguard, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing AI agents: Governance patterns for regulated workloads
description: Financial institutions building agentic AI platforms face a fundamental problem: security and governance controls were designed for humans and applications, not autonomous agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the architecture decisions that matter most—covering identity, authorization, secrets, tenancy, and governance—and classify each as a one-way or two-way door. We'll walk through concrete patterns including agent authentication, agent-to-tool authorization, application-layer data segregation, and a multi-source governance model using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail. Leave with decisions you can apply to your own agentic platform.

title: Securing AI agents: Governance patterns for regulated workloads
description: Financial institutions building agentic AI platforms face a fundamental problem: security and governance controls were designed for humans and applications, not autonomous agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the architecture decisions that matter most—covering identity, authorization, secrets, tenancy, and governance—and classify each as a one-way or two-way door. We'll walk through concrete patterns including agent authentication, agent-to-tool authorization, application-layer data segregation, and a multi-source governance model using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail. Leave with decisions you can apply to your own agentic platform.

title: Securing AI Agents on AgentCore
description: A customer runs a support agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that reaches destinations nobody reviewed and takes requests from any caller. In this SimuLearn session, you work the case as their security expert. Behind Amazon API Gateway, AWS WAF Bot Control labels each script and AI crawler, and you write the rule that refuses them with a 403 that names the reason. On the way out, AWS Network Firewall tags every destination by content category. You watch in alert mode, then reject AI and search categories while permitted sites still load. You leave knowing how to classify, then control, what enters and leaves an agent.

title: Securing AI and Autonomous Agents: Protecting the Lifecycle Across Any Platform (sponsored by Fortinet)
description: AI agents are actively running code, accessing databases, and making critical business decisions across every industry. But as these systems gain independence, they also introduce complex security risks throughout their lifecycle. Are you ready to protect a system that learns and acts on its own as your organization embarks on the AI journey? Join our panel of top AI and cybersecurity experts as they break down the end-to-end security of AI systems and agentic applications. We will explore real-world customer challenges and share practical strategies to safeguard autonomous agents across cloud and on-premises environments. This presentation is brought to you by Fortinet, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
description: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defence-in-depth framework spanning five phases - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defence at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, and CodePipeline. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
description: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defence-in-depth framework spanning five phases - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defence at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, and CodePipeline. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

title: Securing Amazon Bedrock agents with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent
description: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement, not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC Interface Endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the Gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll build an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF, and autonomously remediates threats and generating a plain-English incident summary.

title: Securing Amazon Bedrock agents with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent
description: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement, not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC Interface Endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the Gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll build an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF, and autonomously remediates threats and generating a plain-English incident summary.

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
description: Multi-agent systems create a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.

title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
description: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.

title: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong)
description: AI moves fast until it hits production. Then agents that looked solid in a POC start making calls they shouldn't, hammering the vector database, or failing quietly under load, because the API layer underneath wasn't built for it. This session covers what a strong API foundation does for AI at scale: fine-grained authorization keeps context retrieval inside its data privacy boundaries, touching only what it's permitted to touch; rate limiting protects vector databases from resource exhaustion; edge caching cuts query latency without extra engineering; and circuit breaking plus canary deployments let teams ship changes without compromising security or compliance. You'll leave with architectural blueprints and real enterprise examples showing how the right API foundation turns governance from a blocker into what lets AI teams move faster. Presented by Kong an AWS Partner, alongside FanDuel. This presentation is brought to you by Kong, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler)
description: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

title: Security Jam - sponsored by Fortinet
description: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Work through simulated incident response scenarios - including a sponsored challenge from Fortinet to test your skills securing cloud workloads with Fortinet's network and cloud security platform. Can you find the breach and prevent the next one? AWS experts and guided exercises support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Security Jam - sponsored by Semgrep
description: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Work through simulated incident response scenarios - including a sponsored challenge from Semgrep to find and fix code vulnerabilities early using Semgrep's static analysis and code security scanning. Can you find the breach and prevent the next one? AWS experts and guided exercises support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Self-Healing Enterprise-Wipro & AWS Moving from System of Record to System of Action (sponsored by Wipro)
description: For decades, enterprises have invested in technologies that digitize, automate and optimize work. Yet when disruptions occur, decisions still depend on emails, escalations, meetings and manual coordination across teams. The next phase of enterprise transformation is about creating enterprises that can sense change, assess impact, coordinate responses and drive outcomes at speed. Wipro and AWS demonstrate how intelligent agents, enterprise systems and human expertise come together to create a Self-Healing Enterprise, one that can proactively identify issues, orchestrate actions across functions and continuously adapt while keeping humans accountable for critical business decisions. Through a realistic business disruption scenario, see how organizations can evolve beyond visibility and automation towards systems of action that improve resilience, responsiveness and operational efficiency. This presentation is brought to you by Wipro, an AWS Partner.

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge
description: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many have data residency, low latency, and security requirements that depend on running AI closer to their data. This workshop explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while enabling autonomous operations. Learn how to architect, provision, configure, and optimize AI agents that run locally, and how to extend the same architecture to AWS hybrid and edge infrastructure such as AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts.

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge
description: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many have data residency, low latency, and security requirements that depend on running AI closer to their data. This workshop explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while enabling autonomous operations. Learn how to architect, provision, configure, and optimize AI agents that run locally, and how to extend the same architecture to AWS hybrid and edge infrastructure such as AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts.

title: Sell to AI agents through AWS Marketplace
description: Today, buyers are using autonomous AI agents for discovery and digital purchases on their behalf. AWS Marketplace enables buyers' agents to discover partner solutions, transact securely, and meet their enterprise governance controls. As a seller in AWS Marketplace, learn how to sell products that support agentic discovery and procurement to position your offerings for this new frontier.

title: Sell to the AI Buyer, Scale Revenue, and Build Long-Term Value
description: The buying journey is shifting to AI agents and assistants that evaluate and procure software autonomously. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.

title: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
description: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session we cover where existing serverless patterns hold up without modification, what actually changes, and how to start with what you have and add only what you need. See how the calls you already run can become tools that describe themselves to the agent that uses them. Learn how coding agents and skills make best practices part of every build, and where doing less with AI pays off.

title: ServiceNow: The AI Control Tower for Business Reinvention (sponsored by ServiceNow)
description: AI without workflows is just expensive advice. The next generation of AI leaders are moving beyond disconnected copilots and isolated use cases to reinvent how work gets done. Join ServiceNow to learn how the AI Control Tower for Business Reinvention helps organizations govern AI, connect enterprise data, and orchestrate work across every agent, model, and workflow. Discover how AI that thinks and workflows that act enable enterprises to deploy AI quickly while maintaining trust, security, and control. This presentation is brought to you by ServiceNow, an AWS Partner.

title: Serving World Model at scale with AWS Trainium and Native PyTorch
description: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads at scale. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave equipped to take world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.

title: Setting up the Right AI Architecture: Bringing Together Agents, Teams, and Context (sponsored by Notion)
description: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. These different layers have been arranged over many years of procuring tools, but can sometimes feel like a jumbled mess in the AI era. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. This presentation is brought to you by Notion, an AWS Partner.

title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era
description: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.

title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era

title: Ship agents, not chaos: a 90-day pattern for production on AWS. (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
description: AI agents are moving from pilots into production faster than most organizations can govern them, and independent teams building in parallel are creating what practitioners now call agent sprawl. This session presents a repeatable 90-day pattern that converts sprawl into governed agents ready for production, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Guardrails, and Kiro alongside NIST AI RMF and the Well-Architected Generative AI Lens. Architects, platform owners, and public-sector leaders see how a governed runtime, evidence-based mission KPIs, and cost discipline turn compliance into an accelerator. Audit-ready patterns from CDW customer engagements across regulated commercial and public-sector missions are included This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Ship Agents You Can Trust: An Agent Evaluation Framework for Partners
description: Partners shipping production agents at scale need to answer: is this good enough for customers? Agentic transformation doesn't end at build; quality evaluation is the missing layer. In this chalk talk, we walk through an open-source evaluation framework: define test criteria for your agent, run it in a sandbox on Bedrock, calibrate an automated judge against human labels, and track failure rates in CI. For multi-agent systems, attribute failures to the agent that caused them, not where the harm showed up.

title: Ship AI Agents Faster with AgentCore Harness
description: Building a production-ready AI agent meant writing orchestration code, packaging containers, and managing deployment pipelines. AgentCore Harness eliminates all of that. In this hands-on lab, you declare what your agent does through configuration and let AgentCore handle the execution loop. You create a harness agent, iteratively add tools, attach AWS Skills, swap models mid-session to suit your output requirements, and publish versioned endpoints for safe rollout to your customers.

title: Shipping AI Code with Confidence Using Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro (sponsored by Dynatrace)
description: See how Western Governors University uses Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro to deliver AI-generated code with greater confidence. By combining live production intelligence with AI-assisted development, teams can provide agents with real runtime context, detect issues quickly, and create evidence-backed GitHub Issues for rapid remediation. Learn how Bluebox supports the software lifecycle before, during, and after deployment, helping teams validate fixes, reduce risk, and accelerate software delivery. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

title: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
description: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.

title: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
description: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.

title: Simple Governance: How Kiro Makes Enterprise Policies Human-Friendly
description: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.

title: Single Agent to Global Scale: One Postgres, Any Workload, Run by Agents (sponsored by YugabyteDB)
description: An agent needs a Postgres database for perhaps twenty minutes. A payments platform needs one that never goes down across three regions. Most teams cover that range with different products, several vendors, and scores of on-call operators. Yugabyte delivers it as a single stack on AWS. YugabyteDB is distributed PostgreSQL built for global scale and resilience that also scales down to fractional instances. YugabyteDB AMP puts agents in charge of the fleet, handling provisioning, migration, and on-demand tuning. Meko gives agent teams the shared context they run on. See what it takes to run every Postgres workload on one foundation. This presentation is brought to you by YugabyteDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Six Ways AI Fails Who Your Nonprofit Serves — And How to Stop Each One
description: Every AI application touching real people can fail in ways that cause harm. In this chalk talk, we walk one application through six failure modes — PII exposure, phantom citations, out-of-scope advice, unreviewed judgments, hidden bias, and unaccountable decisions — and whiteboard a defense-in-depth architecture using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AgentCore, Automated Reasoning, and human-in-the-loop patterns. Leave with a responsible AI stack applicable to any form factor — chatbot, agent, RAG pipeline, or model call — whether you serve donors, patients, customers, or citizens.

title: Six Ways AI Fails Who Your Nonprofit Serves — And How to Stop Each One

title: Small Language Models, Total Control: Sovereign AI Agents, Lower Cost (sponsored by Boomi)
description: Enterprises are waking up to a hard truth: the AI their business now depends on runs on infrastructure, models, and pricing they don't control. In this session, Boomi's engineering and AI leadership show a different path — AI agents that run anywhere you choose (your Amazon VPC, your data center, behind your firewall) powered by small language models fine-tuned to each agent's job and served entirely on infrastructure you govern. You'll see the full architecture on AWS — Amazon EKS, EC2 GPU instances, Amazon S3, Aurora, MSK, and Amazon Bedrock as a governed escalation path — plus the fine-tuning pipeline (LoRA SFT + DPO), the evaluation gate that decides when a small model is ready, and a live demo of an agent reasoning locally at a fraction of the latency and cost of a frontier LLM. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

title: Small Startup. Big Data. Rare Hopes. (sponsored by Cloudera)
description: Making a big impact always starts small - a dream, an idea, a hope.  Brian Martin - co-founder of Rare Hopes NFP and CTO of Applied AI at Cloudera - will share the story of the non-profit he and industry colleagues founded with the support of AWS, Cloudera, and other companies to deliver a multi-million dollar equivalent platform supporting drug repurposing for rare disease hypothesis generation.  Illustrating the concept and components necessary to deliver this advanced graph analytical approach to transforming knowledge into insights, the story demonstrates the power and potential that AI brings allowing companies to work with knowledge - not just data. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: Smoking on Airplanes: Rethinking How Enterprises Trust Software (sponsored by Glow)
description: Every day, employees install browser extensions, IDE plugins, and open-source packages with powerful access to corporate devices, code, credentials, and data. AI coding agents are accelerating this practice by recommending and installing software to complete tasks. Yet much of it enters the enterprise without comprehensive security review. We've normalized a practice that may someday seem as unthinkable as smoking on airplanes. In this session, we'll expose hidden risks in plugin and package ecosystems, show why traditional application controls miss this rapidly changing software layer, and explore what security teams must rethink as AI makes software adoption faster and increasingly autonomous. This presentation is brought to you by Glow, an AWS Partner.

title: Snowflake: Build a Multi-Engine Architecture on A single AI Ready Governed Data Copy (sponsored by Snowflake)
description: Delivering enterprise analytics and AI requires an architecture designed for operational flexibility not forcing complex data movement. Snowflake's interoperable lakehouse gives teams total agency to query and write to data where it lives using the right engine for every job. This session explores how organizations establish universal open metadata governance powered by Apache Polaris while preserving rich semantic business context across tools. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud simplifies data management, lowers total cost of ownership, and accelerates time to insight for every team, and agent, across your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

title: Spec-Driven AI Development with Kiro
description: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) brings structure, traceability, and human oversight to every phase of high-velocity, Agentic-AI powered software delivery. In this bootcamp, apply AI-DLC in Kiro to build a production application through Feature Specs, control agent behavior with steering files and execution modes, extend capabilities with MCP servers and Kiro Powers, and automate workflows with hooks. Leave with a governed, repeatable process for shipping quality software with AI assistance.

title: Speed Wins: Compress Migration Timelines from Pipeline to Production
description: Enterprises face a wall of technical debt standing between them and the AI opportunity. In this session, learn how AWS Transform helps compressing the entire partner lifecycle — from intelligent prospecting and AI-powered co-sell through to automated delivery and simplified funding — and why first-movers will own disproportionate share of the opportunity.

title: Stop building agents that stop short of action (sponsored by IBM)
description: AI value doesn’t come from creating more agents. It comes from putting agents to work—securely, reliably, and across the systems where business gets done. In this session, see how IBM Bob helps developers build and modernize applications with agentic AI, while watsonx Orchestrate coordinates agents, tools, and workflows across the enterprise. Discover how IBM helps teams move from code and intent to governed action—with the visibility and control needed to scale. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop Building Agents Without Unified Enterprise Context (sponsored by Glean)
description: Many AI programs start with a model, a prompt, and a narrow workflow. They stall when agents need to understand permissions, people, policies, past decisions, and data spread across AWS and SaaS systems. This session shows a different path: establish a governed enterprise context layer and scale the enterprise workflows that prove value. Attendees will learn the elements that make up a robust context platform, what to keep open and flexible, and how to measure whether agents improve real work. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop Moving AWS Data. Turn It into Action with Splunk (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
description: Machine data across AWS environments is growing faster than teams can move, normalize, and analyze it. What if you could stop moving all that data and start putting it to work? In this session, learn how Cisco Data Fabric, powered by Splunk, federates data across AWS and enterprise sources, correlates it at scale, and prepares it for AI and agentic workflows. Through practical architecture patterns and a live demonstration, you’ll see how to reduce data movement and operational cost while turning distributed telemetry into trusted context, faster decisions, and action. This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
description: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of organizations that have deployed an AI agent have rolled it back or shut it down, and the rate rises to 81% among those reporting fully mature guardrails. Getting agents into production got easier. Keeping them there without hurting customers did not. We'll walk through the failure patterns behind rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.

title: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
description: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.

title: Streamlining Claims Processing with Amazon Quick
description: Claims adjusters spend hours retrieving policy data, applying business rules, and drafting decision letters manually. In this SimuLearn session, you use Amazon Quick Automate to orchestrate the entire claims process. You configure REST API and MCP connectors, build a multi-step workflow with Custom Agent steps, and chain together policy retrieval, rules validation, and AI-powered letter generation. The workflow handles missing data gracefully and stores audit-ready decision letters in S3.

title: Take Voice and Image AI into Production with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
description: Build production AI workflows that turn language, vision, voice, and structured data into useful action. This session explores how developers can combine varied enterprise inputs with tool use on Amazon Bedrock. Learn approaches for model routing and evaluation, and explore the security and governance considerations involved in making voice and image workflows dependable in production. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Talk to your market data: Agentic AI meets exchange feeds
description: In this builders’ session, connect an Amazon Bedrock agent layer to a high-performance data pipeline that turns 560M IEX exchange messages into an interactive playground. Analysts describe trading ideas in natural language (no SQL or Python required) while the agent queries Parquet data, generates strategy logic, runs backtests, and returns results. Dig into the C++ parsing, serverless orchestration with AWS Batch and AWS Fargate, Amazon S3, and guardrail patterns that make it production ready. Leave with architecture patterns, a cost model, and a blueprint for adding an agentic layer that takes anyone from market intuition to tested strategy in minutes.

title: Taming AI Token Costs and Security Risks with Cribl and AWS (sponsored by Cribl)
description: Govern enterprise AI: Optimize costs, control prompt risks, and gain visibility with Cribl and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cribl, an AWS Partner.

title: Tapestry, Grupo Boticario & Nestle Purina on agentic commerce
description: AI agents are changing how consumers discover and buy, splitting into two investments: retailers building conversational shopping on their own properties, and consumer goods companies optimizing how their products surface when agents shop on a consumer's behalf. In this session, hear how Tapestry built the Kate Spade AI Gift Concierge that turns luxury gifting into a guided conversation; Grupo Boticario launched an agentic Virtual Assistant orchestrating product discovery and checkout for millions of users; and Nestle Purina implemented an Answer Engine Optimization strategy, using their native chatbot Allie to pressure-test how external AI engines surface proprietary brand data before releasing it into circulation.

title: Teaching agents to pay with Stripe (sponsored by Stripe)
description: AI agents can already search, reason, and call tools. What changes when they can spend money, too? This talk explores the shift from human checkout to machine-native commerce, where payments become part of an agent's reasoning loop. We will look at how agents can discover and purchase products today, then explore Stripe’s Machine Payments Protocol and a future where agents autonomously pay for APIs, compute, data, and other capabilities needed to complete a task. When software becomes the buyer, developers may need to rethink not only checkout, but also how software itself is discovered, priced, and consumed. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

title: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
description: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.

title: Tech debt anonymous: bring your worst code to this chalk talk
description: We all have it: the monolith nobody wants to touch, and the pile of small apps and Lambda functions racking up end-of-life notices. This chalk talk is your support group. Bring your real modernization headaches and we'll discuss how AWS Transform tackles the whole spectrum. On one side, Transform custom handles the big, complex jobs: decomposing Java and .NET monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at scale. On the other, continuous modernization autonomously scans thousands of repositories, prioritizes what's drifting, and opens remediation pull requests on a schedule. Bring questions about your own portfolio and leave with a plan of attack.

title: Techniques for Cost-Optimized Video Understanding on AWS
description: Video understanding unlocks powerful insights from media assets, but cost concerns often slow adoption. In this hands-on session, we walk through practical techniques for building cost-optimized video understanding pipelines on AWS. You'll learn how to reduce inference costs, right-size your architecture, and accelerate time to value without sacrificing accuracy. Whether you're processing thousands of hours of content for metadata enrichment, content moderation, or search, these patterns help you scale AI-driven video analysis while keeping your bill predictable.

title: Techniques for Cost-Optimized Video Understanding on AWS
description: Video understanding unlocks powerful insights from media assets, but cost concerns often slow adoption. Whether you're processing thousands of hours of content for metadata enrichment, content moderation, or search, these patterns help you scale AI-driven video analysis while keeping your bill predictable.

title: Tekion: Reinventing automotive retail with agentic AI on AWS
description: Automotive retail runs on complex, menu-driven workflows — scheduling service, ordering parts, structuring deals, closing books. Tekion, whose cloud-native platform powers thousands of dealerships, reimagined it as conversational AI, the industry's first AI-native automotive DMS. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Tekion's production agents — spanning sales, service, parts, F&I, and accounting — execute actions rather than suggesting them, serving every role from service advisor to dealer principal. Learn how Tekion architected a reusable agent platform, applied guardrails for safe autonomy, and turned industry operations AI-native.

title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
description: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
description: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. title: The AgentCore Governance Loop: Policy, Guardrails, Observability
description: Building an agent takes an afternoon. Operating it safely across a team takes architecture. In this session learn how to build a multi-agent reference platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and walk the full governance loop including cataloging agents for discovery, enforcing what they can do with Cedar policy at the gateway, filtering what they can say with Guardrails, and tracing behavior through observability. You will learn where the pieces integrate cleanly and where the seams break. You leave with a governance reference architecture you can adapt to any agentic workload, plus the lessons the documentation leaves out.

title: The Agent Harness: Unifying Fragmented Tools for Mission AI Advisors
description: Advisors across mission-driven organizations—financial advisors, benefits navigators, program coordinators—juggle fragmented tools, manual research, and delayed plan delivery while clients go underserved. AI agents change this equation. See how to collapse this fragmentation into configuration using the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. Learn to securely plug domain-specific skills and disparate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly into the harness to generate tailored action plans in real time. Then, deploy the agent to isolated microVM sessions utilizing native memory strategies and Bedrock Guardrails. Leave with sample configurations, deployment patterns, and blueprints for building production advisors that scale.

title: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
description: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

title: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action
description: MSPs managing hundreds of customer environments can no longer rely on manual, reactive workflows. In this hands-on workshop, MSP teams will deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — using natural language to monitor, diagnose, and remediate issues across accounts in real time. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. The session covers agent-to-agent coordination, cross-account operations, and MCP-based tool access. MSPs will leave with a production-ready blueprint to transform operations from reactive to agentic. Laptops required — everyone builds live.

title: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action
description: MSPs managing hundreds of customer environments can no longer rely on manual, reactive workflows. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. title: The Agentic MSP: How AI Compounds Customer Outcomes at Every Layer
description: The most profitable Managed Services Providers aren't just using AI internally. They're creating a compounding cycle: automate your own operations with Agentic AI, deliver measurably better outcomes to customers, then help those customers adopt AI themselves so the results multiply. This session shows how the AWS Managed Services Provider Program rewards that progression, from foundational automation through outcome-based delivery powered by AI agents. Leave with your own assessment and a concrete plan to reach the next level.

title: The agentic restaurant: AI agents that run your kitchen
description: The restaurant industry is transforming as AI agents move from pilots to production. Leading QSR and casual dining brands are deploying a "virtual general manager," multiple specialized agents orchestrated together to optimize drive-thru ordering, kitchen workflows, labor scheduling, and guest experience in real time. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, with Amazon Nova Sonic powering voice ordering at sub-2-second latency. We design a supervisor agent coordinating specialists across drive-thru, kitchen prep, inventory, and labor scheduling. Explore how agents share context, resolve conflicts, validate decisions against synthetic personas before deployment, and maintain human-in-the-loop oversight. Bring your architecture challenges.

title: The Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Postman)
description: Autonomous agents are no longer assisting the software development lifecycle. They are rewriting it. When agents write, review, test, and ship code at machine speed, the SDLC stops being a sequence of human handoffs and becomes a control problem. This session covers the failure modes that only appear at scale: review queues that no human can absorb, test suites that validate the wrong invariants, provenance gaps that make incidents unexplainable, and CI/CD pipelines built for tens of commits a day now absorbing thousands. It closes with the specific architectural decisions engineering leaders should be making now, drawn from our own experience running agents in production. This presentation is brought to you by Postman, an AWS Partner.

title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
description: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."

title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
description: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."

title: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
description: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

title: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
