In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

title: The Capability Overhang: Ask More of the Frontier (sponsored by Anthropic)
description: Frontier models can do more than anyone asks of them. At Anthropic, the hardest part of testing a new model is finding work hard enough to make it fail. Outside, most teams hand Claude the tasks they gave last year's model. This session closes that gap: what the newest Claude models do on AWS when you delegate the job, not the task. Multi-day autonomous work, large migrations end to end, agents that verify their results and keep going. Evals, live demos, and how our researchers keep raising the bar. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: The Control Plane for Your Agent Workforce: Governance, Cost and ROI at Scale (sponsored by Cognition)
description: Cognition has rolled out Devin, the autonomous software engineer, at the world's largest Fortune 500 companies. Along the way, we learned that scaling an agent workforce hinges on three questions every enterprise asks: How do we onboard agents? How do we know they're delivering value? How do we ensure they only do what they're supposed to? Drawing from real deployments, this session introduces the practical patterns we developed to answer them — governance, cost controls, ROI measurement, and federated configurations. You'll leave with a playbook for turning agents from a promising pilot into a trusted, scaled workforce. This presentation is brought to you by Cognition, an AWS Partner.

title: The EBA cloud party: compete to build agentic migration solutions
description: The cloud journey isn't just about migration anymore. It's about building intelligent frameworks that transform how organizations operate. In this gamified Experience-Based Acceleration (EBA) workshop, cross-functional teams compete in real time to architect migration and modernization solutions, build agentic AI workflows that automate at scale, and deploy AI-powered applications on AWS. Push boundaries, solve real challenges together, and have fun doing it. Walk away with battle-tested architectures, agentic automation patterns, and a cloud-fluent mindset your team can adopt immediately. Ready to play?

title: The Economics of an AWS Partner: Revenue, Incentives & AWS Marketplace
description: A forward-looking session reframing Partner economics for the year ahead. Revenue measurement is no longer just tracking, it's the backbone connecting all AWS Partner Programs. Walk away with a clear action plan to position for next year’s benefits.

title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
description: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

title: The Frontier Doesn't Hold Still: Running Claude Agents at Scale on AWS (sponsored by Anthropic)
description: Enterprises are moving faster with AI than ever. And they're falling further behind. Once the first agents land and the numbers look good, most teams turn to cost control while the frontier keeps moving. This session covers how to do both with Claude on AWS: the security and compliance controls enterprises require, execution inside your own boundary, observability and cost governance, and the safeguards that let you trust agents with more. Then how to keep expanding what agents do as new models arrive, so efficiency doesn't become the ceiling. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
description: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.

title: The Governance Gap Keeping AI Agents Out of Production (sponsored by WSO2)
description: Every leader is under pressure to show AI value now. Some move fast, and agents sprawl across teams with no shared controls. Others lock everything down, and pilots never reach production. Both point to the same gap: governance maturity hasn't kept pace with agent speed. This talk covers how governance becomes an accelerator, not a blocker, to production AI. You’ll learn how to design identity, policy, and guardrails from day one, so agents ship with the same controls whether they run on AWS Bedrock, hybrid, or otherwise. Get the principles right early, and agents move from pilot to production without every team reinventing governance on their own. Takeaways: Why AI programs sprawl or stall, and what governance maturity looks like in between. How trusted AI governance turns into speed instead of slowing teams down. What governance principles to design in from day one, on AWS & beyond. This presentation is brought to you by WSO2, an AWS Partner.

title: The latest innovations in multicloud agent security
description: AI agents are showing up everywhere your teams work, and security teams also want to keep pace. In this session, explore the latest innovations in securing AI across multicloud environments. See how AWS is thinking about the challenges security teams face as AI is used by teams, and the direction it is taking to help them stay ahead. Walk away with a clearer picture of where AI security is heading and practical ways to get ahead of it in your own organization.

title: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
description: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.

title: The Next Phase of AI for SRE: Distributed Reasoning for Enterprise Operations (sponsored by Ciroos)
description: AI for SRE isn’t just a speed or accuracy problem; it’s a problem of deeper understanding. This session explores how team members across different domains in an enterprise can use a shared AI reasoning layer to operate production systems and collaborate effectively to increase reliability. We’ll show how this AI reasoning layer handles the extremes of alert storms and alert silence, catching deployment-triggered anomalies before they cause production impact. Learn how teams are moving beyond reactive dashboards, using state-of-the-art techniques to instantly correlate cross-domain telemetry, execute complex investigations, and achieve proactive reliability in dynamic cloud and hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Ciroos, an AWS Partner.

title: The Physical AI Blueprint: A Full-Stack Solution with AWS and NVIDIA (sponsored by NVIDIA)
description: Get hands-on building a complete Physical AI pipeline using the AWS and NVIDIA toolchain. This workshop walks you through each stage—synthetic data generation with Isaac Sim, foundation model training with GR00T and Cosmos, digital twin simulation in Omniverse, edge deployment via IoT Greengrass, multi-robot orchestration with AgentCore, and continuous learning with SageMaker using NVIDIA OSMO. Walk away with a working blueprint you can apply to manufacturing, logistics, or autonomous systems. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: The Trade Desk's Cloud Journey: AI-Assisted Optimization to AI Agents
description: The Trade Desk operates a real-time advertising platform on AWS, where infrastructure must handle massive scale while making bidding decisions in milliseconds. At that volume, cloud cost optimization is a continuous discipline, not a one-time audit. In this breakout, The Trade Desk shares how it moved from manual cost audits to an AI-assisted approach: an internal MCP server that lets AI agents investigate cost and usage data, surface savings across services like S3, NAT Gateway, EBS, and Graviton, and apply a repeatable method for optimizing workloads over time. You'll see how the team structured the agents, what they found, and where the approach is headed.

title: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
description: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

title: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
description: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. We walk through a practical path from "I have a serverless app" to "my app has agent capabilities," adding capabilities incrementally without rewriting what already works. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard where agents fit in what you've already built.

title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB)
description: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with three architectural changes on AWS: Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Threat detection and IR in AgentCore workloads
description: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

title: Threat modeling the agentic SDLC: from user story to deployment
description: "Threat modeling the agentic SDLC with ThreatForest Agentic development is speeding up, and traditional threat modeling assumes a person makes the decisions. In this code talk, you follow one process end to end. You threat model a user story with the autonomous threat modeling built into AWS Continuum, carry it through the developer workflow, and take it to deployment. You see how ThreatForest, an agentic tool built on the Strands framework, generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings on its own, and how to build a mitigations catalog your organization can reuse. We also show where traditional threat modeling can be used for agentic systems."

title: Token Counts to Business Impact: Measurable AI Architectures at Scale
description: As AI workloads scale, the question shifts from "what does this cost?" to "is this delivering real value?" The answer depends on your workload, architecture, and adoption maturity. We present progressive architecture patterns using agentic software development — from vibe-coding to cloud agents to self-hosted inference to custom models — with a live demo across the AWS AI Stack, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker HyperPod, and Trainium, showing how the right metrics evolve with your architecture. You'll leave with cost-per-outcome comparisons, spend controls that work at scale, and an ROI measurement framework with architecture patterns to implement across any AI workload.

title: Token-efficient retrieval for production AI agents (sponsored by Exa)
description: Most agent bills aren't driven by the model,  they're driven by the context it's given. Raw web pages, HTML boilerplate, and 10 blue links padded with irrelevant text quietly multiply token spend and degrade answer quality. This lightning talk walks through how Exa engineered retrieval to hand LLMs exactly the text they need: neural search that returns precise passages instead of whole pages, highlight extraction tuned to the query, and context-budgeting techniques that cut input tokens dramatically without hurting accuracy. Using real production traces, we'll show how token-efficient retrieval changes the economics of agents at scale on AWS, and give you a practical checklist you can apply to any RAG or agent pipeline this week. This presentation is brought to you by Exa, an AWS Partner.

title: Tokenomics for AI on AWS: Local inference plus Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Spectro Cloud)
description: Power users in AI teams building on AWS face the challenge of frontier models delivering the best answers and token costs scaling with adoption. Not every prompt requires frontier models. The ones that do, belong on the best endpoint. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. We will show how routing, quotas, and per-team attribution keep tokenomics predictable, so platform teams can enable AI adoption without inheriting the bill. This presentation is brought to you by Spectro Cloud, an AWS Partner.

title: Tokenomics: Understanding What Your AI Actually Costs (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
description: Your AI pilot ran smoothly and stayed on budget. Then you launched, and the invoice was much higher than the estimate. This session breaks down why that happens and what to do about it. We'll walk through where AI spend actually goes once a system leaves the demo stage, why agentic AI costs differently than a simple chatbot, and how choosing the right model for each task, not just the flagship model for everything, can cut spend dramatically without hurting quality. You'll leave with a practical framework for tracking cost, avoiding common budgeting traps, and having a more confident conversation with finance the next time AI spend comes up. This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
description: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
description: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

title: Transform Episodic Content into High-Converting Microdramas
description: Turn your episodic content into binge-worthy microdramas. In this session, you'll learn how to build both single- and multi-episode formats, multiply one source into a library of platform-ready content assets, and monetize a story in multiple ways including advertising, subscription, and social distribution. We'll walk through scroll-stopping production techniques optimized for vertical, mobile-first viewing, and the pacing and cliffhanger patterns that drive completion and re-watch rates. Leave with a repeatable workflow for producing microdrama series at scale and a clear playbook for turning your existing catalog into high-converting, platform-ready short-form videos.

title: Transforming Customer Experiences Through Tapestry’s Order Management (sponsored by Digitate)
description: Customers expect fast, personalized, and seamless experiences across every interaction with a brand. For Tapestry, connecting consumer feedback, sentiment, and operational signals is key to identifying issues that can impact customer experience and brand reputation. In this session, Sonal Sharan will share how Tapestry is leveraging ignio's AI Agents to continuously analyze these signals, surface emerging concerns, and provide real-time visibility into business-impacting issues. Intelligent workflows help prioritize and route issues for faster resolution, while actionable insights support more proactive customer engagement, resulting in a more connected, responsive, and customer-centric organization delivering exceptional experiences across Tapestry’s leading brands. This presentation is brought to you by Digitate, an AWS Partner.

title: Transforming legacy core to agentic AI with Nissan & Bread Financial
description: Legacy mainframe applications were built for stability, scale, and batch-oriented processing, but they were never designed to power real-time, intelligent, agentic experiences. Modernization changes that. Discover how Nissan reimagined core operations into a cloud-native platform designed for responsiveness, adaptability, and AI-ready workflows. Hear how Bread Financial is evolving beyond credit-processing architectures to accelerate innovation by decomposing monolithic capabilities into bounded context services, creating a modern foundation for autonomous workflows. See how both used AWS Transform to extract business rules from decades-old applications and Kiro to forward-engineer production-ready code. Learn how modernized applications unlock the architecture that makes agentic AI possible.

title: Transforming Patient Engagement with AI and Cloud (sponsored by Incedo Inc.)
description: Life sciences organizations are reimagining patient engagement through cloud data and artificial intelligence. This session explores how generative AI and intelligent automation can help create more connected personalized and responsive patient experiences across the patient journey. Drawing on real world transformation experiences the discussion will highlight practical opportunities to improve patient engagement reduce friction and enable more proactive interactions while addressing the data governance and adoption considerations required to scale AI responsibly. Attendees will gain practical perspectives on how life sciences organizations can move from AI experimentation to scalable solutions that deliver meaningful patient and business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Incedo Inc., an AWS Partner.

title: Transform your SaaS for the agentic AI era on Amazon ECS
description: Your multi-tenant SaaS application runs on Amazon ECS. Now your customers expect AI-powered features but adding agents to an existing platform introduces new challenges. Including tenant isolation for model access, per-tenant memory and conversation state, cost attribution across shared infrastructure, and agent orchestration at scale. In this workshop, you start with a working SaaS application on Amazon ECS and progressively add agentic capabilities using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement tenant-aware agent routing, configure isolated tool execution with ECS task-level security boundaries, add persistent memory per tenant, and instrument with end-to-end observability. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Trust at Scale: Unlocking Enterprise Agentic AI (sponsored by Qlik)
description: Agentic AI dies at scale. It is easy to get one agent working on one dataset for one team. The challenge is trusting its answers across hundreds of thousands of users, regions, languages, regulators, and constantly changing data. AWS provides global infrastructure, security, data residency, and compliance controls to scale AI. Qlik provides trusted governed data, business context, and intelligence that agents can rely on. See how Amazon Bedrock and the Qlik MCP Server bring trusted Qlik intelligence to production agents and any LLM including Amazon Quick. Learn how enterprises can scale agentic AI without sacrificing trust governance or choice. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

title: Trusted intent: How Kiro proves your specs before writing any code
description: Your AI agent writes code fast, but is it building what you actually meant? Kiro's requirements analysis goes far beyond asking an LLM to generate a spec. It combines auto-formalization, SMT solvers, and neuro-symbolic techniques to mathematically detect ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. In this session, learn how we turned decades of formal methods into a developer experience that feels like answering simple yes/no questions while catching the bugs that cost the most to fix.

title: Trusting an Autonomous Agent With Your Production Environment (sponsored by NeuBird AI)
description: The biggest barrier to autonomous operations isn't capability, it's trust.Handing an incident to an autonomous agent raises a fair question. How do you know it is not guessing from raw log lines. This session shows how NeuBird AI reasons over your live environment and shows the causal chain behind every root cause, not a coincidence in the metrics. We’ll examine the guardrails that make production deployment safe: VPC-native execution, zero external data retention, complete auditable reasoning paths, and human-gated action approvals. Learn how to safely transition from human-driven triage to trusted, autonomous production operations on your own terms. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird AI, an AWS Partner.

title: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants
description: Partners are building agentic consulting practices with human consultants, but what if they could deliver 10x more engagements by augmenting their teams with consulting agents? In this hands-on builders' session, work alongside a team of consulting agents that guide a human consultant through structured discovery — asking the right questions and validating assumptions — then build out business requirements, generate agent designs and AWS architectures, calculate ROI-backed financial models, and export ready-to-use Statement of Work — all in a single, AI-accelerated workflow you can take straight back to your practice.

title: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants
description: Partners are building agentic consulting practices with human consultants, but what if they could deliver 10x more engagements by augmenting their teams with consulting agents? In this hands-on builders' session, work alongside a team of consulting agents that guide a human consultant through structured discovery — asking the right questions and validating assumptions — then build out business requirements, generate agent designs and AWS architectures, calculate ROI-backed financial models, and export ready-to-use Statement of Work — all in a single, AI-accelerated workflow you can take straight back to your practice.

title: Turn autonomous agents into accountable ones
description: Your AI agents pass the demo but struggle in production because of limited accountability and controls. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard a governance framework that closes the loop. You get governed agent accounts with AWS Control Tower, hard API boundaries with AWS Organizations policies, and runtime tool-access controls and behavior scoring in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AWS Config detects drift from policy and triggers automated rollback. You leave with a repeatable, observe-score-remediate pattern for keeping AI agents operating within your policies."

title: Turn AWS Security Signals into Action with AI-First SecOps (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
description: Security teams operating on AWS need a faster path from signals to action without adding more operational complexity. In this session, Splunk and AWS will explore a new approach to cloud and AI-native security operations designed for faster onboarding, earlier detection, and more efficient investigation and response. You’ll leave with practical insights into AI-first SecOps and how AWS-centered security teams can improve outcomes, regardless of the size or maturity of their security operations. This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Turning Data into Decisions: Pacific Life's Modern Insurance Operations with AWS AI (sponsored by PwC)
description: Abstract: PwC-built Generative AI data processing solution for Pacific Life Re, hosted on AWS. The solution automates the ingestion, transformation, validation, schema mapping, and PII redaction of client actuarial datasets that arrive in different formats, languages, and quality levels. In short, it helps PLRe move from manual, time-consuming data preparation to a secure, auditable, AI-enabled workflow that can reduce processing times from weeks to days, improve data quality, and provide clean, validated outputs for actuarial, pricing, and R&D teams. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Turning Pharma Field Insights into Enterprise Intelligence (sponsored by ZS)
description: Learn how ZS and AWS help pharma teams turn field insights into AI-powered intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.

title: Uncover the Opportunity. Build the AI Agent. Scale It Live. (sponsored by NiCE)
description: Your CX data already knows where automation will pay off. See Agentic Analytics pinpoint the opportunity, then watch that recommendation become a working AI agent — built, tested, and scaled live.  This presentation is brought to you by NiCE, an AWS Partner.

title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
description: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy

title: Unifying fragmented data: A lakehouse for the agentic AI era
description: Financial services organizations face growing data volumes, strict regulations, and architectures where siloed warehouses and separate data lakes fragment data, drive up costs, and slow insights. In this chalk talk, we walk through a modern Lakehouse architecture on AWS that combines the cost benefits of data lakes with the governance and performance of data warehouses. We explain how Amazon S3 Tables with managed Apache Iceberg and AWS Glue Catalog semantic search deliver a single governed data foundation supporting agentic AI, traditional AI/ML, and analytics workloads. Learn practical patterns for a scalable Lakehouse you can apply immediately.

title: Unlock cost efficiency with Graviton savings tools
description: While AWS Graviton delivers up to 40% better price-performance, uncovering those savings across your fleet shouldn't take weeks of manual analysis. Building a concrete migration plan for a specific environment is where teams get stuck. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities over time. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill that any AI coding agent can run against your accounts to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. This lightning talk demonstrates both tools against a real-world scenario, showing how to analyze compute usage, visualize potential savings, and turn efficiency insights into actionable migration plans you can use to accelerate your Graviton adoption.

title: Unlocking SAP Data with AI: From Zero-ETL to Agentic Automation
description: Critical business data remains locked inside SAP ERP and BW systems, limiting real-time insights and AI-driven automation. In this hands-on workshop, learn how to break down data silos using a modern, cost-effective architecture without expensive ETL pipelines. Explore a unified analytics strategy spanning Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services that enables end-to-end SAP data modernization. Then, build with the AWS for SAP MCP Server, enabling agentic AI to orchestrate across SAP, Salesforce, and AWS without writing code.

title: Unlock intelligent AI with MCP-powered agentic Neptune graph reasoning
description: Graph-based agentic reasoning empowers AI systems to dynamically interact with the rich context and relationships in an Amazon Neptune graph, enabling intelligent, flexible, and scalable AI solutions that extract valuable insights from complex, interconnected data. In this session, build a generative AI application for investment analysis spanning the full lifecycle, from raw unstructured data to autonomous AI agents, by combining Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Construct autonomous AI workflows that extract entities and relationships from raw EDGAR data, build a domain knowledge graph, surface actionable insights from graph relationships, and build an agent to find investment analysis trends. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Unlock intelligent AI with MCP-powered agentic Neptune graph reasoning
description: Graph-based agentic reasoning empowers AI systems to dynamically interact with the rich context and relationships in an Amazon Neptune graph, enabling intelligent, flexible, and scalable AI solutions that extract valuable insights from complex, interconnected data. In this session, build a generative AI application for investment analysis spanning the full lifecycle, from raw unstructured data to autonomous AI agents, by combining Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Construct autonomous AI workflows that extract entities and relationships from raw EDGAR data, build a domain knowledge graph, surface actionable insights from graph relationships, and build an agent to find investment analysis trends. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Unlock your Graviton savings potential using AI and analytics tools
description: How much can you save by migrating to Graviton? In this builder session, explore a real-world scenario and uncover two ways to answer that question. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill any AI coding agent can run to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. Deploy both hands-on, identify migration candidates, and see how quickly cost data becomes a migration strategy. Walk away with actionable insights and a deployment kit.

title: Use AWS Continuum to move from annual pentesting to continuous security
description: AI coding tools can make developers 10–20x more productive and yet many organizations may only be able to pentest critical apps once a year. The rest need to go untested entirely. In this builders' session, use AWS Security Agent (now part of Continuum) to run an on-demand penetration test against a live application. You'll triage findings by exploitability, validate real-world impact, and apply automated code remediations. Leave with prescriptive next steps to scan your own applications using a frontier AI agent that secures workloads from design through deployment. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Using AI for Impact: Achieving Sustainability and ROI on AWS
description: AI is accelerating sustainability at unprecedented speed, but only if the infrastructure behind it keeps pace. In this session, we will explore how AWS makes AI infrastructure more sustainable through hardware design decisions that minimize embodied carbon, custom silicon optimized for energy efficiency, and ML-driven data center optimization. Amazon Operations will show how AI and ML turn facility maintenance into prescriptive, autonomous operations: optimizing HVAC, water, and utilities for greater equipment reliability, and sustainability. Leave with a clear understanding of the AWS services powering these solutions, how AWS is building a more sustainable infrastructure, and how to get started with tracking and reducing your environmental impact.

title: Using AI to scale legacy app modernization with Experian & Itaú
description: A successful modernization approach only matters if it scales beyond the first pilot. Experian and Itaú share how they grew their approach with AWS Transform and Kiro from a single engagement into an enterprise-wide operating model. Experian compresses mainframe analysis from months to days, then standardizes modernization across 550+ workloads and multiple regions with a fully agentic reverse-engineering pipeline. Itaú expanded to 43 business domains, processing nearly 140 million lines of code in a single month. Leave with the operating models that scale modernization from one application to the entire portfolio, unlocking AI-driven capabilities along the way.

title: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS (sponsored by Deloitte)
description: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
description: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.

title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
description: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.

title: VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts with AWS Transform
description: Many organizations struggle to migrate VMware workloads due to complex dependencies, network translation challenges, and the need to support both cloud and on-premises targets. In this workshop, you use AWS Transform MGN, an agentic AI service, to execute an end-to-end VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts. You work through AI-driven discovery, dependency mapping, intelligent wave planning, automated network conversion, and orchestrated execution. See how Trianz's Concierto platform also integrates with AWS Transform to streamline migration to AWS Outposts with automated orchestration and operational governance.

title: Warehouse Alchemy: How Eni's AI agents cut days of sourcing to minutes
description: Eni operates one of the world's most complex upstream supply chains, managing exploration and production materials across warehouses on multiple continents. Tubular items alone represent €1.5 billion out of a €2.5 billion inventory — scattered across dozens of facilities with fragmented visibility. Engineers searching for available spare parts faced a manual, days-long process of cross-referencing spreadsheets, navigating import restrictions, certifications, third-party stock, and delivery schedules — often resulting in unnecessary new purchases while surplus materials sat idle in distant warehouses. With Eni's expansion into fast-track development, biofuel production, and CCUS, the traditional material management approach couldn't keep pace with the speed and complexity of global operations.

title: Watch AWS Transform convert SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL live
description: Modernizing SQL Server and its dependent .NET applications to Aurora PostgreSQL typically requires months of manual effort across schema conversion, stored procedure rewriting, and application code changes. In this code talk, see how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to automate this journey end-to-end. Through a live walkthrough, we'll showcase complex schema transformations, T-SQL to PL/pgSQL stored procedure conversions, Entity Framework provider updates, and wave-based orchestration of multi-database estates with human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints. Ask questions throughout. Leave with patterns for modernizing SQL Server at scale.

title: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
description: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.

title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
description: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

title: What Observability at the Speed of AI Looks Like (sponsored by groundcover)
description: For a company like Polymarket, moving fast isn’t a nice-to-have. It’s a requirement. Failing to scale quickly enough can stall unprecedented momentum, while compromising its PII and security posture can carry even greater risk. Built on AWS, this session explores how Polymarket uses groundcover to shift infrastructure responsibilities to AI agents, build agentic development loops, maintain full data residency, and gain instant visibility into every change, no matter how quickly production evolves. We’ll also share the immediate impact: at least 50% lower MTTR for infrastructure escalations and an approximately 7% reduction in Polymarket’s AWS bill. This presentation is brought to you by groundcover, an AWS Partner.

title: What's new in full-stack AWS app development
description: Web developers are under pressure to deliver differentiating experiences to more users, faster than ever. Building secure, reliable, scalable applications at 10x speed takes solutions that let developers start easily, ship quickly, and iterate without friction. In this breakout, we'll share how AWS is evolving to meet the needs of modern full-stack developers from defining backends in code and connecting real-time data, to deploying and scaling globally with minimal overhead. Join us to see what's new and where full-stack development on AWS is headed.

title: What's new with Amazon API Gateway
description: Your next API consumer might not be a person. AI agents, MCP servers, and coding assistants are calling APIs programmatically, and they need machine-readable schemas, predictable error contracts, and discoverable endpoints. In this session, we cover what's new with Amazon API Gateway: recent launches, direct service integrations that eliminate Lambda glue code, declarative event wiring, and patterns from real customer deployments. We also discuss how to design APIs that serve both human developers and autonomous agents without maintaining separate interfaces.

title: What's new with Amazon S3... and now files!
description: Twenty years of redefining storage, and Amazon S3 continues to evolve beyond objects to serve you wherever you are and however you work with data. This session highlights that evolution, led by the convergence of object and file storage with the launch of S3 Files, delivering full file system access to your S3 data without sacrificing scalability or economics you expect from S3. We also explore S3 Vectors for AI workloads, S3 Metadata for richer data discovery, and S3 Tables for managed Apache Iceberg data lakes. Come see what’s launched, what’s next, and how to put it all to work.

title: What's new with NVIDIA GPUs in Amazon EC2
description: A large-scale AI workload can run for weeks across thousands of interconnected GPUs, where a single failure or security gap can be costly. Amazon EC2 brings together a portfolio of accelerated computing instances and innovations that keep the most demanding AI workloads secure by default and resilient to failures and maintenance. In this session, discover what's new in the AWS accelerated compute portfolio and dive deep into the architecture behind the latest generation of GPU instances for training and inference across large language and multimodal models. Hear real-world examples of how leading companies build on AWS, and leave understanding how AWS accelerated computing enables AI at scale.

title: What's new with OpenSearch: AI-native search, agents & observability
description: "The OpenSearch project has shipped its most transformative year ever. From agentic search with autonomous relevance tuning and persistent memory, to GPU-accelerated vector search with 58% throughput gains, to a reimagined observability stack with Prometheus and Apache Iceberg support, the 3.x release train delivers capabilities builders can use today. OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits and TSC Chair Andrew Ross walk you through what's new, what it means for your architecture, and how to put it to work, whether you're building RAG pipelines, deploying monitoring, or creating AI agents."

title: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
description: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.

title: When agentic AI meets critical infrastructure (sponsored by IBM)
description: Agentic AI can transform how utilities serve customers, manage infrastructure and respond to operational events. Join IBM Consulting and industry leaders to see how organizations are putting agentic AI to work on AWS across complex operational workflows. Through real client stories, explore how modern platforms, trusted data and secure software foundations help teams improve service, strengthen resilience and move AI into production with confidence. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
description: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

title: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
description: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.

title: When AI Moves Money: Secure the Agentic Future of Financial Services (sponsored by TrendAI™)
description: Organizations are racing to adopt AI, but many struggle to balance innovation, governance, and security. In this session, learn how Discover how technology leaders are enabling AI innovation while reducing operational risk and complexity. enterprises are using TrendAI Vision One on AWS to accelerate AI initiatives, gain visibility across complex cloud environments, and reduce operational risk without slowing the business. Discover real-world deployment patterns, lessons learned, and the architectural principles that help security teams move from reactive defense to proactive risk management while enabling AI at scale. Built on AWS-native services and integrated across the cloud ecosystem, this approach helps organizations simplify operations, improve threat detection, and confidently embrace the next wave of transformation. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: When Guardrails Break: Defense in Depth for Non-Deterministic AI (sponsored by Darktrace)
description: Organizations are deploying copilots, AI agents, and LLM-driven workflows faster than governance and security can adapt. Non-deterministic AI creates a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data, and runtime behavior, and acts as both defensive force multiplier and adversarial accelerant. Static guardrails are necessary but insufficient: they miss novel behavior, unsafe tool use, and risk that only surfaces when AI interacts with identities and downstream systems. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI at runtime, using NIST's Secure/Defend/Thwart framing: an identity control plane for agents, least-privilege and JIT access, runtime observability, behavior detection, and autonomous investigation and containment. We'll share a blueprint for a minimum viable AI security baseline, and why behavioral oversight is the decisive layer for securing AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Darktrace, an AWS Partner.

title: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
description: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

title: When Software Builds and Improves Itself (sponsored by Factory)
description: Software is becoming more than something companies build. It is becoming the system through which they improve. The next generation of software factories will turn business signals into production software, measure the outcomes, and use those outcomes to improve each cycle of development. Engineers set the goals, architecture, policies, and approval gates, while the system handles execution and continuously improves itself. Factory cofounder Eno Reyes will share what this future looks like, what has to be true to build it, and why self-improving software will fundamentally change how every company operates. This presentation is brought to you by Factory, an AWS Partner.

title: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT)
description: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.

title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
description: Not every workflow needs an agent, and applying agentic AI where it doesn’t fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. We’ll ideate on a scoring framework that assesses the inherent nature of the work to reveal where agentic approaches thrive. You’ll apply the PERCEIVE-REASON-ACT pattern for isolating AI reasoning from orchestration, and walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately.

title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
description: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Who Checks the Agents? Quality and Governance for the Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Qodo)
description: Agents now plan work, write code, generate tests and open PRs—sometimes without human review before production. Yet most teams rely on a trust model built for a slower SDLC: one reviewer, one merge gate and one chance to catch what went wrong. That model fails when agents operate at every stage and final review can’t reveal what happened upstream. This session treats trust as a property of the pipeline, not a final checkpoint. We’ll explore why the system generating code shouldn’t also verify it, how to turn tribal standards into enforceable, auditable controls, and where independent review belongs between spec and deploy. Key takeaways: Why end-stage review fails in an agent-driven SDLC. How to enforce and trace standards across teams, repos and AI tools. How to decide what can merge automatically, what needs human review and how to document that decision for auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Qodo, an AWS Partner.

title: Who's Your Security MVP? Here's How AI Ranks Them (sponsored by Trellix)
description: Yeah, yeah, AI SOC, we get it. But what really goes into getting wins out of AI in security vs saving a couple of clicks? This talk will show the importance of small (dumb) LLM's and how they create opportunities for secops by allowing you to use more tokens, anywhere you want. It will demo how you can go beyond enriching a few alerts to stack rank your most valuable security tools in an ROI thunderdome. You'll learn the AI confidence guardrail framework you need so you to actually start taking actions on your behalf without accidentally deleting all your VM's when you asked it to "eliminate all vulnerabilities." Seeing is believing, so there will be real-world demos of where AI works, where it doesn't, and why--bring your 3D glasses. This presentation is brought to you by Trellix, an AWS Partner.

title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and Ontology Patterns on AWS
description: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.

title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB)
description: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
description: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

title: Wrong, Not Broken, & Why your Observability should know the difference
description: Agentic applications need different access patterns and tooling than traditional apps. Teams often stitch together several tools and act as the human orchestrator just to answer a basic question: is my agent doing what the business needs? That gets harder when the agent runs on one cloud and calls models or APIs on another. In this session, we show how CloudWatch Omni brings AI agents and applications across clouds into one view, accelerating root cause whether its due to performance, availability or response quality.

title: You cannot write the eval for a failure you have not seen yet (sponsored by Arize AI)
description: LLM-as-a-judge works beautifully when you already know what you're looking for. You write the rubric, validate it against human labels, and it catches the failure you designed it to catch. But agents in production don't fail the way you anticipated. They fail as they meet new tools, new users, and environments that shifted underneath them, and every new failure arrives after the rubric was written. This talk argues the evaluation layer itself must become agentic. Instead of specifying a metric, you describe the behavior you want, and a judge with tool access inspects the trace, finds the spans that matter, classifies what went wrong, and generates labels you can monitor against. We'll cover why this became viable only recently, where it fails, and how to keep an agentic judge honest against human labels, so you know when to reach for one and how to validate it. This presentation is brought to you by Arize AI, an AWS Partner.

title: Your Agent Has an Upstream Dependency You Can't See (sponsored by Brave)
description: Verify, don't trust: a reproducible needle test that surfaces undeclared upstream calls in any stack. This presentation is brought to you by Brave, an AWS Partner.

title: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps (sponsored by ManageEngine)
description: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment. This presentation is brought to you by ManageEngine, an AWS Partner.

title: Your next Quantum developer might be an AI agent
description: AI is changing who can build quantum applications. See how AI assistants including Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Jupyter AI, and Classiq help developers move from natural-language prompts to optimized quantum workloads on Amazon Braket. Learn how AI generates code, synthesizes hardware-aware circuits, benchmarks on simulators and QPUs, and integrates with HPC resources. Through real examples, you'll see how AI-native workflows reduce complexity, accelerate experimentation, and make quantum development accessible to more builders.

title: Your playbook for modernizing 988K lines of .NET in 2 days
description: Transaction Network Services (TNS) needed to modernize their Altitude payments platform that included 274 projects, 988K lines of code, and 20 years of legacy .NET Framework to .NET 10. Their estimate: six months. The result: two days, 26 modules migrated, and 34 security vulnerabilities resolved. In this session, you'll learn what made it possible - from upgrading shared libraries first, running deterministic tools before AI, using human-verified tests, to keeping engineers on the keyboard after the tools stop running. Walk away with a practical, repeatable playbook for accelerating large-scale .NET modernization.

title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
description: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
description: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.

title: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
description: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier; devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.

title: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
description: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.
